But on a serious note, I believe 30% is a reasonable starting point to consider when negotiating an advance payment, but it is NOT a universal rule for every project.

The suitable percentage depends on the contract terms, the cost of mobilisation, the materials required, the project duration, the payment structure and the risks involved.

Let’s use this same project as an example.

For a 1.5 billion project:

10% advance = 150 million
20% advance = 300 million
30% advance = 450 million

The 200 million offered is approximately 13.3% of the project value.

Now, is that too small? It depends on what the contractor needs to spend before receiving the next payment.

For a project that requires expensive machinery, imported equipment, bulk material purchases and significant mobilisation costs, 200 million might not be enough.

However, if the contractor doesn’t need much money upfront and the client has a reliable payment structure based on milestones, a lower advance could work perfectly well.

For example, imagine a contractor needs 350 million to purchase equipment and materials before work can progress. An advance of 200 million would leave a funding gap of 150 million. That gap must be covered somehow, either through the contractor’s own funds, agreed supplier credit or another financing arrangement.

That is why contractors should not negotiate advance payments based on percentages alone. They should calculate the actual cash required to get the project moving.

My advice to contractors: Before accepting a major project, prepare a cash-flow forecast, estimate your mobilisation costs, identify your initial material requirements and understand when subsequent payments will arrive. Then negotiate an advance that matches the project’s actual funding needs.

My advice to clients: Don’t choose an advance percentage arbitrarily. Ask the contractor to justify the amount with a cost breakdown, and agree on appropriate safeguards, documentation and recovery terms.

Remember, 30% is a negotiation benchmark some contractors may consider, not a mandatory industry standard or a percentage that automatically suits every contract. The right figure is the one that supports project execution while keeping both parties financially protected.

Now, let me ask my fellow construction professionals:

For a 1.5 billion rice mill project, would you accept 200 million upfront, negotiate for 30%, or calculate the advance based on actual mobilisation costs?

Let’s hear your reasons.

text:
Other Princes Searched for Rare Delicacies. He Won the Throne with Rice.

Vietnamese legend tells of a king who asked his sons to prepare offerings for their ancestors. The one whose offering pleased him would inherit the throne.

The other princes searched the mountains and seas for precious foods.

Lang Liêu, the poorest among them, turned to familiar ingredients: sticky rice, mung beans and pork.

He prepared two kinds of rice cakes.

One was square, wrapped in leaves, with a filling of mung beans and pork. It represented the earth.

The other was round, made from pounded sticky rice. It represented the sky.

The king chose Lang Liêu as his successor.

The square cake was bánh chưng. Its round companion was bánh giầy.

This is a legend associated with the sixth Hùng King, not a documented account of how the foods were invented. But the tradition it explains remains alive.

During Tết, Vietnam’s Lunar New Year, families still prepare bánh chưng and offer it to their ancestors. Leaves are folded, rice and fillings packed inside, and the cakes boiled for hours.

A royal succession story survives in something people can unwrap, share and eat.

For those who grew up with bánh chưng, what comes back first: its taste, or the people who made it with you?

text:
$DASH — Dash ⚡

Bitcoin proved that digital money could exist.

Dash tried to make it practical for everyday payments.

Instant settlement.
Low transaction fees.
Optional privacy.
Decentralized governance.

More than a decade later, DASH is still operating.

But the token trades roughly 97% below its historical peak.

Here's the question.

Is Dash a forgotten payment network with genuine utility, or has the market moved on to stablecoins and newer blockchains?
⠀
01 | WHAT IS DASH?

Dash is a cryptocurrency launched in 2014, originally designed for fast, inexpensive digital payments.

Its infrastructure includes:

• InstantSend — Fast payment confirmation
• ChainLocks — Protection against chain reorganizations
• CoinJoin — Optional transaction privacy
• Masternodes — Network services and governance
• Dash Platform — Application and data infrastructure
• DASH — Native payment and network asset

Unlike many newer tokens, DASH isn't primarily a governance claim on a DeFi application.

It is the currency powering its own blockchain.

That creates direct utility.

But utility alone doesn't guarantee growing demand.
⠀
02 | WHERE DOES DEMAND COME FROM?

Three major sources:

• Payments and transfers
• Masternode collateral
• Network services and ecosystem activity

DASH is required for transactions.

Traditional masternodes require 1,000 DASH in collateral, while Evolution masternodes require more.

That creates a meaningful reason to hold tokens.

But there's a limitation.

A payment token can circulate quickly without investors needing to hold it for long periods.

High transaction activity doesn't automatically mean sustained buying pressure.

Velocity matters.
⠀
03 | THE BIG NARRATIVE 🔥

Three potential catalysts:

• Renewed demand for payment cryptocurrencies
• Expansion of Dash Evolution
• Growing interest in financial privacy

Bitcoin increasingly serves as a store-of-value asset.

Stablecoins dominate dollar-denominated crypto payments.

Dash occupies a different position.

A decentralized payment network with optional privacy and built-in governance.

The opportunity?

Demand returns for cryptocurrencies designed to function as money.

The risk?

Users prefer stablecoins because they don't want payment volatility.

Dash must compete on actual usefulness, not nostalgia.
⠀
04 | THE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE

Dash has several established strengths.

• More than a decade of operation
• Fast transaction confirmation
• Low network fees
• Masternode infrastructure
• Decentralized treasury funding
• Optional privacy functionality

Its governance model is particularly distinctive.

Part of newly issued DASH funds community-approved development and ecosystem proposals.

But competition is intense.

$LTC offers established payment infrastructure.

$XMR has stronger privacy-focused positioning.

Stablecoins offer predictable dollar value.

Dash needs to demonstrate why users should choose DASH over these alternatives.
⠀
05 | THE NUMBERS 📊

October 28, 2026 market snapshot:

• Price: ~$55
• Market cap: ~$708M
• Maximum-supply FDV: ~$1.04B
• Circulating supply: ~12.88M DASH
• Maximum potential supply: ~18.92M DASH
• Circulating percentage: ~68%
• 24H trading volume: ~$116M
• Historical ATH: ~$1,642
• Decline from ATH: ~96.7%

Recent DeFiLlama chain tracking also showed:

• Daily active addresses: ~34K
• Daily transactions: ~11K
• Daily chain fees: ~$23
• Tracked DeFi TVL: ~$96K

These metrics require context.

Dash is primarily a payments network, not a DeFi-first blockchain.

Low DeFi TVL doesn't mean the payment network has no users.

But the economic challenge is obvious.

Network fee generation remains extremely small relative to market capitalization.
⠀
06 | THE TOKENOMICS TRAP

Dash has no conventional venture-capital token allocation waiting to unlock.

Its supply is created through block rewards.

Current block-subsidy allocation:

• 20% — Miners
• 60% — Masternode rewards
• 20% — Decentralized governance budget

The maximum eventual supply is approximately 18.92M DASH, depending on treasury allocations.

But here's the trap.

A limited supply doesn't mean zero inflation.

New DASH continues entering circulation.

And masternode rewards aren't automatically profits generated by paying customers.

Much of the reward system is funded through newly issued coins.

A scarcity narrative needs real demand behind it.
⠀
07 | THE NEXT BIG UNLOCK

Dash doesn't have a conventional monthly insider unlock calendar.

There is no major VC vesting cliff comparable to newer altcoins.

Instead, supply expands through ongoing block rewards.

Dash reduces its block subsidy by approximately 7.14% every 210,240 blocks, roughly once a year.

This gradually slows issuance.

But future supply still matters.

And masternode collateral isn't permanently removed from circulation.

Operators can eventually release and sell their holdings.

The key risk is continuous issuance and changing holder demand.

Not a single scheduled insider unlock.
⠀
08 | THE VALUE CAPTURE PROBLEM 👀

This is the central investment debate.

Dash has a direct economic relationship between network usage and DASH.

Users pay transaction fees in the native asset.

Masternodes lock DASH as collateral.

But consider the distinction:

• Payment volume — Value transferred
• Transaction fees — Paid by network users
• Block rewards — Newly issued DASH
• Masternode rewards — Compensation for network services
• Holder earnings — Not automatic dividends

The network's low fees are excellent for payments.

But they generate limited direct economic revenue.

Masternode yields also need to be evaluated against token inflation and price risk.

A high nominal reward doesn't necessarily create real investment returns.

Dash needs stronger organic payment demand to support its long-term valuation.
⠀
09 | FINAL VERDICT 🎯

Dash has genuine strengths.

Established infrastructure.

Fast payments.

A limited supply.

Decentralized governance.

And a long operating history.

But it faces a difficult competitive reality.

Stablecoins dominate many practical crypto-payment use cases.

And privacy-focused cryptocurrencies compete for users seeking financial confidentiality.

The bullish case?

Dash Evolution expands functionality, payment adoption strengthens, and reduced issuance supports a healthier supply-demand balance.

The bearish case?

The network remains technically functional but fails to attract enough new users and capital.

Meanwhile, competing payment systems continue gaining market share.

🔥 DASH doesn't need to prove that it can survive.

It has already survived multiple market cycles.

It needs to prove that people still want to use it.

Survival is impressive.

Adoption is what determines the next chapter.

Save this before the next payment-coin rotation.

$DASH  vs $LTC vs $XMR — which has the strongest long-term use case?

Is DASH an overlooked survivor, or is its discount justified by changing market demand?

Drop your pick below. 👇

text:
The History of the Music Man StingRay Guitar, 1976-2026

Music Man emerged in the early 1970s through Tom Walker and Forrest White, both associated with Fender. Leo Fender joined the company in 1975, helping develop a new generation of electric instruments. Introduced in 1976, the StingRay guitar represented one of his most ambitious departures from traditional Fender designs.

1976-1982 - StingRay I and II

The original StingRay featured a solid ash body, bolt-on maple neck, 25.5” scale, two humbucking pickups and active electronics. Unlike conventional passive guitar circuits, its battery-powered preamplifier provided bass and treble equalization, expanding the instrument’s frequency-shaping capabilities.

The StingRay I featured a 12” fingerboard radius and 22 jumbo frets. The StingRay II offered a 7.5” radius and 22 standard frets. Both employed four-position pickup switching and a separate bright switch.

The pickups used Alnico magnets and conventional electromagnetic coils feeding the active preamplifier. This distinction is important: the original StingRay was an active-electronics guitar, not simply a guitar fitted with unusually powerful pickups.

Despite its advanced circuitry, the StingRay struggled commercially. Leo Fender departed Music Man in 1980, and guitar production ended around 1982.

1984-2015 - The Ernie Ball Era

Ernie Ball acquired Music Man in 1984. While the StingRay bass became a cornerstone of the company, the guitar remained discontinued for more than three decades.

2016 - StingRay Returns

Ernie Ball Music Man revived the StingRay with a redesigned African mahogany body, five-bolt maple neck, 25.5” scale, 22 stainless steel frets, dual passive humbuckers, five-way switching and modern tremolo.

Unlike the original, the revived StingRay emphasized passive electronics and contemporary construction rather than active equalization.

2018 - StingRay RS

The RS introduced roasted maple neck construction, revised appointments and expanded finishes. Its passive humbuckers, stainless steel frets and modern tremolo continued the 2016 design philosophy. Body woods varied across production.

2022 - StingRay HT

The HT introduced a heat-treated bridge humbucker, ceramic-magnet neck humbucker and onboard boost circuit. Its active electronics offered up to 20 dB of adjustable boost, while the guitar incorporated an alder body, roasted maple neck and Tune-o-matic-style bridge.

Legacy

The StingRay’s evolution illustrates two distinct approaches to electric guitar engineering: Leo Fender’s pioneering active equalization in 1976 and Ernie Ball Music Man’s modern combination of passive pickups, specialized magnets and selective active circuitry.

The original StingRay remains an important, relatively uncommon chapter in Leo Fender’s career, while its modern descendants preserve the name through substantially redesigned instruments.

EAAA INDIA ALTERNATIVES IPO: LAST DAY TODAY (28 Oct)

📌 THE OFFER

Price band: ₹1,585–1,665
Issue size: ₹1,200 crore
Fresh issue: ₹0
OFS: ₹1,200 crore (100%)
Lot size: 9 shares
Minimum investment: ₹14,985 at ₹1,665
Retail quota: at least 35% (QIBs up to 50%, NIIs at least 15%)

Dates:
Opened: 26 October
Closes: TODAY, 28 October (accept the UPI mandate by 5 PM)
Expected allotment: 29 October
Tentative listing: 2 November on BSE and NSE
Registrar: MUFG Intime India

🏦 WHAT DOES EAAA DO?

It is the alternative investment arm of the Edelweiss group. It was earlier called Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors.

It manages ₹95,345 crore of client money in two main businesses:

Real Assets: infrastructure and commercial real estate through 10 funds, including 2 InvITs
Private Credit: lending to companies outside the banking system (performing credit, special situations, real estate credit) through 16 funds
Fees are earned on ₹48,623 crore of fee-paying AUM, about half the total.

It has 11,009 client relationships. 49% of AUM comes from institutions and 34% from foreign clients. Offices: Mumbai, Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore.

📊 FY26 PERFORMANCE

Total income: ₹964 crore, up 22.5%
Management fees: ₹579 crore, up 20.8%
Performance fees: ₹290 crore, up 52.3%
PAT: ₹265 crore, up only 15.4%
PAT margin: 27.5%, down from 30.0% in FY24
Q1 FY27: total income ₹336 crore (up 58.8%) and PAT ₹81 crore (up 45%). That PAT includes ₹54 crore of mark-to-market gains on its own fund investments.

✅ WHAT WORKS IN ITS FAVOUR

India's first listed pure-play alternatives manager, in a fast-growing sector

Sticky clients: 77% of AUM comes from repeat clients
Fee-paying AUM grew 21% a year, from ₹30,398 crore in FY24 to ₹44,710 crore in FY26

Real Assets fee-paying AUM grew 46% in one year
ROE of about 26%

Low debt: borrowings of ₹399 crore, or ₹0.34 for every ₹1 of net worth

Mutual funds took 65% of the anchor book

⚠️ WHAT HOLDS ME BACK

100% OFS. The full ₹1,200 crore goes to Edelweiss Securities and the company gets nothing.

The promoter's average cost is ₹54.45 per share, so it is exiting at about 30 times its cost. Group companies bought shares at ₹925 in Sept 2025, and the IPO price is 1.8 times that just 13 months later.

Much of the profit is still on paper. Performance fees are booked as unrealised gains. After the linked employee bonuses, they came to ₹129 crore, about half of FY26 PBT. Of the ₹685 crore booked since FY24, ₹287 crore has not been received in cash.

Cash lags profit. From FY24 to Q1 FY27, PAT was ₹751 crore but operating cash flow was only ₹232 crore. 

Operating cash flow was negative in FY24 and FY25.
High costs: the cost-to-income ratio is 64%, against 20–38% for listed AMCs.

SEBI history:

SEBI returned the first DRHP in March 2025 over "reclassification between revenue lines"

After an inspection, SEBI issued administrative warnings in July 2026 for not following investment processes and investor disclosure rules

A settlement application is pending

Leadership churn: the MD & CEO quit in Sept 2025, the head of real estate credit in April 2026 and a co-CEO in June 2026.

The current CEO was paid ₹39.75 crore in FY26, about 15% of PAT.

A ₹206 crore pre-IPO dividend (₹32 per share) went almost entirely to the promoter.

Edelweiss group baggage: RBI orders against ECL Finance and Edelweiss ARC in 2024 (since lifted), a police FIR that names the company, and a ₹34 crore tax demand.

💰 VALUATION

At ₹1,665, the market cap is about ₹10,765 crore. That is 40.4× FY26 EPS of ₹41.26, against 39.89× for the RHP's peer group. Price to book is 9.4×.

360 ONE trades at 35.7× and Nuvama at 31×. AMCs trade at 28–46×, but they run PAT margins above 50%.

Remove the performance fees that are still on paper and you are paying about 66× core earnings.

My fair value range: ₹1,210–1,610 (30–40× FY26 diluted EPS). My base case is ₹1,413 (35×), about 15% below the IPO price. There is no margin of safety.

🏛️ ANCHOR BOOK

₹360 crore was allocated across 26 anchor allocations at ₹1,665, the top of the band. That is 30% of the issue.

SBI Midcap Fund: ₹38 crore
ICICI Pru Smallcap Fund: ₹38 crore
HDFC MF: ₹38 crore across 2 schemes
Nippon India MF: ₹38 crore across 2 schemes
Kotak MF: ₹20.5 crore across 2 schemes
Carnelian Bharat Amritkaal Fund: ₹20.5 crore
Schroders: ₹18.4 crore across 2 funds
Norway's Government Pension Fund Global: ₹10 crore
Mutual funds took 65.42% of the book, across 10 AMCs and 13 schemes. No insurer or pension fund bid. 

Goldman Sachs and BNP came in through ODIs, ₹5 crore each.

Nuvama is a lead manager, and its EDGE fund took ₹5 crore. 360 ONE, a listed competitor, took ₹11 crore.

Lock-in: 50% for 30 days (about 28 Nov) and 50% for 90 days.

📊 SUBSCRIPTION (Day 3)
QIB: 1.01×
NII: 1.30×
Retail: 0.17× 🚨
Total: 0.65×

The issue is still not fully covered on the last day. Retail has bid for less than a fifth of its quota.

📈 GMP

GMP was ₹10 (0.6%) as of 27 Oct, 4 PM, pointing to a listing near ₹1,675. It peaked at ₹121 (7.27%) on 23 Oct, so it fell more than 90% in four days.

📝 MY VIEW

I am not applying. Weak demand on the last day and an almost flat GMP confirm my view: the valuation leaves no room for upside, either at listing or over the long term.

Not SEBI registered. Educational purposes only. Do your own research. GMP is unofficial and listing gains are not assured.

Greatmartyr Paraskevi of Iconium
Commemorated on October 28
The Great Martyr Paraskevi (Paraskevḗ) of Iconium, lived during the third century in a rich and pious family. The parents of the saint especially reverenced Friday, the day of the Passion of the Lord, and therefore they called their daughter Paraskevi. This name, Paraskevi, also means Friday.

Young Paraskevi with all her heart loved purity and the loftiness of the virginal life, and she took a vow of celibacy. She wanted to devote all her life to God and to enlighten pagans with the light of Christ.

Because of her confession of the Orthodox Faith, the pagans in a frenzy seized her and brought her to the city prefect. They demanded that she offer unholy sacrifice to the pagan idols. With a steady heart, and trusting on God, the saint refused this demand. For this she underwent great torments: after stripping her, they tied her to a tree and beat her with rods. Then the torturers raked her pure body with iron claws. Finally, they threw her into prison, exhausted by the torture and lacerated to the bone. But God did not forsake the holy sufferer, and miraculously healed her wounds. Not heeding this divine miracle, the executioners continued with their torture of Saint Paraskevi, and finally, they cut off her head.

Saint Paraskevi has always enjoyed a special love and veneration among the Orthodox people. Many pious customs and observances are associated with her. In the ancient Russian accounts of the Saints’ Lives, the name of the Great Martyr is inscribed as: “Saint Paraskevi, also called Piatnitsa (in Russian: Friday).” Churches dedicated to Saint Paraskevi in antiquity were given the name Piatnitsa. Small wayside chapels in Rus received the name Piatnitsa. The simple Russian people called the Martyr Paraskevi variously Piatnitsa, Piatina, Petka.

Icons of Saint Paraskevi were especially venerated and embellished by the faithful. Russian iconographers usually depicted the martyr as an austere ascetic, tall of stature, with a radiant crown upon her head. Icons of the saint guard pious and happy households. By Church belief, Saint Paraskevi is protectress of fields and cattle. Therefore, on her Feastday it was the custom to bring fruit to church to be blessed. These blessed objects were kept until the following year. Moreover, Saint Paraskevi is invoked for protection of cattle from disease. She is also a healer of people from grievous illness of both body and soul.

$LH Q3 2026 earnings: Labcorp raises its outlook as clinical-trial orders grow again

Labcorp, the medical testing and drug-trial laboratory group, accelerated its underlying sales growth and restarted its clinical-trial order book. Revenue rose 7%, while profit per share excluding one-offs climbed 15% on cost savings and earlier share buybacks. Chief executive Adam Schechter raised the full-year sales and profit outlook for a third straight quarter, leaving fourth-quarter revenue on track to grow about 7% by our math.

• Sales from businesses owned a year ago: +𝟓.𝟓% (from a year ago (total revenue $3.81B, +6.9%))
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟒.𝟕𝟖 (+14.5% from a year ago (reported EPS $3.22, +3.3%))
• Biopharma contracted backlog: $𝟖.𝟗𝟐𝐁 (+3.9% from a year ago (trailing book-to-bill 1.10))
• Full-year outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 (middle of the range: 6.3% sales growth and $18.50 EPS)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the three main worries from the first half all improved at once. Biopharma backlog broke out of a four-quarter stall as trailing orders reached 1.10 times sales, specialty testing lifted Diagnostics prices and mix back above 3%, and a 47% jump in free cash flow removed the pressure on fourth-quarter cash generation. One caution: reported operating margin slipped as restructuring, deal integration, and system expenses climbed.

The question now is how much of Labcorp's profit expansion reaches the bottom line as it absorbs three more acquisitions signed after quarter-end. Supporters see a repeatable formula of buying lab volume and cutting operating costs, while skeptics point to $168 million of quarterly one-off charges that kept reported net income nearly unchanged. Fourth-quarter restructuring charges and the 2027 outlook will show whether those deal costs start to come down.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐁𝐢𝐨𝐩𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐦𝐚 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐤𝐞 𝐎𝐮𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐭𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐥
Biopharma Laboratory Services, the division that runs clinical trials and drug testing for pharmaceutical companies, had a flat order book around $8.7 billion for four straight quarters. That plateau ended this quarter, and the company raised the division's full-year sales outlook by nearly two percentage points.

• Contracted backlog: $8.92 billion, up 3.9% from a year ago and up $190 million from last quarter
• Trailing twelve-month book-to-bill (orders won divided by sales): 1.10, up from 1.03 last quarter
• Trailing twelve-month net orders: $3.59 billion, up from $3.32 billion in Q2
• Backlog expected to turn into revenue over the next 12 months: $2.82 billion, up from $2.75 billion

The jump in trailing orders indicates roughly $980 million of new business in the third quarter by our math, because a weak year-ago quarter dropped out of the twelve-month window. Combined with an 8.5% revenue increase this quarter and the higher full-year plan, both the quarter and the outlook confirm that drug-development demand is growing again.

What to watch: fourth-quarter backlog and book-to-bill when full-year results arrive in February. Holding the trailing ratio near 1.10 against a tougher fourth-quarter comparison would support high-single-digit biopharma growth in 2027.

🟢🟢 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐲 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐋𝐚𝐛 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬
Diagnostics Laboratories, Labcorp's main network of patient testing centers, relies on complex specialty tests to raise the average revenue collected per patient order. Chief executive Adam Schechter said the group widened its lead in specialty testing by launching new assays for advanced melanoma, Alzheimer's disease, and hepatitis D.

Underlying prices and product mix in Diagnostics rose 3.1% from a year ago, rebounding from 1.8% in both the first and second quarters. Combined with a 1.3% rise in underlying test volume, sales from businesses owned a year ago grew 4.4% even against last year's 6.3% comparison, and the company raised its full-year Diagnostics sales plan.

What to watch: fourth-quarter underlying prices and mix in Diagnostics. A reading near 3% when volume comparisons ease in the fourth quarter would push underlying division growth back toward 5%.

🟢 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚 𝐒𝐢𝐱𝐭𝐡 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫
"Labcorp delivered another strong quarter with 7% revenue growth, continued margin expansion and 14.5% adjusted EPS growth, leading to a raise in our full-year guidance," Schechter said. Operating margin excluding one-offs rose 0.6 percentage points from a year ago to 15.0%, marking a sixth consecutive quarter of improvement as the company upgraded its Global Trial Connect portal.

By our math, the cost of performing tests fell 0.3 percentage points of revenue to 70.9%, and overhead and selling expenses excluding one-offs fell 0.2 points to 14.1%. Biopharma margin rose 1.8 points to 18.3% on "organic growth and operating efficiencies from the strategic actions taken in Early Development", its early-stage drug testing unit that grew 0.4% after shrinking in Q2.

What to watch: Early Development revenue growth in the fourth quarter, when it compares against a 13.5% drop a year ago. A return to mid-single-digit growth would show the site closures are complete and sustain Biopharma margins above 17%.

🟢 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐄𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐇𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐥𝐞
Entering the quarter, Labcorp's unchanged full-year free cash flow plan of $1.24 billion to $1.36 billion looked stretched because first-half cash flow was down 12% from a year earlier. In the third quarter, free cash flow rose 47% from a year ago to $412.2 million as the company managed accounts payable and inventory more tightly.

Nine-month free cash flow reached $796.6 million, up 11.3% from a year ago despite $93.6 million more in capital spending. By our math, the middle of the full-year outlook now leaves $503.4 million for the fourth quarter, just 2.7% above last year's fourth quarter, fading the risk of a cash shortfall.

What to watch: fourth-quarter operating cash flow and capital spending. Collecting recent receivables will determine whether full-year free cash flow finishes near the $1.30 billion middle of the range.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧
Labcorp uses hospital and regional lab acquisitions to add testing volume, and supporters view its steady deal pipeline as a reliable growth engine. Schechter highlighted "expanding access through strategic acquisitions across our Diagnostics and Biopharma Laboratory Services businesses", noting four deals that should be "accretive to adjusted EPS in year one and return cost of capital by year three".

• Reported operating margin: 10.6%, down 0.6 percentage points from 11.1% a year ago
• Operating profit adjustments: $167.9 million, up 44% from $116.7 million a year ago
• LaunchPad system and consulting charges: $28.6 million, more than double last year's $13.7 million
• Acquisition, disposition, and restructuring charges: $38.9 million, up from $16.7 million a year ago
• Loss from minority stake in European lab group SYNLAB: $10.9 million, more than double last year's $5.0 million

While management emphasized expanding margins excluding one-offs, total selling and administrative expenses on the income statement rose 0.5 percentage points of revenue, and intangible amortization rose 13% to $78.7 million. Because Labcorp spent $683.4 million on acquisitions over nine months and just signed agreements for BioReference assets, Myriad Genetics' prenatal business, and Millennium Health, these integration and amortization costs are recurring expenses that kept reported net profit nearly unchanged at $262.8 million.

What to watch: acquisition and LaunchPad charges in the fourth-quarter reconciliation table. If quarterly operating adjustments stay near $170 million as the three new deals close, reported profit will keep trailing the company's headline earnings.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Labcorp's third-quarter earnings release announced new tests—including FDA approval for its PGDx elio tissue complete "companion diagnostic to help identify patients with advanced melanoma", the Marker genetic panel on Labcorp OnDemand, and an at-home HPV screening partnership with Waters Corporation—but gave no numbers on five standing concerns.

• Medicare 2027 rate cuts (PAMA): no update in the release on the planned $100 million revenue and profit hit or the September Analyst Day mitigation plan.
• Medicaid and ACA coverage losses: no third-quarter figure for the 0.2 to 0.3 percentage point volume drag discussed last quarter; the earnings call and 10-Q filing will be the first places to check.
• Specialty and consumer revenue size: OnDemand now offers over 140 tests, but management still did not disclose revenue for specialty, neurology, or consumer testing.
• Ravgen patent appeal: no update in the release on the appeal of the $372 million patent verdict; the 10-Q legal footnote will show its status.
• At-home self-collection impact: no data on whether at-home tests are pulling routine visits away from Labcorp's physical patient service centers.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐,𝟒𝟏𝟑 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Accounts receivable—money owed by patients, insurers, and drug companies for completed lab work—rose $70.5 million in the third quarter and is up 14.7% since December 2025. That is more than double the 6.2% nine-month revenue growth rate, absorbing $317.3 million of operating cash flow so far this year.

𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟓𝟏.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Spending on property and lab equipment jumped 42.1% from a year ago to reach 4.0% of revenue, up from 3.5% in the first half. The diagnostic group is building a 500,000-square-foot central laboratory facility in Indiana, which lifted nine-month capital spending by 30.1% to $404.2 million.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟖𝟏.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Weighted-average diluted shares fell 2.5% from a year ago and 0.5% from the second quarter, boosting per-share profit growth by about 2.5 percentage points. After spending $451.8 million on share buybacks in the first half, the company bought back no stock in the third quarter and kept $1.4 billion of authorization.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐄𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟏𝟒,𝟕𝟕𝟗–𝟏𝟒,𝟖𝟖𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟓.𝟗–𝟔.𝟕% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡)  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from $14,710–14,827 million (5.4–6.3% growth)
Raised. The middle of the full-year sales range moved up $64.5 million to $14,833 million, or 6.3% growth. By our math, that leaves $3,754 million for the fourth quarter, or 6.8% growth from a year ago against Q3's 6.9%. This is the third raise this year, and each step has grown larger: +20, +30, and +45 basis points.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐃𝐢𝐚𝐠𝐧𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐬 𝐋𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟏𝟏,𝟒𝟕𝟓–𝟏𝟏,𝟓𝟓𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟓.𝟓–𝟔.𝟐% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡)  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from $11,450–11,532 million (5.3–6.0% growth)
Raised. Labcorp lifted the middle of the Diagnostics target by $22 million to $11,513 million, or 5.9% growth for the year. By our math, that points to $2,901 million in the fourth quarter, up 6.3% from a year ago as the division laps an easier 1.1% underlying volume quarter from late 2025.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐁𝐢𝐨𝐩𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐦𝐚 𝐋𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟑,𝟑𝟐𝟖–𝟑,𝟑𝟓𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟕.𝟒–𝟖.𝟒% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡)  ⇒ stable
🠅 raised from $3,269–3,300 million (5.5–6.5% growth)
Raised. The clinical-trial unit's target rose $58.5 million at the middle of the range to $3,343 million, or 7.9% growth, despite currency help trimming from 1.5% to 1.3%. By our math, the outlook implies $860 million of fourth-quarter revenue, or 8.4% growth, matching Q3's 8.5% pace as Early Development laps a 13.5% drop.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐏𝐒: $𝟏𝟖.𝟑𝟎–𝟏𝟖.𝟕𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $18.10–18.55
Raised. Profit per share excluding one-offs moved up $0.18 at the middle of the range to $18.50, or 12.5% growth for the year. By our math, that leaves $4.48 for the fourth quarter, up 10.1% from a year ago versus 14.5% in Q3. It is the third raise of 2026: +$0.13, +$0.30, and +$0.18.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰: $𝟏,𝟐𝟒𝟎–𝟏,𝟑𝟔𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $1,240–1,360 million
Unchanged. The full-year cash plan stays at $1.30 billion in the middle of the range, or 7.8% growth over 2025. After generating $796.6 million in the first nine months, the company needs $503.4 million in the fourth quarter by our math, a 2.7% increase over last year's fourth quarter.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐰𝐥𝐲 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐜𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭?
Labcorp announced agreements to buy clinical testing assets from BioReference Health, Myriad Genetics' prenatal business, and Millennium Health, while pausing share buybacks in Q3. Disclosing the purchase prices and expected revenue will show how much cash they require and how much growth they add in 2027.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐘𝐍𝐋𝐀𝐁 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐣𝐮𝐦𝐩?
Operating adjustments excluded from headline profit rose 44% to $167.9 million, led by $28.6 million in LaunchPad system costs, while losses on the minority stake in SYNLAB more than doubled to $10.9 million. Investors need to know when these charges will peak.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐢𝐟 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐥𝐚𝐛 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬?
Management previously sized the potential January 2027 Medicare rate reduction (PAMA) at $100 million of revenue and profit, and pointed to its September Analyst Day for details. With the third-quarter release silent on the topic, what offsets are now in place?

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐰𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐚𝐬 𝐟𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐬 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬?
Accounts receivable have climbed 14.7% since the end of 2025 to $2.41 billion, compared with 6.2% nine-month revenue growth. Is the build coming from newly acquired hospital outreach labs, or are insurers and patients taking longer to pay?

text:
In a town of eight hundred people in Iowa, I woke up at six in the morning and saw twelve pickup trucks idling outside the gas station.

Nobody was pumping gas.

I thought there had been a town emergency. I walked inside to offer my assistance.

There was no emergency. There was only a rotating glass carousel inside a Casey's General Store, and inside that carousel was something the Midwest calls Breakfast Pizza.

It is pizza dough covered in warm cheese sauce, scrambled eggs, bacon, and melted cheddar, baked at dawn by a woman named Barb who knows every farmer in the county by the sound of his diesel engine.

A man in Carhartt overalls saw me hesitating. He opened the glass door with tongs, slid a massive triangle onto a paper plate, and handed it to me before taking his own.

"First time?" he asked.

I nodded, mouth full.

"You're ruined now," he said gently, pouring black coffee into a foam cup.

He was right. I now judge every bakery in the world against a gas station in a cornfield.

text:
Rocky Marciano and film funnyman Jerry Lewis, on October 28, 1955, thirty-eight days after what would be the Heavyweight Champion's last title defense and final career bout, against Archie Moore, on September 21st.

On April 27, 1956, Marciano and his manager, Al Weill, announced his retirement at a press conference at New York City's Hotel Shelton. 
---------------------------------------------------------
From  Sports Illustrated Classic in 2020:

Rocky Marciano holds one of the greatest records in boxing after ending his career early as an undefeated world heavyweight boxing champion at the age of 31. 
On April 27, 1956, Marciano and his manager, Al Weill, announced his retirement at a press conference at New York City's Hotel Shelton. Marciano, who went 49–0 with 43 KOs, said he wanted to retire to spend more time with his family. The sports world was stunned. Many boxers had retired only to later make comebacks, and people immediately wondered if Marciano would change his mind and eventually return to the ring. However, his mind was made up.
"I thought it was a mistake when Joe Louis tried a comeback. No man can say what he will do in the future. But, barring poverty, the ring has seen the last of me," Marciano said, per The New York Times. "I am comfortably fixed, and I am not afraid of the future. Barring a complete and dire emergency, you will never see Rocky Marciano make a comeback."
Boxing had given Marciano a great life, as far as he was concerned. Born in Brockton, Mass., on September 1, 1923, Marciano grew up in a working-class family. He played baseball as a kid but took up boxing after he was drafted into the Army in 1943. Marciano continued his amateur boxing career after he left the military in 1946 and even tried out for a Chicago Cubs farm team. With his dreams of playing professional baseball dashed, Marciano became a pro boxer and defeated Lee Epperson in a third-round knockout on March 17, 1947.
Marciano was heavily criticized for his awkward boxing style and lack of footwork throughout his career. However, sportswriters respected his aggressiveness and the Italian-American community loved him. In October 1951, Marciano knocked out former heavyweight champion Joe Louis in eight rounds, joining the conversation as a potential contender. 
The "Brockton Blockbuster" was crowned champion when he knocked out Jersey Joe Walcott in Philadelphia on Sept. 23, 1952. The following year Marciano beat Walcott again in a first-round knockout in Chicago. Marciano defended his title five more times and defeated Archie Moore in September 1955 in what would become his final professional fight. 
Some people debate if Marciano's undefeated record is flawed and he won 49 bouts thanks to luck or mostly fighting guys that were past their prime. Despite the criticism, he retired as the only undefeated heavyweight champion in history. Thirteen years later, Marciano died in a plane crash in Iowa on Aug. 31, 1969.
On June 18th of 1957, Marciano announced publicly that he and Weill were ending their partnership "amicably." Weill had largely limited Marciano's public appearances, and as a result of his retirement a year earlier, wanted to focus on charitable work that Weill had so long forbid.
----------------------------------------------------------
From The Long Island Press in 2009 in reviewing Mike Stanton's Marciano biography ('Unbeaten: Rocky Marciano's quest for perfection in a crooked world'):

The young Marciano didn’t care for school. A soldier in World War II, he was court-martialed for theft. When it came to boxing, however, Marciano was all business. The sport has never seen such a dedicated pugilist. “[You’ve] got to make boxing a kind of religion,” he once told a reporter. “You believe in yourself and you believe in the things you got to do. You never forget them for a minute. Then you get there and you think of what you had to go through and you say to yourself, ‘It was worth it, it was worth everything.’” After winning the title, Marciano trained for a defense of the crown. The actress Jayne Mansfield, a poor man’s Marilyn Monroe, visited the camp. Rocky had no problem turning this siren away. In the weeks before a fight, Marciano literally sealed himself off from the outside world.
The story of Marciano’s rise in the boxing world never grows old. He turned professional when he was 25, well past the average age. But the man had a punch, “Suzy Q” that when delivered, had a habit of putting opponents on their backs—often for weeks at a time. Marciano remains the proprietor of the most famous blow in boxing history. Fighting for the title against Jersey Joe Walcott in 1952, the challenger went into the final round trailing on points to the wily veteran. Marciano shockingly decked Walcott with a right cross, winning the title and in the process, keeping the entire citizenry of Brockton from going broke on the bets they had made. (“If he loses, 50,000 Italians are going to commit suicide,” one of Rocky’s boyhood pals told the press.) The photo of that punch remains the most legendary in all of sports. Marciano connects, Walcott’s knees buckle, his face becomes terribly contorted: It hurts every time you look it at.
Marciano was a puncher who learned how to box from Charley Goldman, a veteran of the sports’ prohibition days. He was managed by Al Weill. The former got Rocky fights; he talked up his prize fighter, but he also pocketed 50 percent of the money. Indeed, this biography is different in that it details the grip that organized crime had on the sport throughout the ‘50s. Marciano was clean; when a mid-level mobster tried to make him throw a fight, Rocky brushed him off. Still, a slice of Weil’s take went to Frank Carbo, the prime minister of the boxing underworld. In all, about 10 percent of Rocky’s total earnings went to the mob. Carbo and his associates ran the fight game like a well-oiled corporation, similar to the way that Meyer Lansky and Lucky Luciano ran their rackets. All of the top fighters—Joe Louis, Walcott, Ezzard Charles and Sonny Liston—had their careers run by the syndicate.
In the early 1960s, the Feds finally caught up with Carbo. By then, Marciano had retired. As with Joe DiMaggio, Rocky left while still on top, owner of a perfect 49-0 record. Let us remember Marciano in his prime. Did he retire too early? Friends thought so, but the man was heavily influenced by his loving parents; his mother, Pasqualena, would spend fight nights in a church with a friend, reciting the rosary, meanwhile Pierino Marciano suffered at ringside while his son took blow after blow from the best the game had to offer. Marciano’s retirement years were restless. He never lacked for friends or companions. Constantly on the road, he succumbed to adultery. His weight ballooned. Marciano even began paling around with organized crime figures he had once professed to dislike. Burned by Weil’s greedy ways, Marciano was paranoid. He insisted on being paid in cash for lucrative personal appearances. The money then, would end up stashed away under beds, in closets, in unknown locations.
“Oh, you’re gonna drive me crazy,” Pasqualena Marciano once told her son, wishing that he would get off the road and spend time at home. “Good thing I have Sonny and Peter [her other sons].” She meant it jokingly, but Marciano’s mother knew her son was gone. Rocky couldn’t go back to Brockton, back to his wife and children. He set up his home base in Fort Lauderdale, FL, but he couldn’t stay there, either. Marciano, as William Butler Yeats once sang of another tragic figure, could never part gray hairs. In 1969, he met a tragic ending in a Iowa cornfield.

Washington and Moscow are talking about gas, assets, and technology again. Nord Stream is the piece that still draws the sharpest reaction.

Discussions cover Lukoil’s foreign assets, nuclear cooperation, Arctic LNG, a possible Nord Stream restart, and access to immobilised Russian funds. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov confirmed talks on Lukoil’s portfolio after the Witkoff-Putin meeting. The US extended the buyer licence deadline to 21 November. An earlier Carlyle bid collapsed; the assets remain on the market.⁠

One Nord Stream 2 line is reportedly still serviceable. Russian officials have called a restart “inevitable.” Reports describe a US operator buying the infrastructure, waiving sanctions on Gazprom, and selling the gas to European utilities as an intermediary. Germany has stated that putting Nord Stream 2 into operation is not on the agenda and certification remains suspended.⁠

The barrier is European. Even if Washington and Moscow agree on a structure, EU buyers and German regulators still have to accept the gas. Several capitals have already rejected restoring Russian pipeline volumes. A US intermediary does not override that veto.⁠

The package sits inside the same track. Lukoil sales, Arctic LNG technology, and partial release of frozen reserves appear as economic incentives. Some Arctic LNG talks later showed Russian funding links. None has produced a signed deal. All remain conditional on Ukraine progress that has not materialised.

Moscow is being offered commercial pathways before a durable ceasefire. European governments see energy leverage returning while fighting continues. US LNG exporters see a direct commercial threat if Nord Stream volumes re-enter Europe at scale. That is why the pipeline piece is treated as more sensitive than the Lukoil sales.

If volumes return under a US intermediary model, European buyers regain lower-cost pipeline gas. That undercuts the premium US and Norwegian LNG have held since 2022 and restores Russian leverage over German and Central European industry. Germany has rejected it publicly. Other EU capitals have signalled the same. The structure keeps the option alive and divides European positions further.

The wider package functions as an incentive track running parallel to the Ukraine talks. It signals Moscow can extract concessions before a ceasefire is locked in. That sequencing weakens sanctions deterrence and opens a pathway back into Western energy and technology markets while fighting continues. European governments see the risk as asymmetric: dependence returns faster than any security guarantees.⁠

For the United States the calculus is mixed. A Nord Stream restart would compete with US LNG exports to Europe. Involvement as an intermediary creates a commercial stake for US firms and a potential lever over both Moscow and European buyers. The Arctic LNG discussions carry optics risk from earlier Russian funding links.⁠

Ukraine’s position is the most exposed. Restored Russian gas flows reduce economic pressure on Moscow and strengthen arguments inside Europe for faster normalisation. Kyiv has not been fully briefed on every element of the latest US proposals. The energy piece can move independently of territorial or security outcomes.⁠

The net effect is a partial re-opening of the pre-2022 energy relationship, managed through American commercial intermediation rather than direct Russian-European contracts. It lowers short-term costs for some European industry and creates a revenue stream for Moscow. It also reintroduces energy as leverage inside NATO and the EU before the military balance in Ukraine has been settled.

The talks are real. The delivery is not. Nord Stream can be discussed in Washington and Moscow. It still has to be accepted in Berlin, Brussels, and the European utilities that would have to buy the gas. That last step has not moved.

$UE Q3 2026 earnings: Urban Edge raises its profit outlook, but debt costs rise

Urban Edge Properties, a shopping-center landlord in the Washington to Boston corridor, grew property profits faster as newly leased stores opened for business. Rental profit from centers owned a year ago rose 4.6%, above what the company's own plan pointed to, and new leases were signed at 27% higher rents. Chief executive Jeff Olson raised the full-year profit outlook for a third time, which by our math leaves same-property profit growth accelerating to nearly 6% in the fourth quarter.

• Same-property NOI growth (incl. renovations): 𝟒.𝟔% (above the 3.5–4.5% implied H2 pace)
• FFO per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟎.𝟑𝟖 (+6% from a year ago)
• New lease cash rent increase: 𝟐𝟔.𝟗% (12.8% last quarter)
• Full-year FFO outlook, excluding one-offs: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 $𝟎.𝟎𝟏 (middle of the range: $1.53 (+7%))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because new store openings lifted property income ahead of schedule and tenant defaults stayed below the company's allowance. One caution: the landlord stepped outside its core Northeast corridor to buy a $90 million Boca Raton center using credit line debt, which raised its full-year interest bill, while its backlog of signed leases waiting to open shrank by $1 million.

The question now is whether rental growth from the $21 million signed lease backlog and below-market Florida leases will outrun higher interest costs as debt grows and older mortgages come due in 2027. If the company sells more low-growth centers to pay down its $138 million credit line, property gains will flow through to per-share profit; if it keeps borrowing at current rates, interest expense will absorb much of the rent increase. Management's first 2027 outlook in February will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐒𝐚𝐦𝐞-𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Urban Edge owns shopping centers and tracks same-property net operating income (NOI), the rental profit from centers it owned a year ago after property expenses. That figure, including centers under renovation, grew 4.6% from a year ago, "primarily driven by rent commencements on new leases from our signed but not open pipeline". Property operating margin rose 1.2 percentage points to 66.3% because real estate taxes fell 1.4 percentage points of property revenue while maintenance rose 0.2 points.

This 4.6% growth topped the 3.5% to 4.5% second-half pace that the prior full-year outlook pointed to by our math. The real estate trust raised its full-year growth plan by 0.6 percentage points at the middle of the range to 4.1%, which leaves 5.7% growth for the fourth quarter by our math. Because only $0.7 million of new rent opens in the fourth quarter, most of that gain comes from stores that are already open.

What to watch: fourth-quarter same-property NOI growth when full-year results arrive in February. Reaching the implied 5.7% pace would show that recently opened stores and lower winter snow costs can carry growth into 2027.

🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐭 𝟐𝟕% 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬
Limited new retail construction gives the landlord pricing power when leases expire or underperforming chains leave. Chief executive Jeff Olson said the quarter's 26.9% cash rent increase on new leases for previously occupied spaces was "demonstrating the embedded value in our portfolio". Meanwhile, exposure to department store chain Kohl's fell from nine stores to eight, cutting its yearly base rent by 17.2% from last quarter to $8.3 million.

• New lease cash rent increase: 26.9% on 43,000 square feet, bringing the nine-month average to 28.1%
• Renewal and option cash rent increase: 11.5% on 406,000 square feet, with zero landlord spending on store build-outs
• Landlord build-out spending on new leases: $13.62 per square foot, down from $38.99 in 2025

Signing new tenants at 27% higher rents while spending two-thirds less on store build-outs than last year means more of every rent increase turns into cash. What to watch: full-year new-lease rent increases and landlord build-out spending per square foot in the fourth-quarter report. Holding rent increases above 20% with low build-out costs would confirm that tenant demand remains strong.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐔𝐫𝐛𝐚𝐧 𝐄𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐚 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭
"Our third quarter results reflect the strength of our operating platform and the progress of our capital recycling strategy," chief executive Jeff Olson said. Urban Edge sold Briarcliff Commons in New Jersey for $60.5 million, bought The Shops at West Falls Church in Virginia for $40.4 million, and in October paid $90.3 million for Regency Court in Boca Raton, Florida. Olson said Boca Raton "shares the dense, affluent demographics, high barriers to entry and limited new supply that exists in our D. C. to Boston portfolio".

The company says Regency Court is anchored by grocer Publix and pharmacy chain Walgreens, "both with in place rents significantly below market with limited remaining lease terms". Yet the numbers cut against a self-funded property swap: full-year acquisitions jumped to $185 million against only $60.5 million of property sales. To pay for Boca Raton, management borrowed $63 million on its credit line in October, pushing credit line debt to $138 million and raising its full-year interest cost outlook by $1.0 million.

Buying properties with credit line debt instead of property sales raises borrowing costs right away, while the rent increases at Publix and Walgreens will not happen until their leases expire. What to watch: new property sales announced in the fourth quarter to pay down the $138 million credit line balance. Without matching sales, higher interest expense will eat into the rent gains from the Florida purchase.

🔴 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐢𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐤 𝐚𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐝
Urban Edge relies on its signed-but-not-open pipeline, which is future yearly gross rent from signed leases where tenants have not yet opened for business, to drive future profit growth. During the third quarter, $2.6 million of yearly rent started paying as tenants such as Fidelity and Adidas opened their doors, while the leasing team added $1.6 million in new signed contracts. That left the pipeline at $21.0 million, down $1.0 million from June.

Because store openings are outrunning new signings, the pool of future rent is getting smaller. At the same time, the expected return on the $151.6 million of active renovation projects held at 12%, down from 15% a year ago and well below the 23% return earned on the $39.6 million of projects completed over the past year. As older, high-return projects finish, the remaining pipeline offers a smaller boost to future earnings.

What to watch: the signed-but-not-open pipeline dollar total and the expected return on active renovations in the fourth-quarter report. A drop below $20 million or a return below 12% would mean slower profit growth once the current wave of store openings finishes in 2027.

🔴 𝐒𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐥-𝐒𝐡𝐨𝐩 𝐎𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐁𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫-𝐄𝐧𝐝 𝐆𝐨𝐚𝐥
Small shops under 10,000 square feet pay an average base rent of $41.25 per square foot, more than double the $18.05 paid by large anchor stores. Management previously set a goal to push small-shop leased occupancy back above 93% by the end of 2026. In the third quarter, small-shop leased occupancy stood at 91.7%, unchanged from June and down from 92.5% a year ago, while overall leased occupancy dipped 0.2 percentage points from June to 96.4%.

Same-property leased occupancy rose 0.2 percentage points from June to 96.6%, leaving both shop and overall occupancy short of the year-end targets with one quarter left. Because small shops pay twice the rent per square foot of anchor tenants, empty shop spaces weigh heavily on rental revenue. What to watch: small-shop leased occupancy at year-end in the fourth-quarter supplement; falling short of 93% would show that replacing smaller tenants is taking longer than planned.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Two standing financial and regulatory concerns received no new numbers in the third-quarter earnings release or supplement, though management DID modify the $69.7 million Montehiedra mortgage out to 2033.

• 2027 mortgage refinancing cost: the company has $1.64 billion in mortgages with an average maturity of 3.0 years; the quarterly filing's debt footnote will show the exact 2027 maturities and rates.
• Sunrise Mall parcel sale: no update on regulatory approvals for the $75.9 million contract after paying $25 million to end a tenant lease earlier this year; the filing's property footnote will show its status.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬
Benchmark interest rates remain higher than when Urban Edge locked in its older mortgages. When the trust modified its $69.7 million loan on The Outlets at Montehiedra in October, it borrowed an extra $17 million at a 6.95% fixed rate (3.9% after Puerto Rico tax rules), while the original 5.0% loan will reset in June 2030 to the three-year US Treasury yield plus 2.5 percentage points.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐧𝐧𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀𝐫𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟓.𝟕𝐱  ⇘ decelerating
Debt relative to operating cash flow improved from 6.1x in the first quarter to 5.7x in the third quarter as property profit grew. Adjusted EBITDAre is property earnings before interest, taxes, and depreciation, excluding one-offs. Net debt stood at $1.63 billion, or 37.7% of total market value, before the $63 million October credit line borrowing.

𝐓𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟏.𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Uncollected rent balances fell 18.0% from $26.7 million at the end of 2025. Rent written off as uncollectible in the third quarter was $525 thousand, or 0.45% of gross property revenue by our math, beating the 0.60% to 0.75% second-half allowance management set last quarter and lifting operating cash flow for the first nine months by 29.9% to $171.1 million.

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟒.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Cash spending on property upgrades, new buildings, and tenant spaces fell 20.0% from $30.9 million a year ago as two renovation projects finished during the quarter. For the first nine months of 2026, total capital spending rose 40.7% from a year ago to $110.1 million, leaving $56.6 million still to spend on active renovations.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐅𝐎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞: $𝟏.𝟓𝟗–$𝟏.𝟔𝟏  ⇗ accelerating

Funds from operations (FFO), which adds back property depreciation and removes property sale gains from net income, moved up $0.015 at the middle of the range to $1.60 per share, up 11.9% from 2025. By our math, the plan leaves $0.39 per share for the fourth quarter, matching the fourth-quarter rate for FFO excluding one-offs.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐚𝐦𝐞-𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐍𝐎𝐈 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡, 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭: 𝟒.𝟎𝟎%–𝟒.𝟐𝟓%  ⇗ accelerating

By our math, after 3.6% growth over the first nine months, the full-year plan points to 5.7% growth in the fourth quarter, helped by an easy comparison against last year's fourth-quarter snow removal costs. It is the third raise this year: +0.125, +0.125, and +0.625 percentage points.

text:
Let me get this straight.

Crypto has a name for this scheme. Insiders hype a worthless token, flood your phone with fake urgency, take your money, cash out, and leave you holding the bag. The regulators shrug, and the insiders run it again next quarter under a new name. In Washington they call it the two-party system, and they were running it long before anyone had heard of Bitcoin.

Republicans and Democrats will tell you they are mortal enemies. Watch what they do with your phone number and you would never guess. They run the same tricks on the same victims, and they protect each other with the same exemptions they wrote for themselves. Two logos on one cash machine.

Every pump starts with distribution. You average thirteen political calls and texts a week. Reply STOP, and 72% of you keep getting them anyway. The Do Not Call list does nothing, because the people who wrote that law exempted the only telemarketers you aren’t allowed to escape: themselves. Your number came from the voter file, enriched by data brokers, then rented, swapped and sold to the next committee in line.

Then comes the token, something that sounds valuable and is worth nothing. On the right, Trump’s PAC emailed supporters, in his voice, “I want to try and get to heaven,” and asked for fifteen dollars. A billionaire president, crowdfunding his way past Saint Peter. Next came a “Citizens Only Survey” asking whether you’re an illegal alien and whether “ICE need[s] to come and track you down,” which you had to pay to submit. After that, a “National Security Briefing Membership” nobody has ever explained. Finally, a request to confirm the spelling of your name for your Tariff Check. The check is still in the mail. So is heaven.

The left minted its own coins. The DSCC warned that your membership expires at midnight. The five-dollar membership does not exist. The real one costs $44,300, and you are not invited. The DCCC offered a 400% match. House Majority PAC smelled weakness and pumped it to 600%. Nobody has ever met the matching donor, because the matching donor is Helvetica Bold.

Once you buy in, they lock you in. In 2020, Trump’s campaign pre-checked a tiny box that turned one donation into a weekly withdrawal, then pre-checked a second box to double it. When the banks drowned in fraud complaints, the campaign refunded $122 million. The FEC, a body that agrees on nothing, voted six to zero to ban the trick. Congress never touched it, because the trick works for everybody. Four years later CNN caught both the Trump and Harris campaigns using pre-checked boxes. Two parties, one checkbox, zero shame.

Every pump and dump needs bagholders, and the best ones can’t read the fine print anymore. An 81-year-old man in Arizona with dementia gave more than $80,000 through WinRed, sometimes more than a hundred donations in a single day, because he believed Donald Trump was texting him personally. A woman in cognitive decline gave more than $200,000 through ActBlue. Some elderly donors opened new credit cards and took out mortgages to keep the deadlines from expiring. The FTC says it has no jurisdiction. Neither does Grandma, and that is the entire business model.

When the heat came, Washington held a pair of hearings aimed carefully away from home. Republicans hauled ActBlue before Congress, where its CEO pleaded the Fifth twenty-two times. Democrats demanded the records of WinRed, which racked up 803 FTC complaints to ActBlue’s 120. Each party investigated fundraising fraud with tremendous courage and discovered, every single time, that it lives on the other side of the aisle. Neither has ever opened its own inbox.

Then the dump. One Democratic consulting network raised $678 million from people trying to save democracy, and by one Stanford count about 1.6% reached actual candidates. The consultants dispute that, and their best defense is that the real number might reach single digits. End Citizens United, a PAC founded to get money out of politics, raised $21.18 million and spent $21.14 million. They did get the money out. Of you. On the right, scam PACs played Trump’s own voice in robocalls, told seniors to press 3 to show their support, and sent 3% of the haul to candidates. Another promised a 100X match and spent 73% of what it raised on raising more. Mankind finally built the perpetual motion machine. It runs on retirees, and both parties hold the patent.

Your five dollars was never the point anyway. More than $15 billion has been raised for this midterm, and the biggest checks come from people who will never see a midnight deadline in their lives. What your five dollars buys them is your belief that you own a piece of the thing. You don’t. You own the bag.

Here is what the product delivered. A Congress at 10% approval. A 43-day shutdown, then a 76-day shutdown, each a record when it happened. New members told by their own party to dial for dollars four hours a day and legislate for about two, and judging by the output, they’ve been rounding the second number down. On the single question of protecting you from them, the two parties have voted in perfect harmony every time. They passed no ban on pre-checked boxes, left you no Do Not Call protection, and gave no agency jurisdiction over a dementia patient drained a hundred times in one afternoon. Every loophole that hurts you is one they built, and one they both keep open.

Even the con men get conned. The DNC, $18.5 million in debt, wired $28,860.92 to a scammer pretending to be its own chairman. Somebody finally sent a fake urgent email to a political party, and the party paid. It was the only fundraising email in history that worked exactly as written.

So let me get this straight one last time. They pump you with fear, mint worthless memberships, lock your card into autopay, harvest your grandparents, cash out to their consultants, sell your number to the next crew, and deliver shutdowns. In any other market that would be securities fraud. In this one it’s called a midterm.

Democracy dies at 11:59 p.m., one minute before a deadline that was never real, matched 600% by nobody.

Reply STOP to unsubscribe. Congress already did.

text:
Rapper @NICKIMINAJ has surfaced in speculation over President @realDonaldTrump’s next White House press secretary after Communications Director Steven Cheung jokingly suggested her for the post.

The position became vacant when Katie Zacharia left on Oct. 16, five days after taking over following Karoline Leavitt’s August departure. The press secretary serves as the president’s spokesperson and answers questions from journalists.

On Oct. 25, Cheung posted footage of Minaj aboard Air Force One praising Trump’s leadership, economic policies and approach to foreign affairs, then floated the rapper as a possible replacement.

The joke reached political prediction markets. On Oct. 26, Minaj’s implied chance on Polymarket briefly hit 8%, behind Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly at 18% and commentator Scott Jennings at 9%. By Oct. 27, her figure had fallen to 2%, while Kalshi put it at 4%. These figures reflect trading expectations, not public polling, and neither platform appoints White House staff.

Minaj has become increasingly vocal in supporting Trump. On Jan. 28, the Trinidad and Tobago-born rapper appeared alongside him at the Trump Accounts Summit in Washington, D.C., backed investment accounts for American children and called herself his number one fan.

She later displayed a Trump Gold Card and said her U.S. citizenship paperwork was being finalized. A White House official clarified that the card was commemorative rather than an immigration document. Minaj has not publicly confirmed obtaining U.S. citizenship.

On Oct. 25, Minaj also joined Trump at a Republican rally in Port Huron, Michigan, ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, voicing support for Trump and Republican candidates. Trump drew attention during the event by praising the rapper’s behind.

The White House has yet to name Zacharia’s replacement or confirm any formal offer to Minaj. Her inclusion in the discussion stems from Cheung’s joking remarks and subsequent prediction-market speculation.

text:
US hints at expanding Russian diesel deal
More Russian fuel could soon enter global markets despite the backlash in Ukraine, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said
Published 28 Oct, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/JQDAbHxH3W
More Russian diesel fuel could enter global markets as part of a trade agreement between Moscow and Washington struck earlier this month, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said. He claimed the shipments could be a “carrot” for Moscow to scale back fighting in Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump announced the landmark diesel deal with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, on October 9, saying Russia would release more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel immediately, 500,000 tons in November, another million afterward and potentially 3 million more, depending on refinery capacity.
Trump called lowering fuel prices for American consumers his “greatest priority” ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, where the Republicans are at risk of losing their congressional majority.
Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky condemned the surprise deal as a “weak decision,” prompting an angry response from Trump, who suggested that Ukraine replace Zelensky with someone willing to negotiate peace with Russia. Trump has also repeatedly pressed Zelensky to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, something Kiev has refused to do.
Speaking to CNBC on Tuesday, Wright described the diesel deal as an “incentive” for Moscow to stop hostilities with Ukraine, adding that more Russian tankers could “quite possibly” depart under a six-month sanctions waiver.
“It’s trying to put a carrot in front of Russia,” he said, arguing that reduced hostilities would allow Moscow to export more diesel and marginally ease global fuel shortages.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Aleksandr Novak said on Tuesday that three tankers carrying diesel are already en route to the US, with a fourth expected to depart Wednesday. On Sunday, he offered to supply as much as buyers wanted within Russia’s available export volumes, saying: “We can supply all of it.” He previously said Russian diesel exports could reach 3.5 million tons monthly by year-end.
During a meeting with Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff last week in St. Petersburg, Putin noted that global diesel prices fell 5%-6% after the deal was announced. Earlier this week, Reuters reported that Russia’s daily diesel output rose from 160,000 tons in early October to 180,000 tons after the introduction of new export quotas.
The agreement has nevertheless met bipartisan resistance in Washington, with a group of senators calling it a “gift to our adversary” and a betrayal of Ukraine. Novak pushed back on Tuesday, singling out Democrats and wondering why US lawmakers were acting “not in the interests of the residents of the United States.”

text:
Armenia ratifies US-backed TRIPP transport deal despite opposition objections

Armenia’s parliament has ratified a strategic cooperation agreement with the United States on a planned transport corridor linking Azerbaijan with its exclave of Nakhchivan through Armenian territory.

The agreement on the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) was approved by 63 votes to 32 on Wednesday. The ruling Civil Contract faction voted in favour, while the opposition factions Strong Armenia and Armenia (Hayastan) opposed it. 

The agreement was presented to parliament by Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan, who said the project would operate under Armenia’s sovereignty and jurisdiction.

The project is intended to reopen transport links across the South Caucasus after decades of conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan. It could include railways, roads, electricity transmission lines and fibre-optic cables, with possible oil and gas pipelines.

Under the agreement, a development company will be established with a 74% stake held by a US entity and 26% by Armenia. The initial arrangement will last 49 years, with an option to extend it by another 50 years by mutual agreement. If extended, Armenia’s share would rise to 49%. 

***
Opposition lawmakers have questioned whether the deal offers Armenia sufficient benefits in return for allowing Azerbaijan to establish a connection with Nakhchivan through its territory.

Anna Grigoryan, a lawmaker from the Armenia faction, argued during parliamentary debate that although the agreement is formally bilateral between Armenia and the US, Azerbaijan’s interests are strongly reflected in its terms.

Opposition representatives have also raised concerns about the lack of clear financial calculations for Armenia’s expected gains and the absence of a detailed agreement guaranteeing reciprocal transport access through Azerbaijani territory. 

***
Mirzoyan has argued that reopening regional routes would expand Armenia’s trade opportunities and strengthen its role as a transit hub. He has also said that Armenian authorities would retain control over border security, customs and law enforcement within the country.

The TRIPP agreement follows commitments made by Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at a meeting in Washington in August 2025, witnessed by US President Donald Trump. The broader initiative is intended to improve regional connectivity and support lasting peace between the two countries. 

The ratification is an important step towards implementing the project, but the development company’s charter and shareholders’ agreement still need to be finalised. The Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement, meanwhile, remains unsigned.

Washington is discussing a return of US oil majors to Russia as part of Ukraine peace talks, while Putin holds to maximalist preconditions.

The proposal, reported by the FT, offers renewed postwar business ties to bring Putin to the table. It was raised during envoy Steve Witkoff's Moscow visit in early September.

A US official said any economic deal would sit inside a comprehensive peace framework, and that nothing is finalised.

On his call with Finland's Alexander Stubb and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre, Putin said the war's "root causes", including NATO expansion, must be resolved before any negotiations. A deal must also recognise the "realities on the ground".

A source close to the Kremlin said that means no compromise on seizing all of Donbas.

The only concrete step so far is local. A ceasefire in occupied Oleshky began on October 27 for aid and evacuations, and First Lady Melania Trump said it has been expanded within Kherson region.

Ahead of Abu Dhabi talks in the first half of November, Trump said a Putin-Zelensky meeting would soon be arranged.
