text:
I'm at Excalibur #45 now, and I want to go back through Courtney Ross and Sat-Yr-9, because there is a lot of history sitting underneath that name and that face.

First, there are three women to keep straight. Courtney Ross is Brian Braddock's old girlfriend. Saturnyne is the powerful official involved in policing the multiverse. Sat-Yr-9 is the dictator from another reality who murders Courtney and takes her place. They are counterparts, separate people with the same face. Saturnyne isn't secretly the woman pretending to be Courtney.

Courtney goes back to Captain Britain #3 in 1976, right near the beginning of Brian's published history. She's part of his life at Thames University, before Excalibur exists and before this becomes a story about somebody stealing her life. Brian has the familiar superhero problem of disappearing when trouble starts, then looking unreliable to the people he left behind. Courtney is one of those people, but she also makes an effort to spend time with him and stands up for him against Jacko Tanner.

Those early stories put her through quite a bit. She is injured during the Lord Hawk storyline. In Super Spider-Man and Captain Britain #233–234, she joins the university expedition to Loch Ness, where Captain Britain has to rescue the students from their sabotaged bathysphere. Then #235–238 brings the Black Baron, a vampire and werewolf who sees Courtney as the image of his lost love and wants to make her his bride. Brian gets her out of that too.

That matters when she returns in Excalibur. Courtney has already lived through the strange and dangerous side of Brian's life. She eventually knows he is Captain Britain, and their relationship continues with that knowledge.

There is also an earlier Arcade connection. Marvel Team-Up #65–66 brings Brian together with Spider-Man and introduces Arcade's threat. Courtney is a captive in Murderworld in #66, and the two heroes save her. The Excalibur encounter is a return to someone who has already endangered her, not her first experience of him.

Brian's long absence separates them. Courtney believes he has died, grieves, and builds a life without him. Even while she is absent from his everyday life, the comics use her as somebody who matters to him: in Mighty World of Marvel #10, Jaspers torments Brian with an illusion in which Courtney is his wife. That is an illusion, not a marriage in Courtney's history.

Meanwhile, Sat-Yr-9 enters the Captain Britain stories in the 1985 series, starting with #2. She rules a brutal alternate Britain, and Kaptain Briton, that world's counterpart of Brian, is her lover. He flees to Brian's world. Her efforts to retrieve him eventually involve Gatecrasher and the Technet.

In #5–6, Kaptain Briton defeats Brian, switches their clothing, and lets the Technet take the wrong man home. Brian ends up facing Sat-Yr-9 while the impostor stays at Braddock Manor. Betsy kills Kaptain Briton in self-defense after he attacks her. Brian convinces the Technet they have the wrong person, and they fight their way out of Sat-Yr-9's reach.

Captain Britain #14 follows through on her regime. Roma sends Captain UK to deal with Sat-Yr-9, and she is overthrown. When Excalibur #3 picks that thread up, Sat-Yr-9 is a prisoner. Rupert Holloway wanders through one of Widget's gateways into her cell, providing the opening for her return to the story.

Back on Brian's Earth, the real Courtney has become a senior banking executive. Excalibur #1 reunites them. She has stopped dyeing her naturally blonde hair auburn, which makes the resemblance to her counterparts much more apparent. She has money, independence, and a shared history with Brian. He can talk to her about things he struggles to discuss with Meggan.

The triangle is already uncomfortable before the replacement. Brian is drawn back toward Courtney while he is still involved with Meggan, and Kurt challenges him about the hurt he is causing. Courtney's murder shouldn't erase her own relationship with Brian, or turn everything leading up to it into something her killer did.

Excalibur #4–5 puts Courtney through Murderworld again, this time with the Crazy Gang involved. She helps restore the heroes after their minds have been switched, working with Kitty instead of simply waiting for someone to carry her out.

Then she goes home, still exhilarated at having survived. Sat-Yr-9 arrives and kills her. By the time Brian comes to the apartment, the woman welcoming him is the impostor. Courtney's burned outline is still on the floor.

That ending changes every subsequent scene carrying her name. Brian thinks an old relationship is opening up again. The reader has seen the woman he remembers being removed from her own life.

Sat-Yr-9 starts using that stolen position. In #9, she draws Nigel Frobisher into a high-stakes card game at the Hellfire Club and leaves him owing her more than he can pay. In #10, she watches Rachel and Kitty and thinks about possessing their power and potential. Her interest in them is already on the page.

Nigel is then sent to hire the Technet. That leads to Jamie Braddock's extraction from Doctor Crocodile in #15. By #21, Jamie's reality-warping powers are being used to turn the original Vixen into an actual fox and install Nigel in her place. Behind the respectable banking identity, another network of stolen identities and power is taking shape.

And alongside that, she is getting close to Kitty.

In #21, Kitty is stranded at home while the rest of Excalibur is lost across realities. She has already lost people, believes the X-Men are dead, and now fears another team has disappeared from her life. The woman she knows as Courtney listens, comforts her, and offers her someone to depend on.

Kitty has a reason to trust that face. She met the real Courtney during the Arcade rescue. Sat-Yr-9 gets to benefit from a connection somebody else made.

Then #24 gives Kitty her fifteenth birthday: new clothes, a fancy dinner, Paris, dancing, and the use of a Jaguar. It can look like an adult making sure a lonely teenager has one good day. But the encouragement comes with a lesson about being the person who makes the rules, including driving when she isn't legally old enough.

The same issue also shows the actual Saturnyne dealing with the rest of Excalibur at the Omniversal Hub. Keeping those two women separate is essential to reading it.

The St. Searle's storyline in #32–34 continues the influence. “Courtney” has arranged Kitty's schooling, watches how she handles herself, and ultimately helps secure a financial arrangement that saves the school. Kitty makes real connections there and finds her way back to Excalibur. The help she receives still comes from someone whose identity she doesn't know.

That's where I'm leaving this as I reach #45. Courtney's history includes the student, the girlfriend, the survivor, and the banker who rebuilt her life. Sat-Yr-9 takes the reputation and relationships attached to all of that and uses them to get close to people.

The uncomfortable part is how ordinary those scenes can look. A conversation. A favor. A birthday. Someone offering to help with school. Everybody is dealing with a familiar face, while the reader knows what happened to the woman it belongs to.

text:
Dear President McCullough, 
I read your open letter to the Seminole faithful, and I confess it brought to mind Bill Clinton's famous "I feel your pain" — an expression of empathy offered precisely where accountability is owed. "I hear you. I understand your frustration" is easy to say when you have been President for five years and the frustration is the product of decisions made on your watch and that of the Board of Trustees: a football program that has not won a road game in three years, a head coach retained last year in part to avoid a buyout now reported at roughly $46.7 million, and an Athletic Director dismissed without cause in mid-September with a permanent successor still unnamed more than a month later. Supporting the young men who play for Florida State does not require endorsing the decisions of the people who run Florida State athletics, and your letter asks fans to do the former as a substitute for answers about the latter. The comparison that should concern you is Penn State. When that university's leadership failed at oversight, it was the President and the Athletic Director who were ultimately charged with perjury — proof that the people at the top of an institution are not exempt from the consequences of what happens under their management. I am not equating the two situations, only the principle: university presidents and trustees answer for the institutions they govern. At Florida State, the pattern of decision-making — protecting a struggling head coach from an unpayable buyout, firing the Athletic Director without cause, and committing enormous sums to athletic facilities while the product on the field collapsed — deserves that same kind of scrutiny from top to bottom. That is why I have no doubt that Chairman Peter Collins has committed violations of Florida law in connection with the wasteful spending and the poor, if not unlawful, decisions surrounding the Athletic Facilities, and he should be held fully accountable for them. What I ask of you is simple: commission a full, independent, and public review of every expenditure and approval made under his chairmanship of the Board of Trustees, with the findings released to the fans, donors, students, and taxpayers who ultimately pay for them. "I feel your pain" was not a plan in 1992, and it is not a plan now. The standard, as you yourself wrote, is not negotiable — and that standard applies to you and to Mr. Collins first. #FSU #FSUFootball #SeminoleFootball #ESPN College Football #FSUAthletic Department #ACCFootball

text:
BNT's WEDNESDAY MORNING THOUGHTS 🤔

MY TOP 5 CANDIDATES FOR BAYLOR'S NEXT HEAD FOOTBALL COACH...PLUS 3 WILD CARDS!

Baylor Family, Monday I shared why I have confidence in @DougMcNameeBU to lead this search. Tuesday, I talked about what Baylor needs in its next head coach.

Today, I'm naming names!

These are MY five preferred candidates, in order. No inside information, no claim that any of them has been contacted, and no guarantee they'd accept the job.

Let's have some fun with this!

1. JEFF TRAYLOR — UTSA

PROS

• Three Texas high school state championships and an extensive network of recruiting relationships throughout the state.

• Built UTSA into a winner, including consecutive Conference USA titles in 2021 and 2022.

• UTSA is enjoying a strong 2026 rebound after two less impressive seasons.

CONS

• The decline in 2024–25 raises questions about maintaining success.

• Has never coached a Power Four program as head coach.

BNT's Take: I love his Texas roots and his ability to build a program. But I want to know why UTSA slipped after its championship run and what he'd do differently at Baylor.

2. SPENCER DANIELSON — BOISE STATE

PROS

• Three consecutive Mountain West championships and a 30–9 head coaching record entering this week's games.

• Has already taken Boise State to the College Football Playoff.

• Strong leadership, emphasis on culture, and values that appear to fit Baylor.

CONS

• Has spent most of his career outside Texas.

• Would need to build recruiting relationships in one of the nation's most competitive talent markets.

BNT's Take: Maybe the most intriguing candidate on my list. He's only 37, already knows how to win championships, and could be here a LONG time. If Doug puts him at No. 1, I wouldn't argue.

3. JASON ECK — NEW MEXICO

PROS

• Took Idaho to three consecutive FCS playoff appearances after inheriting a struggling program.

• Went 9–4 at New Mexico in 2025 and has started 2026 at 6–1.

• Proven ability to identify, develop, and win with overlooked talent.

CONS

• Has never been a Power Four head coach.

• Limited Texas recruiting background compared with Traylor and Kinne.

BNT's Take: This guy might be the best pure program builder on my list. Fifteen wins in his first 20 games at New Mexico? That's impressive! Give him Baylor's resources and I'm interested in seeing what happens.

4. JAKE DICKERT — WAKE FOREST

PROS

• Has led programs at Washington State and Wake Forest, two challenging Power Four jobs.

• Has experience managing rosters, recruiting, and competing against better-funded opponents.

• His work at Wake Forest in 2026 has attracted national attention.

CONS

• Hasn't established a consistent conference championship contender.

• Would need to demonstrate he can recruit Texas and elevate Baylor beyond simply being competitive.

BNT's Take: Don't overlook this guy. He's done more with less at places where winning isn't easy. My question is whether he can take Baylor from being a respectable program to a CHAMPIONSHIP program.

5. G.J. KINNE — TEXAS STATE

PROS

• Led Incarnate Word to a 12–2 season and a deep FCS playoff run.

• Offensive creativity, Texas recruiting ties, and three bowl victories at Texas State.

• His father played and coached at Baylor.

CONS

• Texas State's conference record under Kinne is 13–13.

• His teams have shown flashes of excellence without consistently dominating their conference.

BNT's Take: He's young, talented, and has Baylor connections. But after watching our program struggle with consistency, I'm reluctant to gamble on another coach who hasn't demonstrated sustained success.

THREE WILD CARDS! 

LINCOLN RILEY — USC

PROS

• Won FOUR consecutive Big 12 championships at Oklahoma.

• Proven offensive innovator and elite quarterback developer.

• Knows Texas recruiting and the Big 12.

CONS

• The financial commitment could be enormous.

• His USC tenure raises questions about defense and building a complete program.

• Would Baylor be his destination or simply his next stop?

BNT's Take: FOUR straight Big 12 championships! That deserves attention. But before writing a massive check, I'd want to know he's coming to Baylor to build something special, not just leave Los Angeles.

ROBERT GRIFFIN III — RGIII

PROS

• Heisman Trophy winner and one of the most important players in Baylor history.

• Loves Baylor, understands its potential, and has publicly expressed interest.

• Would immediately bring excitement and national attention.

CONS

• No college coaching experience.

• Recruiting, hiring assistants, managing NIL, and running a major program are enormous responsibilities.

BNT's Take: RGIII helped change Baylor football forever. I'd love to see him involved with our program. But handing him the head coaching job without coaching experience? That's a pretty big leap, even for a Heisman winner!

JOE KLANDERMAN — BAYLOR

PROS

• Helped Kansas State win the 2022 Big 12 championship as defensive coordinator.

• Coached at North Dakota State during four FCS national championship seasons.

• Knows our players and has five games to demonstrate his leadership.

CONS

• No permanent FBS head coaching experience.

• Five games provide a very limited opportunity to evaluate him.

BNT's Take: Joe deserves our support and a fair opportunity. I'm watching how these Bears respond, how prepared they look, and whether they improve. If he makes a compelling case, Doug should listen.

SO WHO GETS MY FIRST CALL?

JEFF TRAYLOR.

But I'll admit something. Spencer Danielson is close enough that I could change my mind.

Traylor offers the Texas connections and program-building experience I value. Danielson offers an impressive championship résumé and potentially a decade or more of leadership.

And Jason Eck? He might turn out to be better than either one!

That's what makes this search so interesting.

I don't want Baylor to hire a coach simply because he wins the press conference. I want the guy who wins BIG 12 CHAMPIONSHIPS!

As I've said all week, I'm looking for someone who can build something that LASTS.

We've reached the mountaintop before. Now let's find the coach who can keep us there.

YOUR TURN, BAYLOR FAMILY!

Who's YOUR No. 1 choice?

Who did I rank too high, too low, or leave off entirely?

I'm prepared for your disagreements. My attorney, @BearNLaw, has already requested an increase in his retainer. ⚖️ lol

xoxo,
BNT

“Different Leaders, Same Outcome”

text:
Maybe Elon Musk should simply establish a country on Mars. Several countries already offer citizenship through investment without requiring applicants to set foot there. So why not develop something similar for Mars?

Yes, the Outer Space Treaty, other international legal obligations and UN resolutions complicate matters. But @ElonMusk has never shied away from a fight, and according to @Grok, there is a coherent legal argument for at least trying. Here is Grok’s idea.

Legal Position (Counsel’s Submission):

Core Claim

An organised community of persons, regardless of its members’ existing nationalities, can proclaim a state on Mars. The non-appropriation rule of the Outer Space Treaty does not prevent this because it is either inapplicable, qualified by subsequent norms, or subject to a narrower interpretation. This position rests on the right to self-determination, a functional reading of the Montevideo criteria, and the freedom of exploration and use under Article I of the Outer Space Treaty.

Legal Foundations

Right to self-determination of an emerging community

Article III of the Outer Space Treaty subjects space activities to international law, including the Charter of the United Nations. The right of peoples to self-determination (Article 1 of the UN Charter and customary international law) applies to an organised group that constitutes itself as a new political community. It does not require its members to renounce their existing nationalities beforehand. Where the absolute non-appropriation rule in Article II of the Outer Space Treaty conflicts with the right to self-determination, the latter prevails as a higher-ranking norm grounded in human rights. A community that establishes a permanent population, its own government, and the capacity to enter into relations with other states on Mars is exercising this right.

Article II of the Outer Space Treaty covers only appropriation by existing states

The text prohibits “national appropriation.” The term “national” refers to appropriation by already existing states. A new entity that comes into existence only through its proclamation and the establishment of effective control is not an existing state appropriating a celestial body. Article VI of the Outer Space Treaty obliges States Parties only to bear responsibility for the national activities of their own nationals and to authorise those activities. The emergence of a new subject of international law through a group of persons does not automatically fall within this attribution of responsibility, provided that the group does not act as an organ or agent of an existing state.

Functional statehood rather than territorial appropriation of the celestial body

The entity does not claim sovereignty over the soil of Mars as such. It exercises jurisdiction over its members and the installations it constructs and, where required, registers, by analogy with flag-state jurisdiction over ships and the arrangements governing the International Space Station. Article VIII of the Outer Space Treaty confirms jurisdiction and control over objects and their personnel. Once the community establishes its own installations, institutes a legal order, and exercises effective control, functional statehood arises. On this reading, the Montevideo criteria are satisfied: a permanent population, an effective government, the capacity to enter into relations with other states, and a defined territory comprising the controlled installations and the immediate area required for their operation.

Fundamental change of circumstances and subsequent practice

Article 62 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties permits a fundamental change of circumstances to be invoked. The Outer Space Treaty was concluded in 1967 against the backdrop of an uninhabited outer space. The possibility of permanent, self-sustaining human settlements and the emergence of new political communities on a celestial body was not foreseeable. In addition, subsequent state practice (national laws on resource utilisation, the Artemis Accords and their provisions on safety zones, and commercial landings) has already qualified an absolute reading of Article II. Under Article 31(3)(b) of the Vienna Convention, this practice must be taken into account when interpreting the treaty.

Recognition and effective control

Under the declaratory theory, statehood arises when the relevant criteria are fulfilled. Under the constitutive theory, recognition by a sufficient number of states is decisive. Under either theory, the new entity can exist. States that have not ratified the Outer Space Treaty, or that interpret the non-appropriation principle narrowly, can recognise the entity if they accept its functional jurisdiction and do not claim territorial title to the entire celestial body.

Implementation

• The group adopts a constitution and proclaims the state.

• It seeks a launching state willing to authorise the mission under a narrow reading of Articles II and VI of the Outer Space Treaty, or a state that is not a party to the treaty.

• After landing, the settlement is established with a government, a legal order, and a permanent presence. Functional jurisdiction is exercised over persons and installations.

• A diplomatic note is sent to interested states requesting recognition on the basis of the arguments above.

• In parallel, an amendment to the Outer Space Treaty is sought under Article XV, or negotiations are initiated on an additional protocol expressly permitting permanent settlements.

Killer Test

The least expensive test capable of refuting this position within four weeks is for the group to submit a formal request to a major launching state for authorisation of a mission whose declared purpose is to proclaim a sovereign entity on Mars, relying on the right to self-determination and functional jurisdiction. If that state refuses, explicitly citing Articles II and VI of the Outer Space Treaty, and withholds all authorisation, the practical route is blocked unless the treaty is amended or the launching state breaches it. Without an authorised launch, no facts on the ground can arise to which this legal position could be applied.

text:
AN HUMBLE ATTEMPT TO PROMOTE EXPLICIT AGREEMENT AND VISIBLE UNION OF GOD’S PEOPLE - IN EXTRAORDINARY PRAYER - FOR THE REVIVAL OF RELIGION AND THE ADVANCEMENT OF CHRIST’S KINGDOM ON EARTH
By Jonathan Edwards (1703 – 1758)

Every Wednesday, DV

Continuing...

PART II.
MOTIVES TO A COMPLIANCE WITH WHAT IS PROPOSED IN THE MEMORIAL.

I now proceed to the second thing intended in this Discourse, viz. to offer to consideration some things, which may tend to induce the people of God to comply with the proposal and request, made to them in the Memorial.

SECT. I.
The latter-day glory not yet accomplished.

It is evident from the Scripture, that there is yet remaining a great advancement of the interest of religion
285
and the kingdom of Christ in this world, by an abundant outpouring of the Spirit of God, far greater and more extensive than ever yet has been. It is certain, that many things, which are spoken concerning a glorious time of the church’s enlargement and prosperity in the latter days, have never yet been fulfilled. There has never yet been any propagation and prevalence of religion, in any wise, of that extent and universality which the prophecies represent. It is often foretold and signified, in a great variety of strong expressions, that there should a time come, when all nations, throughout the whole habitable world, should embrace the true religion, and be brought into the church of God. It was often promised to the patriarchs, that “in their seed all the nations, or (as it is sometimes expressed) all the families of the earth shall be blessed.” 318 Agreeably to this, it is said of the Messiah, Psal. lxxii. 11.“That all nations shall serve him;” and in ver. 17. “Men shall be blessed in him, and all nations shall call him blessed.” And in Isa. ii. 2. it is said, that “all nations shall flow unto the mountain of the house of the Lord.” And Jer. iii. 17. “That all nations shall be gathered unto the name of the Lord to Jerusalem, and shall walk no more after the imagination of their evil heart.” “That all flesh shall come and worship before the Lord,”.Isa. lxvi. 23.”. “And that all flesh should see the glory of God together,” Isa. xl. 5. “And that all flesh should come to him that hears prayer,” Psal. lxv. 2. Christ compares the kingdom of heaven in this world “to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened;” Matt. xiii. 33.

It is natural and reasonable to suppose, that the whole world should finally be given to Christ, as one whose right it is to reign, as the proper heir of him who is originally the King of all nations, and the possessor of heaven and earth. And the Scripture teaches us, that God the Father hath constituted his Son, as God-man, in his kingdom of grace, or mediatorial kingdom, to be the heir of the world, that he might in this kingdom have “the heathen for his inheritance, and the utmost ends of the earth for his possession.” Heb. i. 2. and ii. 8. Psal. ii. 6, 7, 8. Thus Abraham is said to be the heir of the world, not in himself, but in his seed, which is Christ, Rom. iv. 13. And how was this to be fulfilled to Abraham, but by God’s fulfilling that great promise, that “in his seed all the nations of the earth should be blessed?” For that promise is what the apostle is speaking of: which shows, that God has appointed Christ to be the heir of the world in his kingdom of grace, and to possess and reign over all nations, through the propagation of his gospel, and the power of his Spirit communicating the blessings of it. God hath appointed him to this universal dominion by a most solemn oath; Isa. xlv. 23. “I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear.” (Compared with Phil. ii. 10, 11.) Though the solemn oath of God the Father is to be understood in so comprehensive a sense, as to extend to what shall be accomplished at the day of judgment, yet it is evident by the foregoing and following verses, that the thing most directly intended, is what shall be fulfilled by spreading the gospel of his salvation, and the power of the Spirit of grace, bringing “all the ends of the earth to look to him that they may be saved,” and come to him for “righteousness and strength, that in him they might be justified, and might glory.”

God has suffered many earthly princes to extend their conquests over a great part of the face of the earth, and to possess a dominion of vast extent, and one monarchy to conquer and succeed another, the latter being still the greater; it is reasonable to suppose, that a much greater glory in this respect should be reserved for Christ, God’s own Son and rightful heir, who has purchased the dominion by so great and hard a service: it is reasonable to suppose, that his dominion should be far the largest, and his conquests vastly the greatest and most extensive. And thus the Scriptures represent the matter, in Nebuchadnezzar’s vision, and the prophet’s interpretation, Daniel ii. There are four great monarchies of the earth, one succeeding another, are represented by the great image of gold, silver, brass, iron, and clay; but at last a stone, cut out of the mountain without hands, smites the image upon his feet, which breaks the iron, clay, brass, silver and gold in pieces, that all become as the chaff of the summer threshing floors, and the wind carries them away, that no place is found for them; but the stone waxes great, becomes a great mountain, and fills the whole earth: signifying the kingdom which the Lord God of heaven should set up in the world, last of all, which should break in pieces and consume all other kingdoms. Surely this representation leads us to suppose, that this last kingdom shall be of much greater extent man any of the preceding.

The like representation is made in the 7th chapter of Daniel;. there the four monarchies are represented by four great beasts that arose successively, one conquering and subduing another; the fourth and last of these is said to be dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly, and to have great iron teeth, and to devour and break in pieces, and stamp the residue with his feet; yea, it is said, ver. 23. that the kingdom represented by this beast shall devour the whole earth: but last of all, one like the Son of man appears, coming to the Ancient of days, and being brought near before him, and receiving of him a dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages should serve him. This last circumstance, of the vast extent and universality of his dominion, is manifestly spoken of as one thing greatly distinguishing this holy kingdom from all the preceding monarchies. Although of one of the former it was said, that it should devour the whole earth, yet we are naturally led, both by the much greater emphasis and strength of the expressions, as well as by the whole connexion and tenor of the prophecy, to understand the universality here expressed in a much more extensive and absolute sense. And the terms used in the interpretation of this vision are such, that scarcely any can be devised more strong, to signify an absolute universality of dominion over the inhabitants of the face of the earth; ver. 27. “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the most high God.” Agreeably to this, the gospel is represented as “preached unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and tongue, and kindred, and people,” Rev. xiv. 6.

The universal prevalence of true religion in the latter days, is sometimes expressed by its reaching to the “utmost ends of the earth,” (Psal. ii. 8.) “To all the ends of the earth, and of the world, (Psal. xxii. 27. Psal. lxvii. 7. Psal. xcviii. 3. Isa. xlv. 22.) “All the ends of the earth, with those that are far off upon the sea,” (Psal. lxv. 5.) “From the rising of the sun to the going down of the same,” (Psal. cxiii. 3. Mal. i. 11.) “The outgoing of the morning and of the evening,” (Psal. lxv. 8.) It seems that all the most strong expressions, that were in use among the Jews to signify the habitable world in its utmost extent, are used to signify the extent of the church of God in the latter days. And in many places, a variety of these expressions is used, and there is an accumulation of them, expressed with great force.

It would be unreasonable to say, these are only bold figures, used after the manner of the eastern nations, to express the great extent of the Christian church, at and after the days of Constantine. To say so, would be in effect to say, that it would have been impossible for God, if he had desired it, plainly to have foretold any thing that should absolutely have extended to all nations of the earth. I question whether it be possible to find out a more strong expression, to signify an absolute universality of the knowledge of the true religion through the habitable world, than that in Isa. xi. 9. “The earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.” Which is as much as to say, as there is no place in the vast ocean where there is not water, so there shall be no part of the world of mankind where there is not the knowledge of the Lord; as there is no part of the wide bed or cavity possessed by the sea, but what is covered with water, so there shall be no part of the habitable world that shall not be covered by the light of the gospel, and possessed by the
286
true religion. Waters are often in prophecy put for nations and multitudes of people. So the waters of the main ocean seem sometimes to be put for the inhabitants of the earth in general; as in Ezekiel’s vision of the waters of the sanctuary, (Ezek. xlvii.) which flowed from the sanctuary, and ran east, till they came to the ocean, and were at first a small stream, but continually increased till they became a great river; and when they came to the sea, the water even of the vast ocean was healed, (ver. 8.) representing the conversion of the world to the true religion in the latter days.

It seems evident, that the time will come, when there will not be one nation remaining in the world, which shall not embrace the true religion, in that God has expressly revealed, that no one such nation shall be left standing on the earth; Isa. lx. 12. “the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” God has declared that heathen idolatry and all the worship of false gods shall be wholly abolished, in the most universal manner, so that it shall be continued in no place under the heavens, or upon the face of the earth; Jer. x. 11. “The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens.” Ver. 15. “They are vanity, and the work of errors, in the time of their visitation they shall perish.” This must be understood as what shall be brought to pass while this earth and these heaven remain, i. e. before the end of the world. Agreeable to this is Isa. liv. 1, 2. “Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the Lord. Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thy habitation: spare not, lengthen thy cords, strengthen thy stakes.” Ver. 5. “For thy Maker is thy husband; the Lord of Hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called.”

The prophecies of the New Testament do no less evidently show, that a time will come when the gospel shall universally prevail, and the kingdom of Christ be extended over the whole habitable earth, in the most proper sense. Christ says, (John xii. 32.) “I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.” It is fit, that when the Son of God becomes man, he should have dominion over all mankind. It is fit, that since he became an inhabitant of the earth, and shed his blood on the earth, he should possess the whole earth. It is fit, seeing here he became a servant, and was subject to men, and was arraigned before them, and judged, condemned, and executed by them, and suffered ignominy and death in a most public manner, before Jews and Gentiles being lifted up to view on the cross upon a hill, near that populous city Jerusalem, at a most public time, when there were many hundred thousand spectators, from all parts that should be rewarded with an universal dominion over mankind; and it is here declared he shall be.

The apostle, in the Rom. xi. 11th of Romans, teaches us to look on that great outpouring of the Spirit, and ingathering of souls into Christ’s kingdom, in those days, first of the Jews and then of the Gentiles, to be but as the first-fruits of the intended harvest, both with regard to Jews and Gentiles, as a sign that all should in due time be gathered in; ver. 16. “For if the first-fruit be holy, the lump is also holy; and if the root be holy, so are the branches.” And in that context, the apostle speaks of the fulness of both Jews and Gentiles, as what shall hereafter be brought in, distinctly from the ingathering from among both, in those primitive ages of Christianity. In ver. 12. we read of the fulness of the Jews, and in the 25th, of the fulness of the Gentiles. And in ver. 30-32. the apostle teaches us to look upon that infidelity and darkness, which first prevailed over all Gentile nations, before Christ came, and afterwards over the Jews, as what was wisely permitted for the manifestation of the glory of God’s mercy, in due time, on the whole world, constituted of Jews and Gentiles. “God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.” These things plainly show, that the time is coming when the whole world of mankind shall be brought into the church of Christ; the fulness of both, the whole lump, all the nation of the Jews, and all the world of Gentiles.

In the last great conflict between the church of Christ and her enemies, before the commencement of the glorious time of the church’s peace and rest, the kings of the earth, and the WHOLE WORLD, are represented as gathered together, Rev. xvi. 14. And then the seventh angel pours out his vial into the air, which limits the kingdom of Satan, as god of this world; and that kingdom is represented as utterly overthrown, ver. 17,. &c. In another description of that great battle, (chap. xix.) Christ is represented as riding forth, having on his head many crowns, and on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords. Which we may well suppose signifies, that he is now going to that conquest, whereby he shall set up a kingdom, in which he shall be King of kings, in a far more extensive manner than either Babylonish, Persian, Grecian, or Roman monarchs were. And in ver. 17., and following, an angel appears standing in the sun, that overlooks the whole world, calling on Rev. xix. 17, 18. “all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, to come and eat the flesh of kings,” &c. And in consequence of the great victory Christ gains at that time, “an angel comes down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit, and a great chain in his hand, and lays hold on the devil, and binds him, and casts him into the bottomless pit, and shuts him up, and sets a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more. 319 ” Satan being dispossessed of that highest monarchy on earth, the Roman empire, and cast out in the time of Constantine is represented (chap. xii.) by his being cast down from heaven to the. earth, but now there is something far beyond that; he is cast out of the earth, and is shut up in hell, and confined to that alone, so that he has no place left him in this world of mankind, high or low.

Now will any be so unreasonable as to say, that all these things do not signify more than that one third part of the world should be brought into the church of Christ; beyond which it cannot be pretended that the Christian religion has ever vet reached, in its greatest extent? Those countries which belonged to the Roman empire, that were brought to the profession of Christianity after the reign of Constantine, are but a small part of what the habitable world now is. As to extent of ground, they altogether bear, I suppose, no greater proportion to it, than the land of Canaan did to the Roman empire. And our Redeemer in his kingdom of grace has hitherto possessed but a little part of the world, in its most flourishing state, since arts are arisen to their greatest height; and a very great part of the world is but lately discovered, and much remains undiscovered to this day. These things make it very evident, that the main fulfilment of those prophecies, that speak of the glorious advancement of Christ’s kingdom on earth, is still to come.

And as there has been nothing as yet, with regard to the flourishing of religion, and the advancement of Christ’s kingdom, of such extent as to answer the prophecies, so neither has there been any thing of that duration that is foretold. The prophecies speak of Jerusalem being made the joy of the whole earth, and also the Joy of many generations. (Psal. xlviii. 2. Isa. lx. 15. That “God’s people should long enjoy the work of their hands,” (Isa. lxv. 22.) That they should “reign with Christ a thousand years,” (Rev. xx.) by which we must at least understand a very long time. But it would be endless to mention all the places, which signify that the time of the church’s great peace and prosperity should be of long continuance. Almost all the prophecies, that speak of her latter-day glory, imply it; and it is implied in very many of them, that when once this day of the church’s advancement and peace is begun, it shall never end till the world ends; or, at least, that there shall be no more a return of her troubles and adversity for any considerable continuance. Then “the days of her mourning shall be ended;” her tribulations ” be as the waters of Noah, unto God, that as he has sworn that the waters of Noah should no more pass over the earth, so he will swear that he will no more be wroth with his people, or rebuke them.” It is implied that “God’s people should no more walk after the imagination of their evil hearts; that God would hide himself no more from the house of Israel; because he has poured out his Spirit upon them; that their sun should no more go down, nor
287
the moon withdraw itself; that the light should not be clear and dark,” (i. e. there should be no more an interchange of light and darkness, as used to be,) but that it should be all one continued day; not day and night (for so the words are in the original in Zech. xiv. 7.) alternately, “but it shall come to pass, that at evening time (i. e. at the time that night and darkness used to be) it shall be light; and that the nations should beat their swords into plow-shares, and their spears into pruning-hooks, and that nation should not lift up sword against nation, nor learn war any more; but that there should be abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.”

But the church of Christ has never yet enjoyed a state of peace and prosperity for any long time; on the contrary, the time for her rest, and of the flourishing state of religion, have ever been very short. Hitherto the church may say, (as in Isa. lxiii. 17, 18.) “Return, for thy servants’ sake, the tribes of thine inheritance; the people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while.” The quietness that the church of God enjoyed after the beginning of Constantine’s reign, was very short. The peace the empire enjoyed, in freedom from war, was not more than twenty years; no longer nor greater than it had enjoyed under some of the heathen emperors. After this the empire was rent in pieces by intestine wars, and wasted almost every where by the invasions and incursions of barbarous nations; and the Christian world, soon after, was all in contention and confusion, by heresies and divisions in matters of religion. And the church of Christ has never as yet been, for any long time, free from persecution; especially when truth has prevailed, and true religion flourished. It is manifest, that hitherto the people of God have been kept under, and Zion has been in a low afflicted state, and her enemies have had the chief sway.

Another thing which makes it exceedingly manifest, that the day of the church’s greatest advancement on earth, which is foretold in Scripture, has never yet come, is, that it is so plainly and expressly revealed, this day shall succeed the last of the four monarchies, even the Roman, in its last state, wherein it is divided into ten kingdoms, and after the destruction of antichrist, signified by the little horn, whose reign is contemporary with the reign of the ten kings. These things are very plain in the 2d and 7th chapters of Daniel,. and also in the Revelation of St. John. And it is also plain by the 9th chapter of Romans. that it shall be after the national conversion of the Jews, which shall be as life from the dead to the Gentiles, and the fulness of both Jews and Gentiles shall be come in, all the nation of the Jews, and all other nations, shall obtain mercy, and there shall be that general ingathering of the harvest of the whole earth, of which all that had been converted before, either of Jews or Gentiles, were but the first fruits. Thus it is meet, that the last kingdom which shall take place on earth, should be the kingdom of God’s own Son and heir, whose right it is to rule and reign; and that whatever revolutions and confusions there may be in the world, for a long time, the cause of truth, the righteous cause, shall finally prevail, and God’s holy people should at last inherit the earth, and reign on earth; and that the world should continue in tumults and great revolutions, following one another, from age to age, the world being as it were in travail, till truth and holiness are brought forth. It is meet, that all things should be shaken, till that comes which is true and right, and agreeable to the mind of God, which cannot be shaken; and that the wisdom of the Ruler of the world should be manifested in bringing all things ultimately to so good an issue. The world is made for the Son of God; his kingdom is the end of all changes, that come to pass in the state of the world. All are only to prepare the way for this; it is fit, therefore, that the last kingdom on earth should be his. It is wisely and mercifully ordered of God, that it should be so, on this account, as well as many others, viz. That the church of God, under all preceding changes, should have this consideration to encourage her, and maintain her hope, and animate her faith and prayers, from generation to generation, that God has promised, her cause should finally be maintained and prevail in the world.

text:
Supernatural tales of Colonial and Revolutionary America.

During the brutal winter of 1779–1780, George Washington’s Continental Army faced its most severe encampment at Jockey Hollow near Morristown, New Jersey, a trial that surpassed even the infamous hardships of Valley Forge. Soldiers endured relentless blizzards that piled snow into drifts as high as fifteen feet, while temperatures seldom rose above freezing. Starved of adequate food and clothing, weakened by disease, and demoralized by desertions, the troops constructed crude log huts that offered scant protection from the elements. Many perished from exposure, hunger, or illness, their suffering leaving an indelible mark on the landscape where a nearby cemetery still marks the graves of those who did not survive.

Long after the army departed, the woods and replica huts have drawn reports of lingering spirits whose presence is widely attributed to that extreme deprivation. Visitors and reenactors describe columns of colonial soldiers marching in silent lockstep through the trees, their forms fading among the trunks, while others hear the sudden, close strains of fife-and-drum music that cease as abruptly as they begin—sometimes heard by individuals when no instruments or other people are nearby. Shadowy figures dart around the reconstructed huts, particularly noticeable to those who stay overnight in the structures, and the trails are said to be walked by a translucent woman in a long white colonial dress who carries a glowing lantern, appearing more often in the quieter winter months. Additional accounts mention a spectral brown dog that materializes near the grounds before vanishing, and the area around Sugar Loaf Hill has earned the local nickname “Haunted Hill.” Many who experience these phenomena believe the tormented spirits remain bound to Jockey Hollow by the memory of the soldiers’ ordeal, making themselves known especially to those who honor the history of their sacrifice.

🇰🇵🇰🇷 Kim Jong Un wants his company commanders "fully ready for fighting a war", as the two Koreas argue over where their border is.

→ He said it Tuesday after a meeting of army company leaders, state media says.
→ Seoul says North Korean troops building border fortifications keep crossing the line, drawing warning shots.

So is this routine drill talk, or a border clash waiting to happen?

What Pyongyang says
→ He asked for "a radical improvement" in training. No target was named.
→ The North calls Seoul's mine finding "fabricated" after three South Korean soldiers were hurt on 21 Sept.

Why the line matters
→ A South Korean and UN probe blames North Korean mines. Many old border markers have rotted or vanished.
→ Seoul offered military talks to fix the line and reopen hotlines. The North has not accepted.

What the past says
→ In 2015 a mine blast brought artillery fire, then talks. Now the North calls the South hostile, so that exit is narrower.
→ In 1914 few planned the big war. Doubt about the other side's moves did the rest.

Kim's words read like drill rhetoric.
The danger is a patrol that cannot tell where the line is.

text:
INDEPENDENCE: THE EARLY YEARS

Uganda's approach to independence was unlike that of most other colonial territories where political parties had been organized to force self-rule or independence from a reluctant colonial regime. Whereas these conditions would have required local and regional differences to be subordinated to the greater goal of winning independence, in Uganda parties were forced to cooperate with one another, with the prospect of independence already assured. One of the major parties, KY, was even opposed to independence unless its particular separatist desires were met. The UPC-KY partnership represented a fragile alliance of two fragile parties.

In the UPC, leadership was factionalized. Each party functionary represented a local constituency, and most of the constituencies were ethnically distinct. For example, Obote's strength lay among his Langi kin in eastern Uganda; George Magezi represented the local interests of his Banyoro compatriots; Grace S.K. Ibingira's strength was in the Ankole kingdom; and Felix Onama was the northern leader of the largely neglected West Nile District in the northwest corner of Uganda. Each of these regional political bosses and those from the other Uganda regions expected to receive a ministerial post in the new Uganda government, to exercise patronage, and to bring the material fruits of independence to local supporters. Failing these objectives, each was likely either to withdraw from the UPC coalition or realign within it.

Moreover, the UPC had had no effective urban organization before independence, although it was able to mobilize the trade unions, most of which were led by non-Ugandan immigrant workers from Kenya (a situation which contributed to the independent Uganda government's almost immediate hostility toward the trade unions). No common ideology united the UPC, the composition of which ranged from the near reactionary Onama to the radical John Kakonge, leader of the UPC Youth League. As prime minister, Obote was responsible for keeping this loose coalition of divergent interest groups intact.

Obote also faced the task of maintaining the UPC's external alliances, primarily the coalition between the UPC and the kabaka, who led Buganda's KY. Obote proved adept at meeting the diverse demands of his many partners in government. He even temporarily acceded to some demands which he found repugnant, such as Buganda's claim for special treatment. This accession led to demands by other kingdoms for similar recognition. The Busoga chiefdoms banded together to claim that they, too, deserved recognition under the rule of their newly defined monarch, the kyabasinga. Not to be outdone, the Iteso people, who had never recognized a precolonial king, claimed the title kingoo for Teso District's political boss, Cuthbert Obwangor. Despite these separatist pressures, Obote's long-term goal was to build a strong central government at the expense of entrenched local interests, especially those of Buganda.

The first major challenge to the Obote government came not from the kingdoms, nor the regional interests, but from the military. In January 1964, units of the Ugandan Army mutinied, demanding higher pay and more rapid promotions. Minister of Defense Onama, who courageously went to speak to the mutineers, was seized and held hostage. Obote was forced to call in British troops to restore order, a humiliating blow to the new regime. In the aftermath, Obote's government acceded to all the mutineers' demands, unlike the governments of Kenya and Tanganyika, which responded to similar demands with increased discipline and tighter control over their small military forces.

The military then began to assume a more prominent role in Ugandan life. Obote selected a popular junior officer with minimal education, Idi Amin Dada, and promoted him rapidly through the ranks as a personal protégé. As the army expanded, it became a source of political patronage and of potential political power.

Later in 1964, Obote felt strong enough to address the critical issue of the "lost counties," which the British had conveniently postponed until after independence. The combination of patronage offers and the promise of future rewards within the ruling coalition gradually thinned opposition party ranks, as members of parliament "crossed the floor" to join the government benches. After two years of independence, Obote finally acquired enough votes to give the UPC a majority and free himself of the KY coalition. The turning point came when several DP members of parliament (MPs) from Bunyoro agreed to join the government side if Obote would undertake a popular referendum to restore the "lost counties" to Bunyoro. The kabaka, naturally, opposed the plebiscite. Unable to prevent it, he sent 300 armed Baganda veterans to the area to intimidate Banyoro voters. In turn, 2,000 veterans from Bunyoro massed on the frontier. Civil war was averted, and the referendum was held. The vote demonstrated an overwhelming desire by residents in the counties annexed to Buganda in 1900 to be restored to their historic Bunyoro allegiance, which was duly enacted by the new UPC majority despite KY opposition.

This triumph for Obote and the UPC strengthened the central government and threw Buganda into disarray. KY unity was weakened by internal recriminations, after which some KY stalwarts, too, began to "cross the floor" to join Obote's victorious government. By early 1966, the result was a parliament composed of seventy- four UPC, nine DP, eight KY, and one independent MP. Obote's efforts to produce a one-party state with a powerful executive prime minister appeared to be on the verge of success.

Paradoxically, however, as the perceived threat from Buganda diminished, many non-Baganda alliances weakened. And as the possibility of an opposition DP victory faded, the UPC coalition itself began to come apart. The one-party state did not signal the end of political conflict, however; it merely relocated and intensified that conflict within the party. The issue that brought the UPC disharmony to a crisis involved Obote's military protégé, Idi Amin.

In 1966 Amin caused a commotion when he walked into a Kampala bank with a gold bar (bearing the stamp of the government of the Belgian Congo) and asked the bank manager to exchange it for cash. Amin's account was ultimately credited with a deposit of £17,000. Obote rivals questioned the incident, and it emerged that the prime minister and a handful of close associates had used Colonel Amin and units of the Uganda Army to intervene in the neighboring Congo crisis. Former supporters of Congolese leader Patrice Lumumba, led by a "General Olenga," opposed the American-backed government and were attempting to lead the Eastern Province into secession. These troops were reported to be trading looted ivory and gold for arms supplies secretly smuggled to them by Amin. The arrangement became public when Olenga later claimed that he failed to receive the promised munitions. This claim appeared to be supported by the fact that in mid-1965, a seventy-five-ton shipment of Chinese weapons was intercepted by the Kenyan government as it was being moved from Tanzania to Uganda.

Obote's rivals for leadership within the UPC, supported by some Baganda politicians and others who were hostile to Obote, used the evidence revealed by Amin's casual bank deposit to claim that the prime minister and his closest associates were corrupt and had conducted secret foreign policy for personal gain, in the amount of £25,000 each. Obote denied the charge and said the money had been spent to buy the munitions for Olenga's Congolese troops. On February 4, 1966, while Obote was away on a trip to the north of the country, an effective "no confidence" vote against Obote was passed by the UPC Mps. This attempt to remove Obote appeared to be organized by UPC Secretary General Grace S.K. Ibingira, closely supported by the UPC leader from Bunyoro, George Magezi, and a number of other southern UPC notables. Only the radical UPC member, John Kakonge, voted against the motion.

Because he was faced with a nearly unanimous disavowal by his governing party and national parliament, many people expected Obote to resign. Instead, Obote turned to Idi Amin and the army, and, in effect, carried out a coup d'état against his own government in order to stay in power. Obote suspended the constitution, arrested the offending UPC ministers, and assumed control of the state. He forced a new constitution through parliament without a reading and without the necessary quorum. That constitution abolished the federal powers of the kingdoms, most notably the internal autonomy enjoyed by Buganda, and concentrated presidential powers in the prime minister's office. The kabaka objected, and Buganda prepared to wage a legal battle. Baganda leaders rhetorically demanded that Obote's "illegal" government remove itself from Buganda soil.

Buganda, however, once again miscalculated, for Obote was not interested in negotiating. Instead, he sent Idi Amin and loyal troops to attack the kabaka's palace on nearby Mengo Hill. The palace was defended by a small group of bodyguards armed with rifles and shotguns. Amin's troops had heavy weapons but were reluctant to press the attack until Obote became impatient and demanded results. By the time the palace was overrun, the kabaka had taken advantage of a cloudburst to exit over the rear wall. He hailed a passing taxi and was driven off to exile. After the assault, Obote was reasonably secure from open opposition. The new republican 1967 constitution abolished the kingdoms altogether. Buganda was divided into four districts and ruled through martial law, a forerunner of the military domination over the civilian population that all of Uganda would experience after 1971.

Obote's success in the face of adversity reclaimed for him the support of most members of the UPC, which then became the only legal political party. The original independence election of 1962, therefore, was the last one held in Uganda until December 1980. On the homefront, Obote issued the "Common Man's Charter," echoed the call for African Socialism by Tanzanian President Julius Nyerere, and proclaimed a "move to the left" to signal new efforts to consolidate power. His critics noted, however, that he placed most control over economic nationalization in the hands of an Asian millionaire who was also a financial backer of the UPC. Obote created a system of secret police, the General Service Unit (GSU). Headed by a relative, Akena Adoko, the GSU reported on suspected subversives. The Special Force Units of paramilitary police, heavily recruited from Obote's own region and ethnic group, supplemented the security forces within the army and police.

Although Buganda had been defeated and occupied by the military, Obote was still concerned about security there. His concerns were well founded; in December 1969 he was wounded in an assassination attempt and narrowly escaped more serious injury when a grenade thrown near him failed to explode. He had retained power by relying on Idi Amin and the army, but it was not clear that he could continue to count on their loyalty.

Obote appeared particularly uncertain of the army after Amin's sole rival among senior army officers, Brigadier Acap Okoya, was murdered early in 1970. (Amin later promoted the man rumored to have recruited Okoya's killers.) A second attempt was made on Obote's life when his motorcade was ambushed later that year, but the vice-president's car was mistakenly riddled with bullets. Obote began to recruit more Acholi and Langi troops, and he accelerated their promotions to counter the large numbers of soldiers from Amin's home, which was then known as West Nile District. Obote also enlarged the paramilitary Special Force as a counterweight to the army.

Amin, who at times inspected his troops wearing an outsized sport shirt with Obote's face across the front and back, protested his loyalty. But in October 1970, Amin was placed under temporary house arrest while investigators looked into his army expenditures, reportedly several million dollars over budget. Another charge against Amin was that he had continued to aid southern Sudan's Anya Nya rebels in opposing the regime of Jafaar Numayri even after Obote had shifted his support away from the Anyanya to Numayri. This foreign policy shift provoked an outcry from Israel, which had been supplying the Anyanya rebels. Amin was close friends with several Israeli military advisers who were in Uganda to help train the Ugandan Army, and their eventual role in Amin's efforts to oust Obote remained the subject of continuing controversy.

Russia Expands War Recruitment in Africa as Burundian Enlistment Rises 23-Fold

NAIROBI, Kenya (Somali Report) - Russia has sharply expanded recruitment of African citizens for its war against Ukraine, shifting its focus towards countries including Burundi and Zimbabwe after facing resistance from authorities in Kenya and South Africa, according to The Insider, citing Bloomberg and Ukrainian intelligence data.

Between January and September 2026, 699 Burundian citizens signed contracts with Russia’s Ministry of Defense, compared with 30 throughout 2025. In Zimbabwe, recruitment rose from 65 in 2025 to 530 during the first nine months of 2026.

Russia recruited 1,229 citizens from the two countries during the nine-month period, compared with 95 throughout 2025. Madagascar has also emerged as a source of recruits as its military officials expand cooperation with Moscow.

Ukrainian intelligence assesses that Russia is seeking foreign recruits to compensate for battlefield losses and personnel shortages. The report said Russia had largely stopped military recruitment in at least nine countries where authorities resisted, instead offering citizens jobs at Russian defense enterprises.

Kenya Seeks Return of Recruited Citizens

Kenya has raised concerns about its citizens joining the Russian military. In February 2026, the National Intelligence Service reported that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited into the Russian army.

Foreign Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi travelled to Moscow to demand an end to recruitment. The Kenyan government later said Russia had agreed to add Kenya to a list of countries whose citizens should no longer be accepted for military service.

In early October, Mudavadi told Parliament that authorities had information about 354 Kenyans involved in the war. Of these, 84 were believed to have been killed or gone missing.

Mudavadi travelled to Moscow on October 26 for the Russia-Africa summit scheduled for October 28–30, with recruitment remaining an issue in bilateral relations.

Zimbabwe Investigates Recruiters

Zimbabwe confirmed in March that 15 citizens recruited to fight in the war had died and said it was seeking the return of another 66. Authorities have investigated alleged recruiters, including Russian nationals accused of luring people with civilian job offers before involving them in military recruitment.

Ukraine Reports Thousands of African Recruits

Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War reported that approximately 45,900 foreign nationals and residents of unrecognized territories had signed contracts with the Russian army by October 1, 2026. About 5,400 came from 43 African countries, representing approximately 12 percent of the identified foreign contract soldiers.

Ukrainian data indicated that Russia recruited 16,200 foreigners during the first nine months of 2026, exceeding the 16,000 recorded throughout 2025.

Russia denies allegations of illegal recruitment. Its embassy in Kenya has said foreign citizens can voluntarily join its armed forces, while the Kremlin has rejected claims that it faces a shortage of contract soldiers requiring another mass mobilization.

text:
Who Could Be World Liberty Financial’s Next Enterprise Partners?

At TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026, WLFI CEO Zach Witkoff said the company plans to provide payment technology to large Web2 businesses, citing payouts to drivers, contractors, and creators. Although no partners were named, these examples reveal potential markets for USD1.

1. Mobility and Delivery Platforms

Uber, Lyft, and DoorDash manage large networks of drivers requiring recurring payouts. USD1 could offer an alternative settlement method, particularly for cross-border payments. Adoption, however, would depend on costs, compliance, local infrastructure, and recipient demand.

2. Global Contractor Platforms

Deel, Upwork, and Fiverr facilitate payments between businesses and workers across borders. Stablecoins could reduce settlement friction and provide dollar-denominated balances. Yet this market is already competitive, with established payment providers exploring stablecoin-based payouts.

3. Creator Economy Platforms

YouTube, TikTok, Patreon, and Meta distribute earnings to creators worldwide. USD1 could potentially serve as an additional payout option, although regulatory compliance, tax reporting, conversion costs, and user preferences remain important barriers.

4. The Infrastructure Opportunity

WLFI may not need direct agreements with household-name platforms. Integrating with payment providers that already serve multiple businesses could deliver broader distribution through fewer partnerships. This approach would align with the strategic rationale behind the Mesh collaboration.

Investment Implications

The underlying ambition is to shift USD1 from exchange-driven circulation toward recurring economic activity.

Exchange listings and incentives can expand distribution, while enterprise payouts could generate repeat demand tied to real business operations.

Three distinctions remain critical:

- Potential customers are not confirmed partners. No evidence in the remarks identifies these companies as WLFI counterparties.
- Payment volume is not revenue. Profitability depends on fees, costs, and contractual revenue sharing.
- USD1 adoption is not WLFI token value accrual. Token holders benefit only if a demonstrable economic mechanism connects business performance to the token.

The decisive evidence will be named customers, executed contracts, actual payout volumes, commercial launch dates, and disclosed revenue economics.

Conclusion: WLFI appears to be pursuing enterprise payments as a new distribution channel for USD1. Uber, Deel, and YouTube illustrate relevant customer categories, not confirmed partners. The investment case ultimately depends on execution, recurring transaction demand, and whether the resulting economic value reaches WLFI token holders.

text:
First, you’re making a fundamental mistake when reading Scripture: You’re assuming that because the Bible records something, God approves of it.

Let’s address your objections individually.

1. The “vengeful” God versus Jesus

Who told you the God of the Old Testament is different from Jesus? Jesus Himself speaks about divine judgment (Matthew 25:46), and the Old Testament repeatedly describes God as merciful, gracious, and slow to anger (Exodus 34:6).

Does God not have authority to judge his creation?

God’s justice and His mercy are not contradictions. They’re both aspects of His character.

2. Blood sacrifices

The sacrifices were never about God enjoying bloodshed. They demonstrated the seriousness of sin and pointed toward the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ.

Hebrews 10:4 explicitly says that the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. Jesus willingly offered Himself as the final sacrifice (Hebrews 10:10–14).

3. Slavery and beating slaves

There is no approval of chattel slavery in the Bible. There were different forms of servitude, including debt servitude, which were consensual.

Exodus 21:16 condemns kidnapping and selling people. Exodus 21:26–27 provides freedom for servants who are abused.

There were clear boundaries on how a servant was to be treated.

4. Lot’s daughters

It’s important to understand the difference between descriptive and prescriptive.

Genesis 19:30–38 records Lot’s daughters getting their father drunk and having intercourse with him without his informed consent.

Where does God command this? Where does He tell anyone it’s perfectly fine to do this?

Nowhere.

Finally, if you want to understand how Jesus relates to the Old Testament, remember John 5:39, where Jesus teaches that the Scriptures testify about Him.

Jesus confirms the Old Testament.

You cannot separate Jesus from the Old Testament simply because you encounter passages you don’t understand that make you uncomfortable.

Kassapa Thero went to Kingsbury specifically for treatment. The 'CCTV footage of nurses arriving' has not been released. 

During a Satyagraha held at Viharamahadevi Park in Colombo, requesting the release of Venerable Galagodaaththe Gnanasara Thero, who is imprisoned, a certain video that stirred up social media recently circulated. It showed Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thero arriving at the Kingsbury Hotel in Colombo.
A group of laypeople, including former Minister Sarath Weerasekara, were also present, and this video of a Buddhist monk arriving at a luxury hotel managed to create a strong discussion within society.

To clarify the facts regarding this controversial incident, a group of monks who participated in the Satyagraha called a press conference in Colombo today. Speaking there, Venerable Thabbowa Hemarathana Thero revealed that the real story behind the video clip exposed to society takes a completely different turn.

According to his explanation, during the Satyagraha, Balangoda Kassapa Thero became severely ill. Suffering from a severe fever, he conducted the Dhamma sermon with his head covered by a shawl offered by a female devotee to ward off the cold. Although Thabbowa Hemarathana Thero suggested that he take medicine, have a warm bath, and go to a place where he could rest, Kassapa Thero initially refused. It was also revealed that at that time, no temple had yet extended an invitation for the monks participating in the Satyagraha to rest or bathe.

As Kassapa Thero's condition worsened, the other monks became very afraid to take him to a hospital. Given the prevailing public opinion and the risky atmosphere at the time, they suspected that Kassapa Thero's life could be in danger if he went to a hospital. Therefore, the monks decided to go to a safe place prepared by the devotees.

Thabbowa Hemarathana Thero stated that he and Venerable Chandakiththi Thero also accompanied Kassapa Thero to that location. However, he emphasized that they did not know it was the Kingsbury Hotel until they arrived. Hemarathana Thero said that Kassapa Thero was trembling with his head covered by a shawl when arriving at the hotel due to a severe fever, and as soon as they arrived, a group including a devotee named Lionel, arranged for doctors to come to the hotel and provide treatment.

However, only the scenes of him arriving at the hotel while ill were circulated on social media. No footage showing doctors and nurses rushing to the hotel to provide treatment was released to the media. text:
The Bridge and the Throne: Where Jesus Fits When We Pray

When videos start dividing the world into rigid categories—labeling billions of people "idol worshippers" because they don't fit a narrow, localized legal definition—it usually comes from looking at faith through the lens of institutional gatekeeping rather than biblical design.

A common question that surfaces in these debates is: If we pray to God, where does Jesus Christ actually come in?

To understand how this works, we have to look at the ancient architectural pattern of the Bible, specifically the concept of the High Priest.

1. The Creator is Always the Destination
In genuine prayer, the ultimate destination is always the Creator—God the Father. Believers are not praying to Jesus as a second, separate deity; rather, prayer is directed upward to the source of all life.

2. The Function of a Priest is to Bridge the Gap
In the Biblical Scriptures, an ordinary person could not simply waltz into the Holy of Holies. They brought their offering to the priest, and the priest stood in the gap—representing the people, maintaining the altar, and keeping the path open.
The problem with the ancient Levitical system was that it was temporary. It was tied to a physical building in Jerusalem, a specific piece of land, and mortal men who eventually died.

3. Jesus as the Permanent, Landless High Priest
The New Testament introduces Jesus not as a rival to God, but as the ultimate, permanent High Priest of an older, universal order.
Because his priesthood is not bound to a physical piece of real estate or a local earthly temple, it is entirely borderless. He serves as the eternal mediator who took on human flesh, lived our experience, and offered the final, definitive sacrifice.

4. Praying "In His Name"
This is why New Testament prayers are directed to the Father, but offered through or in the name of Jesus. It isn't a magical incantation; it is a statement of legal and spiritual standing.
You don't barge into a king's throne room uninvited. You enter under the authority and sponsorship of the designated royal representative. Jesus explicitly stated, "No one comes to the Father except through me." In plain terms, he is the functioning High Priest who keeps the bridge open between the Creator and the seventy nations of the earth. He handles the incense, represents humanity, and ensures our prayer reaches the throne room.

The Bottom Line
When billions of people from every culture and language direct their faith toward the Creator through the appointed mediator, they aren't engaging in foreign idolatry. They are stepping onto the exact bridge that was designed from the beginning—a permanent, open pathway for all the families of the earth to draw near to God.

The Bridge and the Throne: Where Jesus Fits When We Pray

When videos start dividing the world into rigid categories—labeling billions of people "idol worshippers" because they don't fit a narrow, localized legal definition—it usually comes from looking at faith through the lens of institutional gatekeeping rather than biblical design.

A common question that surfaces in these debates is: If we pray to God, where does Jesus Christ actually come in?

To understand how this works, we have to look at the ancient architectural pattern of the Bible, specifically the concept of the High Priest.

1. The Creator is Always the Destination
In genuine prayer, the ultimate destination is always the Creator—God the Father. Believers are not praying to Jesus as a second, separate deity; rather, prayer is directed upward to the source of all life.

2. The Function of a Priest is to Bridge the Gap
In the Biblical Scriptures, an ordinary person could not simply waltz into the Holy of Holies. They brought their offering to the priest, and the priest stood in the gap—representing the people, maintaining the altar, and keeping the path open.
The problem with the ancient Levitical system was that it was temporary. It was tied to a physical building in Jerusalem, a specific piece of land, and mortal men who eventually died.

3. Jesus as the Permanent, Landless High Priest
The New Testament introduces Jesus not as a rival to God, but as the ultimate, permanent High Priest of an older, universal order.
Because his priesthood is not bound to a physical piece of real estate or a local earthly temple, it is entirely borderless. He serves as the eternal mediator who took on human flesh, lived our experience, and offered the final, definitive sacrifice.

4. Praying "In His Name"
This is why New Testament prayers are directed to the Father, but offered through or in the name of Jesus. It isn't a magical incantation; it is a statement of legal and spiritual standing.
You don't barge into a king's throne room uninvited. You enter under the authority and sponsorship of the designated royal representative. Jesus explicitly stated, "No one comes to the Father except through me." In plain terms, he is the functioning High Priest who keeps the bridge open between the Creator and the seventy nations of the earth. He handles the incense, represents humanity, and ensures our prayer reaches the throne room.

The Bottom Line
When billions of people from every culture and language direct their faith toward the Creator through the appointed mediator, they aren't engaging in foreign idolatry. They are stepping onto the exact bridge that was designed from the beginning—a permanent, open pathway for all the families of the earth to draw near to God.
