text:
Airbnb’s founders tried to sell 10% of the company for $150,000

Investors passed. Some didn’t even reply to the email

So they started selling breakfast cereal for $40 a box

Brian Chesky told the story at Stanford. In October 2007, he quit his job as an industrial designer in LA, rolled an old foam mattress into the back seat of a Honda Civic and drove to San Francisco with $1,000 in the bank. His co-founder Joe Gebbia told him the rent was $1,150

That weekend a design conference came to town and every hotel was sold out. Joe had three air beds left over from camping. They inflated them and called it the Air Bed and Breakfast

A year later, they were still trying to raise money. They were introduced to about 15 angel investors. Roughly half never replied. Of the rest, some said it didn’t fit their thesis, some said the market wasn’t big enough, and one said he just wasn’t excited about travel as a category. Everyone passed

The low point was a meeting with an investor on the day they launched on TechCrunch. Chesky was so cocky he didn’t bring a deck. He typed in the website. It didn’t work. He sat there for about an hour trying to explain the idea

By then he was about $30,000 in credit card debt. He kept the cards in a baseball card binder and kept applying for new ones until the banks stopped giving them to him. Joe did the same

So at midnight, broke and desperate, they had an idea. The air beds weren’t working. Maybe they could sell breakfast

They made presidential-themed cereal for the 2008 election: Obama O’s, The Breakfast of Change, and Cap’n McCain’s, A Maverick in Every Bite. General Mills wasn’t interested. A printer agreed to make 1,000 boxes for free in exchange for a royalty, but they arrived as flat cardboard. The founders folded and glued every one by hand, numbered them as limited editions and sold them for $40 a box

They made about $30,000. That’s how they funded the company

Even then, almost nobody believed. A mentor told Chesky he hoped this wasn’t the only idea he was working on. His mom offered to send him money so he wouldn’t have to let strangers stay in his home

Then they interviewed at Y Combinator. Paul Graham thought the idea was terrible. His first question was whether people were actually doing this. His second was what was wrong with them. At the end, Joe handed him a box of Obama O’s

Graham’s verdict: if you can convince people to pay $40 for a $4 box of cereal, maybe you can get strangers to stay in other strangers’ homes. He also called them cockroaches, the only kind of company that survives an investment nuclear winter. Chesky called his mom: I’m a cockroach, I got in

A few months later, Sequoia invested $600,000

The investors who passed were looking at the idea

Paul Graham was looking at the founders

Would you have bought 10% of Airbnb for $150,000?

text:
Connecting innovation with investment is key to unlocking Africa’s next economy.

At the official opening of Africa Tech-Xpo 2026, Laurent Rudasingwa @lrudasingwa, Acting Resident Representative of the United Nations Development Programme - @UNDP in Zambia (@UNDPZambia), highlighting the role of technology in driving inclusive economic growth and sustainable development.

Speaking under the theme Innovation, Infrastructure and Africa’s Next Economy, the address emphasised that technology must translate into real opportunities for businesses, innovators and communities.

UNDP highlighted its three-year partnership with @techtrends_zm and welcomed the evolution of Zambia Tech-Xpo into Africa Tech-Xpo, creating a platform to connect local talent and enterprise with opportunities across the continent.

The address showcased UNDP’s work to strengthen Zambia’s innovation ecosystem through the @timbuktooafrica initiative. At Copperbelt University, the Mukuba UniPod has supported more than 300 innovators since 2024, while the timbuktoo MineTech Hub is connecting startups with opportunities to develop solutions for the mining sector.

Artificial intelligence also featured prominently, particularly efforts to strengthen local AI capabilities and access to computing infrastructure through the University of Zambia’s AI UniPod and the timbuktoo EDGE initiative.

Another example is the planned collaboration with Lusaka Water Supply and Sanitation Company to explore how AI can help identify water losses, metering challenges and billing gaps, potentially improving operational efficiency and investment decisions.

The address further called for deliberate action to increase women’s participation in the digital economy through access to technical training, mentorship, finance, computing resources and procurement opportunities.

For the private sector, investors and development partners, the call was to move beyond conversations and create practical partnerships that connect innovators to markets, provide startups with opportunities to test their solutions, and mobilise financing for businesses ready to scale.

Africa’s next economy will be shaped by how effectively the continent turns technological capability into economic opportunity.

Through collaboration between government, industry, universities, investors and development partners, Africa Tech-Xpo 2026 offers an opportunity to turn that ambition into measurable progress.

text:
India's biggest IPO ever just made its debut. Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital arm of Reliance backed by $META and $GOOGL, closed its first day up about 27% and is now India's second most valuable company. Here's what happened, in plain English.

The numbers
• Raise: 270M new shares at ₹1,119 each, about ₹30,188 crore, or roughly $3.2B (final prospectus, Reuters). It's the largest IPO in India's history.
• Demand: the offer was subscribed more than 22 times. Big institutions bid for about 70.6x their share, retail investors about 2.7x (BSE data via CNBC).
• Day one: shares closed at ₹1,417.50, up about 26.7% from the offer price, after rising as much as 27.3% (Reuters).
• Valuation: about $137B at the close, behind only its parent Reliance Industries (Reuters).

The business
• FY2026 revenue (year to March 31): ₹1,46,885 crore, up about 14.6% from ₹1,28,218 crore the year before
• FY2026 profit: ₹30,049 crore, up about 15.1%, so unlike many big tech IPOs, this one is already profitable
• EBITDA margin: 51.9%
• More than 530 million telecom customers (Reuters)
(Company financial statements and prospectus.)

Where the money goes
All of the shares were new, so the cash goes to the company, not to selling shareholders. Jio plans to use up to about $2.89B of it to pay down borrowings at its telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm (Reuters).

Two terms worth learning
1. Oversubscription: when investors ask for more shares than are on offer. 22x means bids for about 22 shares for every one available, so many bidders got only part of what they asked for, or nothing.
2. Listing pop: the gap between the IPO price and where the stock trades on day one. A big pop shows strong demand, but it also means the company left money on the table by pricing lower than buyers were willing to pay.

What to watch
• Index inclusion: CNBC notes Jio's size could get it added to benchmarks like the Nifty 50 and MSCI indexes, which brings in index-fund buying
• Some investors who bought stakes around 2021 may look to sell in about six months, one analyst told CNBC
• Risks flagged by brokerages: competition, heavy capital spending and changes to India's telecom rules on spectrum, licensing and fees (Reuters)

Sources: Jio Platforms prospectus and financial statements, NSE, Reuters, CNBC.

I like Jason's idea of selling something relatively inert, like BITCOIN (or maybe gold), to invest in a high-risk venture that could offer, as he puts it, “much benefit to humanity.”

The issue with his perspective is that it's not and never will be in everyone’s best interest to put all their money into some newfangled tech venture like AI.

Most people need liquidity and reliability, which is why they need to hold CASH.

But cash has problems: money printing and inflation erode purchasing power. This is why wealthy and savvy people buy bonds. These remain relatively liquid while earning a yield to offset inflation. Smart.

But what about people who don’t want to prop up a banking system they see as corrupt? And/or who want to avoid systemic risk? (See 2008, 1929, etc.)

This brings us first to precious metals. Gold and silver are non-sovereign stores of value that are relatively liquid, but unfortunately not particularly well-suited to our needs in the digital age.

Enter Bitcoin: the one and only scarce, digitally native asset with global liquidity that exists outside the traditional banking system. This role rests on those properties, not on viral memes or narrative momentum.

Bitcoin also has a low enough correlation with the stock market that it provides some protection against risk there as well. A compelling option for the billions of people who want to save up their shekels over time while carefully considering how to deploy their capital, instead of going full YOLO FOMO into AI like the VC class wants them to.

Bitcoin is the greatest globally accessible alternative to cash and stocks. Will it ever hit its ATH again? So long as they keep printing money, it's only a matter of time before it hits $1,000,000.

text:
The photograph of a coal miner's wife and her three children, taken in September 1938 in Pursglove, Scotts Run, West Virginia, offers a poignant glimpse into the lives of families living in coal mining communities during the Great Depression.

Pursglove, a small unincorporated community in West Virginia, was deeply affected by the coal mining industry, which dominated the local economy and shaped the everyday lives of its residents. The company houses, where miners and their families lived, were often basic and stark, reflecting the harsh working conditions and economic challenges faced by these communities.

The image from 1938 captures a moment of familial connection and resilience amidst these difficult circumstances. The coal miner's wife, alongside her children, stands in front of their modest home, likely one provided by the coal company as part of their employment package. These houses were typically simple and functional, built to accommodate the influx of workers drawn to the area by the promise of steady employment in the mines.

The Great Depression had a profound impact on coal mining towns, with widespread economic hardship and limited access to resources and support. Despite the challenging conditions, the coal miner’s family in the photograph exemplifies the strength and solidarity found within these tight-knit communities. The presence of the children highlights the hope for future generations, even in the face of economic adversity.

Coal mining was a grueling occupation, characterized by long hours, dangerous working conditions, and minimal pay. Families often faced difficult living conditions, with limited access to amenities and healthcare. The photograph underscores the stark contrast between the harsh realities of coal mining life and the resilience of those who endured it.

In the context of the era, this photograph is not just a snapshot of daily life but a powerful testament to the human spirit and the challenges faced by working-class families in America. It reflects broader themes of struggle and perseverance during a time of economic and social upheaval.

Today, such photographs are invaluable for understanding the history and heritage of coal mining communities, providing insight into the lived experiences of those who contributed significantly to the industrial growth of the United States while facing tremendous personal and economic challenges

This system identifies substantial favorites facing opponents with winning percentages of at least 60%.

Approximately 72% of Action Network tickets support Detroit.

The public backing and rest disadvantage introduce legitimate concerns.

Nevertheless, the historical system's substantial sample and positive return provide a compelling statistical argument.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Charlotte's 3-1 record is impressive, but the Hornets are missing several established contributors and have relied heavily on Miller's extraordinary scoring.

Detroit's ability to contain Miller and avoid a substantial rebounding disadvantage will be critical.

The historical system, Detroit's potential defensive matchup against Charlotte's leading scorer and the Hornets' depleted rotation provide the foundation for this selection.

NBA FREE PICK #2

PHILADELPHIA 76ERS–INDIANA PACERS OVER 236.5 — 7:00 ET

HISTORICAL SYSTEM: 1,953-1,543-127 OVER (55.9%), +6.6% ROI

A historically profitable NBA mathematical totals system identifies Philadelphia–Indiana as an OVER opportunity Wednesday.

THE MATHEMATICAL ADVANTAGE

The system evaluates the relationship between recent offensive and defensive scoring averages and the posted total, focusing on home games where the combined scoring environment meets specific mathematical conditions.

It excludes several situations involving unusually strong recent scoring margins, significant downward total adjustments and other circumstances that have historically produced less favorable OVER results.

The underlying premise is that short-term scoring patterns can create misleading expectations about a matchup's actual offensive potential.

Since 2012, the system has produced 1,953 OVERS against 1,543 UNDERS, with 127 pushes.

Tyrese Haliburton remains central to Indiana's ability to generate efficient scoring opportunities.

Against Milwaukee on Monday, Haliburton scored 22 points and distributed nine assists.

Pascal Siakam added 20 points, 13 rebounds and six assists.

The combination gives Indiana two established offensive organizers capable of creating opportunities for teammates.

However, the Pacers face significant backcourt uncertainty.

Haliburton is questionable with hamstring soreness.

Andrew Nembhard is questionable with neck discomfort.

T.J. McConnell remains out with a hamstring strain.

The availability of Haliburton and Nembhard is especially important because Indiana must generate sufficient offense to support a total approaching 237 points.

If both are available, the Pacers possess the ballhandling and offensive creativity necessary to challenge Philadelphia's defense.

DECEPTIVE BOX SCORE

Indiana lost 110-102 against Milwaukee, but the final score conceals substantial differences between the two halves.

The Pacers led 61-50 at halftime.

However, Milwaukee outscored Indiana 60-41 after intermission.

The Pacers managed only 17 fourth-quarter points.

Indiana's offensive collapse transformed a game that began with considerable scoring into a relatively modest final total of 212.

The result illustrates both the Pacers' offensive capabilities and their vulnerability when execution deteriorates.

PHILADELPHIA'S REST ADVANTAGE

Philadelphia last played Sunday.

Indiana last played Monday.

The 76ers therefore have one additional day of rest.

MARKET ANALYSIS

The total opened at approximately 237.5, while the updated system database identifies 236.5.

The spread has moved substantially toward Philadelphia, from an opening -1.5 to approximately -5.5.

That adjustment reflects a significant reassessment of the matchup, with Indiana's personnel uncertainty an important consideration.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Philadelphia's offensive personnel create favorable matchups against Indiana's depleted interior rotation.

Embiid's anticipated return adds an important scoring option, while Maxey provides explosive perimeter offense.

Indiana has enough offensive talent to contribute substantially, particularly through Haliburton and Siakam.

With Indiana's principal offensive creators available, the combination of Philadelphia's scoring advantages and the historically profitable mathematical system supports the OVER.

🇨🇳 曾经偷偷熬夜看的小说 TOP10
🇯🇵 こっそり夜更かしして読んだ小説 TOP10
🇰🇷 몰래 밤을 새워 읽었던 소설 TOP10
🇻🇳 TOP10 cuốn tiểu thuyết từng lén thức khuya để đọc
🇺🇸 Novels We Secretly Stayed Up Late to Read: TOP 10
以下是小说主题的创意怀旧盘点，并非调查排名。作品横跨不同年代，书名在不同地区可能有不同译法。
🇨🇳 中国
嘴上说着“再看一章就睡”，回过神来，窗外的天已经快亮了。
《哈利·波特》系列｜『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズ｜《해리 포터》 시리즈｜Harry Potter｜Harry Potter series
每翻过一页，都想知道哈利和朋友们接下来会遇到什么。

《盗墓笔记》｜『盗墓筆記』｜《도묘필기》｜Đạo Mộ Bút Ký｜The Grave Robbers’ Chronicles
越是黑灯瞎火越不敢看，可看到悬念处又舍不得合上书。

《鬼吹灯》｜『鬼吹灯』｜《귀취등》｜Ma Thổi Đèn｜Ghost Blows Out the Light
手电照着书页，越往下读，越觉得房间里安静得有点吓人。

《斗破苍穹》｜『斗破蒼穹』｜《투파창궁》｜Đấu Phá Thương Khung｜Battle Through the Heavens
眼看主角又要迎来一场对决，总觉得再看一点就能等到结果。

《诛仙》｜『誅仙』｜《주선》｜Tru Tiên｜Zhu Xian
跟着张小凡走进仙侠世界，读完一章又忍不住翻下一章。
《射雕英雄传》｜『射鵰英雄伝』｜《사조영웅전》｜Anh Hùng Xạ Điêu｜The Legend of the Condor Heroes
郭靖的江湖故事一展开，连睡前定好的时间都忘了。
《三体》｜『三体』｜《삼체》｜Tam Thể｜The Three-Body Problem
一个问题刚有答案，新的谜团又让人想继续读下去。
《第一次的亲密接触》｜『第一次の親密接触』｜《첫 번째 친밀한 접촉》｜Lần Đầu Tiếp Xúc Thân Mật｜The First Intimate Contact
在那个网络故事让人着迷的年代，屏幕前的一段感情也能让人读到很晚。
《那些年，我们一起追的女孩》｜『あの頃、君を追いかけた』｜《그 시절, 우리가 좋아했던 소녀》｜Cô Gái Năm Ấy Chúng Ta Cùng Theo Đuổi｜You Are the Apple of My Eye
读着校园里的喜欢和遗憾，不知不觉也想起了自己的同桌。
《撒哈拉的故事》｜『サハラの物語』｜《사하라 이야기》｜Câu Chuyện Sahara｜Stories of the Sahara
跟着三毛走进另一种生活，合上书前还想再读一个故事。
🇯🇵 日本
布団に入ってからも続きが気になり、少しだけ読むつもりが夜更けになっていました。
『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズ｜《哈利·波特》系列｜《해리 포터》 시리즈｜Harry Potter｜Harry Potter series
魔法学校の次の冒険が気になり、ページをめくる手が止まりませんでした。
『バッテリー』｜《野球少年》｜《배터리》｜Battery｜Battery
巧と豪の関係を追いながら、二人の次の試合を待ちました。
『十二国記』シリーズ｜《十二国记》系列｜《십이국기》 시리즈｜Mười Hai Nước｜The Twelve Kingdoms series
異世界の地図を思い浮かべながら、物語の続きに入り込みました。
『ソードアート・オンライン』｜《刀剑神域》｜《소드 아트 온라인》｜Sword Art Online｜Sword Art Online
ゲームの世界からどうなるのか気になり、区切りを決められませんでした。
『涼宮ハルヒの憂鬱』｜《凉宫春日的忧郁》｜《스즈미야 하루히의 우울》｜Nỗi Buồn Của Haruhi Suzumiya｜The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya
いつもの学校で始まる不思議な出来事に、夜中まで付き合いました。
『キノの旅』｜《奇诺之旅》｜《키노의 여행》｜Hành Trình Của Kino｜Kino’s Journey
次に訪れる国はどんな場所だろうと、一話ずつ読み進めました。
『告白』｜《告白》｜《고백》｜Lời Thú Tội｜Confessions
語り手が変わるたびに見え方が変わり、続きを確かめたくなりました。
『白夜行』｜《白夜行》｜《백야행》｜Bạch Dạ Hành｜Journey Under the Midnight Sun
長い物語の中で少しずつつながる謎が気になりました。
『容疑者Xの献身』｜《嫌疑人X的献身》｜《용의자 X의 헌신》｜Phía Sau Nghi Can X｜The Devotion of Suspect X
事件の真相だけでなく、登場人物の思いも知りたくなりました。
『君の膵臓をたべたい』｜《我想吃掉你的胰脏》｜《너의 췌장을 먹고 싶어》｜Tớ Muốn Ăn Tụy Của Cậu｜I Want to Eat Your Pancreas
二人の時間がどう続いていくのか、静かに読みふけりました。
🇰🇷 한국
불을 끄고 누운 뒤에도 이야기가 머릿속에 남아, 다음 장만 읽자며 책을 다시 펼쳤습니다.

《해리 포터》 시리즈｜《哈利·波特》系列｜『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズ｜Harry Potter｜Harry Potter series
마법 학교에서 무슨 일이 벌어질지 궁금해 책장을 계속 넘겼습니다.

《퇴마록》｜《退魔录》｜『退魔録』｜Trừ Ma Lục｜The Soul Guardians
무서워서 이불을 꼭 잡으면서도 다음 이야기를 읽고 싶었습니다.

《드래곤 라자》｜《龙族》｜『ドラゴンラージャ』｜Dragon Raja｜Dragon Raja
낯선 세계와 모험을 따라가다 보면 시간이 훌쩍 지나 있었습니다.
《반지의 제왕》｜《指环王》｜『指輪物語』｜Chúa Tể Những Chiếc Nhẫn｜The Lord of the Rings
긴 여정의 다음 목적지가 궁금해 밤늦게까지 읽었습니다.
《나니아 연대기》｜《纳尼亚传奇》｜『ナルニア国物語』｜Biên Niên Sử Narnia｜The Chronicles of Narnia
옷장 너머의 세계를 상상하며 다음 모험을 기다렸습니다.
《완득이》｜《少年菀得》｜『ワンドゥギ』｜Wandeuk｜Punch
완득이의 이야기를 따라가며 웃기도 하고 마음이 뭉클해지기도 했습니다.
《아몬드》｜《杏仁》｜『アーモンド』｜Hạnh Nhân｜Almond
윤재의 시선으로 사람들을 바라보며 이야기에 빠져들었습니다.
《연을 쫓는 아이》｜《追风筝的人》｜『君のためなら千回でも』｜Người Đua Diều｜The Kite Runner
두 친구의 이야기가 마음에 남아 끝까지 읽고 싶어졌습니다.
《용의자 X의 헌신》｜《嫌疑人X的献身》｜『容疑者Xの献身』｜Phía Sau Nghi Can X｜The Devotion of Suspect X
사건 뒤에 숨은 마음과 진실이 궁금해 마지막 장을 향해 읽었습니다.
《어린 왕자》｜《小王子》｜『星の王子さま』｜Hoàng Tử Bé｜The Little Prince
짧은 이야기를 천천히 읽으며 기억에 남는 문장을 다시 찾아봤습니다.
🇻🇳 Việt Nam
Đã định đọc thêm vài trang rồi ngủ, nhưng câu chuyện cứ khiến tay lật tiếp đến khuya.
Harry Potter｜《哈利·波特》系列｜『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズ｜《해리 포터》 시리즈｜Harry Potter series
Thế giới phù thủy mở ra, khiến người đọc chỉ muốn theo các nhân vật đến hết cuộc phiêu lưu.
Kính Vạn Hoa｜《万花筒》｜『万華鏡』｜《만화경》｜Kính Vạn Hoa
Những câu chuyện của Quý, Tiểu Long và Hạnh khiến giờ đi ngủ thường bị lùi lại.
Cho Tôi Xin Một Vé Đi Tuổi Thơ｜《给我一张童年车票》｜『子ども時代への切符をください』｜《어린 시절로 가는 표 한 장》｜Give Me a Ticket to Childhood
Những suy nghĩ ngộ nghĩnh của trẻ con làm người đọc vừa cười vừa nhớ ngày bé.
Mắt Biếc｜《碧眼》｜『碧い瞳』｜《푸른 눈》｜Dreamy Eyes
Chuyện của Ngạn và Hà Lan khiến nhiều người muốn đọc tiếp để biết tình cảm ấy sẽ đi về đâu.
Tôi Thấy Hoa Vàng Trên Cỏ Xanh｜《我在青草地上看见黄花》｜『緑の草に黄色い花を見る』｜《푸른 풀밭 위의 노란 꽃》｜Yellow Flowers on the Green Grass
Từng chuyện nhỏ của tuổi thơ dẫn người đọc đi từ trang này sang trang khác.
Đất Rừng Phương Nam｜《南方森林土地》｜『南の森の大地』｜《남방의 숲》｜Southern Forest Land
Theo chân An qua vùng đất phương Nam, ta muốn biết chuyến đi còn đưa cậu đến đâu.
Dế Mèn Phiêu Lưu Ký｜《蟋蟀历险记》｜『こおろぎの冒険記』｜《귀뚜라미의 모험》｜Adventures of a Cricket
Những chuyến phiêu lưu của Dế Mèn khiến thế giới nhỏ bé trở nên rộng lớn.
Tây Du Ký｜《西游记》｜『西遊記』｜《서유기》｜Journey to the West
Qua mỗi thử thách, lại muốn đọc tiếp xem thầy trò Đường Tăng gặp chuyện gì.
Thám Tử Lừng Danh Sherlock Holmes｜《福尔摩斯探案》｜『シャーロック・ホームズの冒険』｜《셜록 홈즈》｜Sherlock Holmes stories
Từng manh mối khiến người đọc cố đoán lời giải trước khi thám tử nói ra.
Hoàng Tử Bé｜《小王子》｜『星の王子さま』｜《어린 왕자》｜The Little Prince
Một cuốn sách mỏng, nhưng có những trang khiến người đọc dừng lại thật lâu.

🇺🇸 USA

“One more chapter” turned into another hour whenever the story was too good to put down.

Harry Potter series｜《哈利·波特》系列｜『ハリー・ポッター』シリーズ｜《해리 포터》 시리즈｜Harry Potter
There was always one more mystery at Hogwarts waiting on the next page.
The Hunger Games｜《饥饿游戏》｜『ハンガー・ゲーム』｜《헝거 게임》｜Đấu Trường Sinh Tử
Once the Games began, it was hard to stop before finding out what happened next.
Percy Jackson & the Olympians｜《波西·杰克逊与奥林匹斯众神》｜『パーシー・ジャクソンとオリンポスの神々』｜《퍼시 잭슨과 올림포스의 신》｜Percy Jackson và các vị thần trên đỉnh Olympus
A new monster or myth could appear just when you thought it was safe to close the book.
Twilight｜《暮光之城》｜『トワイライト』｜《트와일라잇》｜Chạng Vạng
Bella and Edward’s story kept readers turning pages long after bedtime.
Goosebumps｜《鸡皮疙瘩》｜『グースバンプス』｜《구스범스》｜Nổi Da Gà
A scary chapter was easier to read under the covers—with the light still on.
The Chronicles of Narnia｜《纳尼亚传奇》｜『ナルニア国物語』｜《나니아 연대기》｜Biên Niên Sử Narnia
Stepping through the wardrobe made it tempting to stay in that world a little longer.
The Hobbit｜《霍比特人》｜『ホビットの冒険』｜《호빗》｜Người Hobbit
Bilbo’s journey offered one more reason to read past the planned stopping point.
The Giver｜《记忆传授人》｜『ギヴァー 記憶を注ぐ者』｜《기억 전달자》｜Người Truyền Ký Ức
As Jonas discovered more about his world, the questions became harder to leave unanswered.
Charlotte’s Web｜《夏洛的网》｜『シャーロットのおくりもの』｜《샬롯의 거미줄》｜Mạng Nhện Của Charlotte
Wilbur and Charlotte’s friendship made even a quiet bedtime story difficult to put away.
The Lightning Thief｜《神火之盗》｜『盗まれた雷撃』｜《번개 도둑》｜Kẻ Cắp Tia Chớp
Percy’s first quest was the kind of adventure that made the next chapter irresistible.

Our approach includes:
✅ Comparative Market Analysis — Evaluating your home against current listings and recently sold comparable properties.
✅ Three Pricing Strategies — Quick Sale (10% below estimated market value), Market Price, or Maximum Dollar Strategy (10% above estimated market value).
✅ Professional Marketing — MLS listing, professional photography, video, and drone footage when appropriate.

Russia’s Africa Arms Diplomacy: Advanced UAVs – Air Defence and the Contest for Military Sovereignty - The Moscow exhibition is strategically significant not because it demonstrates that African countries have acquired new Russian weapons, but because it places offensive unmanned systems, layered air defence, security technologies and potential local production within a common diplomatic-commercial framework.

The first-day reporting identifies the Garpia-A (E) long-range UAV, Dan-T air-launched loitering munition, small arms and an air-defence-system model. Rosoboronexport’s separately published programme advertises additional reconnaissance-strike systems and an integrated counter-drone concept. These are distinct bodies of evidence.

Rosoboronexport reports that African countries account for approximately 30% of the value of its signed-contract order portfolio. This is a company statement, not evidence of 2026 deliveries or contracts generated at the forum.

The wider market is changing. SIPRI reports that Russia’s share of global major-arms exports declined from 21% in 2016–2020 to 6.8% in 2021–2025, while China, Türkiye, the United States and European suppliers remain active competitors in African markets.

The principal operational constraint for African customers is not simply equipment affordability. It is the ability to sustain reconnaissance, targeting, command and control, maintenance, trained personnel, ammunition supply and accountable use.

The highest-consequence risks involve diversion, conflict escalation, civilian harm, weak end-use controls and dependence on external technical support.

The decisive indicators will be signed procurement instruments, export permissions, identified recipient units, funded training, sustainment contracts, verified deliveries and operational integration—not expressions of exhibition interest alone.

Russia’s African Arms Offensive: Sovereignty for Sale, Dependency by Contract
At the third Russia–Africa Summit, Moscow is marketing long-range drones, precision weapons and air defence as instruments of national sovereignty. The decisive competition, however, concerns who controls the technology, financing and military institutions after delivery.

Russia’s presentation of advanced weapons at the third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow on 28–29 October 2026 exposes a contradiction at the centre of its African strategy: military sovereignty is being marketed through technologies that may establish lasting dependence on foreign suppliers. The Garpia-A1E long-range unmanned aircraft, Dan-T air-launched loitering munition and integrated air-defence proposals extend Moscow’s offer beyond conventional arms exports into maintenance, industrial production and national-security infrastructure. Yet Russia enters this competition with sharply diminished global arms-transfer volumes and faces Chinese, Turkish, American and European suppliers already embedded in African defence markets. For African governments, the financial question is whether these acquisitions deliver independently sustainable military capability. For Moscow, the diplomatic question is whether commercial contracts can preserve influence that equipment exhibitions alone cannot demonstrate.

Russia’s order book conceals the scale of its export contraction
Rosoboronexport, Russia’s state arms-export intermediary within Rostec, reported on 23 October 2026 that African countries accounted for approximately 30% of the value of its signed-contract order portfolio. Alexander Mikheev, the company’s director general, presented African cooperation as a priority extending into local manufacturing and technical development. The figure demonstrates the importance of African contractual commitments to the exporter, but it does not disclose their monetary value, delivery schedules or the proportion already fulfilled. It cannot establish that the Moscow summit has generated additional sales.

The broader market figures explain why the distinction matters. According to SIPRI’s March 2026 assessment, Russia’s share of global major-arms exports declined from 21% in 2016–2020 to 6.8% in 2021–2025, while its export volume contracted by 64%. The United States accounted for 42% of worldwide major-arms exports in the latter period, France for 9.8% and China for 5.6%. Russia remained a major supplier, but its relative position had deteriorated considerably.

Africa is not compensating uniformly for that decline. The continent represented just 4.3% of global major-arms imports in 2021–2025, while its aggregate import volume fell by 41% compared with the preceding five years. Sub-Saharan Africa, however, recorded a 13% increase. Within that subregion, China supplied 22% of major-arms imports, Russia 12% and Türkiye 11%.

These percentages describe SIPRI transfer volumes, not contract revenue or the entire market for drones and ammunition. Their significance is structural: Moscow is competing for customers in a fragmented market where established supplier relationships, fiscal resources and military requirements differ considerably. Its commercial task is not simply to sell more weapons, but to preserve a position within the institutions that will operate and maintain them.

The advertised weapons extend military reach but expose the limits of procurement
The exhibition’s offensive systems demonstrate the type of capability Russia intends to market. In an announcement dated 21 August 2026, Rosoboronexport attributed to the Almaz-Antey Garpia-A1E an advertised maximum range of 1,000 kilometres, a warhead exceeding 50 kilograms and a circular error probable not exceeding four metres. These remain manufacturer claims, not independently verified performance under all operating conditions.

Rostec’s announcement of 8 September 2026 described Dan-T as a jet-powered, air-launched loitering munition capable, according to the manufacturer, of reaching targets hundreds of kilometres away. The distinction between the two systems matters more than their promotional specifications. Dan-T introduces aircraft-compatibility and certification requirements, while a long-range weapon directed against fixed coordinates depends on reliable target information, authorised command and secure technical support.

Rosoboronexport’s wider Moscow programme included KUB-2E, Lancet-E, Skat 350M and S350M-E, alongside the Pantsir-SMD-E and Pantsir-S1M air-defence systems, Verba, ZAK-30 Citadel and electronic counter-UAV equipment. Its proposed Anti-Drone Dome combines surveillance, electronic countermeasures, physical engagement and command functions.

This breadth allows Moscow to approach governments with different requirements, from reconnaissance to infrastructure protection. It also creates a commercial transmission mechanism: hardware acquisition can generate recurring obligations for ammunition, software, maintenance, specialist training and systems integration.

A government may own an unmanned aircraft without possessing independent access to the technical functions necessary to sustain it. An air-defence system may be delivered without a fully operational network of sensors, trained personnel and command arrangements. A production facility may assemble imported kits while critical components and intellectual property remain under foreign control. In each case, the distinction between nominal ownership and operational sovereignty determines the real value of the transaction.

The first-day exhibition account named Garpia-A (E), Dan-T, small arms and an anti-aircraft system model. The broader official programme announced additional products. Neither record establishes an African purchase, a completed delivery or a functioning recipient capability.

Africa’s buyers face different wars and incompatible fiscal demands
The Russian offer encounters military requirements that cannot be reduced to a continental procurement strategy. SIPRI records Morocco’s major-arms imports increasing by 12% between 2016–2020 and 2021–2025, while Algeria’s recorded imports declined by 78%, subject to SIPRI’s explicit warning that some reported Russian transfers could not be sufficiently verified. These North African procurement patterns reflect a different military environment from the counterinsurgency and institutional-security requirements confronting governments farther south.

Nigeria accounted for 16% of sub-Saharan African major-arms imports during 2021–2025, Senegal for 8.8% and Mali for 8.0%. Their positions establish procurement activity, not a common requirement for long-range Russian strike weapons. An aircraft suitable for conventional deterrence may be an inefficient answer to deficiencies in territorial surveillance, military logistics or accountable command.

The practical alternative is visible in Mozambique. The European Commission reported in March 2025 the completion of an €85 million European Peace Facility package supporting 11 Mozambican Quick Reaction Forces with equipment and training. In May 2026, the European Union Military Assistance Mission reported more than 40 training programmes involving approximately 1,200 military personnel, including around 300 undergoing regeneration training.

Those figures do not prove that European assistance achieved its wider security objectives. They demonstrate, however, that military capability can be developed through institutional investment rather than measured solely through weapons delivered. For African finance ministries, the comparison is consequential: a sophisticated imported platform and an adequately trained, maintained military formation represent different expenditure commitments and different forms of national capacity.

The fiscal constraint is particularly severe when a weapons contract includes foreign-currency payments, proprietary components, specialised infrastructure and recurring technical assistance. A low initial price may conceal higher lifecycle liabilities. A local assembly agreement may create employment while failing to transfer the rights necessary for domestic repair or modification. Without identifiable production volumes, financing terms and enforceable technology licences, industrial localisation remains a political proposition rather than a measurable economic result.

Security partnerships are now competing with established European influence
Russia’s industrial offer enters a security environment in which European governments are redefining relationships rather than uniformly withdrawing from Africa. The resulting competition is neither exclusively military nor adequately described as a confrontation between Moscow and the West.

Italy maintains direct maritime interests through Operation Gabinia, launched in 2020 and included among its 2026 foreign missions. The Italian Navy identifies Gulf of Guinea maritime security, protection of national economic interests and cooperation with Nigeria among its objectives. For Rome, the immediate exposure concerns commercial navigation, infrastructure security and the reliability of coastal partners. Russian equipment acquisitions would become operationally significant if they altered those partners’ actual capabilities or technical relationships, not merely because Russian products were exhibited.

France faces a different institutional adjustment. French military facilities in Senegal were returned during 2025 following the Senegalese authorities’ decision to end permanent foreign basing. A letter of intent signed by the countries’ military chiefs on 15 July 2025 provided for continuing cooperation without permanent facilities. The withdrawal of a base therefore did not necessarily terminate bilateral security relations. Nor does it establish that Moscow inherited the departing military presence or its procurement relationships.

Germany identified Sudan, the Sahel, the Horn of Africa and the Great Lakes among its conflict-prevention priorities in a Federal Foreign Office statement of 18 December 2025. Its exposure concerns the consequences of instability, arms circulation and weaknesses in regional institutions. Germany’s 5.7% share of global major-arms exports during 2021–2025 establishes industrial relevance, but its African security interests extend beyond competition for equipment contracts.

The United Kingdom, eighth among global major-arms exporters during 2021–2025, continues to combine bilateral economic and security engagement. Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s meeting with Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama on 2 June 2026 followed the signing of the UK–Ghana Growth Partnership. London’s separate security and defence partnership with the European Union, established on 19 May 2025, adds another channel for coordination without transferring national export authority to Brussels.

At EU level, the security and defence partnership signed with Ghana on 24 March 2026 provides for annual dialogue covering maritime security, counterterrorism, cybersecurity and crisis management. These programmes are not direct commercial equivalents of Rosoboronexport’s products. They compete in a different but consequential dimension: the formation of continuing institutional relationships.

Russia’s challenge is therefore to demonstrate that its equipment, technical services and industrial agreements can deliver comparable durability. Europe’s challenge is to distinguish the protection of legitimate security interests from an assumption that African procurement decisions belong within established European spheres of influence.

Sanctions, export controls and production dependence constrain the offer
The Moscow exhibition’s economic-humanitarian framing becomes most difficult to sustain where advanced weapons could enter environments characterised by fragmented military command or externally supported armed groups. SIPRI documents armed-UAV transfers to the Sudanese Armed Forces during 2021–2025 from suppliers including Iran, Türkiye, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan and the United Arab Emirates. It also identifies military equipment transfers to the Rapid Support Forces. These findings establish an existing internationalised military supply environment, not a connection between the conflict and the systems presented in Moscow.

The applicable legal distinctions are material. United Nations Security Council Resolution 2830, adopted on 8 October 2026, renewed the relevant Sudan sanctions measures until 11 December 2026 and extended the Panel of Experts’ mandate until 11 January 2027. The restrictions associated with Darfur require recipient- and destination-specific assessment; they are not interchangeable with a blanket prohibition on every transaction involving Sudan.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo presents a different framework. Security Council Resolution 2667 (2022) removed previous notification requirements for arms shipments intended for the Congolese government, while restrictions on supplies to non-governmental armed entities remain relevant. Treating government acquisitions and deliveries to unauthorised armed groups as equivalent would produce an incorrect legal assessment.

The Arms Trade Treaty, particularly Articles 6, 7 and 11, provides rules concerning prohibited transfers, export assessment and diversion prevention for states parties. Its obligations cannot simply be attributed to governments that have not joined the treaty. Binding Security Council measures and applicable national controls nevertheless remain independently consequential.

These restrictions interact with the industrial limitations of defence procurement. Export permissions, retransfer conditions, technical documentation and component availability determine what a recipient can do with equipment after acquisition. The political promise of sovereign capability is therefore constrained by law, production capacity, financing and the contractual distribution of technical rights.

The next 24 months will separate Russian contracts from Russian influence
Between October 2026 and October 2028, the decisive measure of the Moscow initiative will be whether publicised commercial interest develops into identifiable contractual and operational commitments. The relevant evidence will include named recipients, signed procurement instruments, funded training, export permissions, verified deliveries, domestic maintenance arrangements and enforceable industrial licences.

A contract would establish a commitment, not an operational capability. A delivered weapon would establish a transfer, not sustained readiness. A local factory would establish an industrial asset, not necessarily independent production. These distinctions matter because Russia can preserve diplomatic visibility without achieving substantial export growth, while an African government can announce military modernisation without obtaining the financial and technical resources necessary to sustain it.

The cost of inaction will fall unevenly. African defence ministries that purchase equipment without adequate training and support risk inventories with limited availability. Finance ministries will carry the recurring obligations of contracts whose full economic cost was not recognised at signature. Governments that accept poorly defined technology-transfer promises may finance facilities while remaining dependent on imported components and proprietary systems. Civilian populations in conflict-affected areas bear the consequences where military capability expands faster than the institutions responsible for lawful control.

European governments face a different cost: established access and industrial relationships may lose relevance if bilateral security cooperation cannot adapt to African preferences and practical requirements. Russia, meanwhile, risks committing commercial and diplomatic resources to an African market without converting its October 2026 exhibition into deliverable contracts and durable technical partnerships.

The Moscow summit has demonstrated what Russia intends to sell. The next 12–24 months will establish what African governments can afford, what Russia can deliver and who ultimately controls the capabilities acquired. Those results, rather than the weapons displayed at Gostiny Dvor, will determine the economic and geopolitical return on Moscow’s military-technical diplomacy.

NBI completes DNA tests for 90% of Yolanda victims in Tacloban

By Sarwell Q. Meniano

TACLOBAN CITY – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has completed DNA analysis for 90 percent of the more than 2,200 victims of Super Typhoon Yolanda in this city, 13 years after the disaster, the agency said Wednesday.

NBI Eastern Visayas Regional Director Jeremy Lotoc said the DNA results will be turned over to Mayor Alfred Romualdez for distribution to the victims’ surviving families ahead of the 13th anniversary of the disaster on Nov. 8, 2026.

A team of medico-legal and forensic experts from the NBI central office returned to Metro Manila on Oct. 27, signaling the completion of the latest round of DNA analysis.

“The analysis aims to help surviving families identify the specific burial locations of their loved ones in a mass grave at Holy Cross Memorial Park,” Lotoc said in an interview.

He said the DNA analysis was expedited following his appointment as regional director in the last week of August.

Lotoc, a resident of the city's coastal district of Sagkahan, lost his wife and father when Yolanda devastated Tacloban in 2013.

DNA testing is used as a last resort when families cannot provide dental or fingerprint records to help establish the identities of their missing loved ones.

“There are still issues for the remaining 10 percent of victims since we need more specimens, but they will be identified too,” Lotoc said.

The intensified DNA analysis was conducted with assistance from Tingog Party-list and the Department of Public Works and Highways.

In previous years, the NBI acknowledged delays in the identification process, noting that DNA testing was available only at its central office in Manila.

Lotoc said the agency will also work to identify victims buried in mass graves in the nearby coastal towns of Palo and Tanauan.

In the immediate aftermath of Yolanda, bodies were rapidly recovered and initially buried in temporary or common burial sites in various areas to prevent a public health crisis.

In early 2014, the city government transferred thousands of recovered remains to the mass grave at Holy Cross Memorial Park to consolidate the burial site and establish a dedicated memorial area.

While awaiting DNA test results, many families remain uncertain about the exact burial locations of their loved ones. They continue to visit the common graves to light candles, offer flowers, and prayers. (PNA)

IDENTIFIED. The nameless graves at the Holy Cross Memorial Park mass grave in Tacloban City in this file photo. The National Bureau of Investigation has completed DNA analysis for 90 percent of more than 2,200 victims of Super Typhoon Yolanda in this city, 13 years after the disaster, the agency announced Wednesday (Oct. 28, 2026). DEMOCRATS DISCOVER MILLIONS OF ELVES LIVING IN AMERICA'S FORESTS — ANNOUNCE PLANS TO REGISTER THEM TO VOTE

Party Officials Claim Previously Undocumented Woodland Population Could Transform the Midterm Elections, While Republicans Demand Proof of Citizenship and Elves Threaten to Turn Campaign Workers Into Toads

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best Selling Author

SATIRE — FICTIONAL NEWS REPORT
The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Democratic Party officials have reportedly discovered millions of elves living undetected in America's national forests, potentially creating the largest new voting constituency since someone realized college students could register without first graduating.

The discovery occurred when Democratic campaign workers conducting voter outreach in the Pacific Northwest encountered several diminutive individuals wearing pointed hats, green clothing, and shoes with curled toes. Initial communication attempts failed until one volunteer mentioned universal health care, affordable housing, and federal subsidies for sustainable mushroom cultivation.

Within minutes, approximately 400 elves emerged from the underbrush demanding voter registration forms, government identification cards, and assurances that their underground homes would qualify for federal energy-efficiency tax credits.

Democratic headquarters immediately dispatched constitutional attorneys, environmental consultants, and campaign strategists to determine whether the creatures represented an indigenous civilization, an endangered species, or an electoral opportunity capable of changing congressional control.

The classification remains unresolved, although party attorneys reportedly agree that whatever the elves are, they should be registered before November.

EXHIBIT ONE — FORTY MILLION POTENTIAL VOTERS

Preliminary estimates suggest that America's forests may contain between 12 million and 40 million elves, pixies, woodland sprites, and other previously unrepresented inhabitants.

Researchers reportedly arrived at these figures by counting 600 miniature houses beneath a grove of redwoods, multiplying that number by the estimated acreage of federally managed forests, and adding 15 million to account for elves who might be temporarily invisible.

Republicans immediately challenged the methodology, noting that the alleged inhabitants had never appeared in the federal census, filed income tax returns, obtained Social Security numbers, or registered motor vehicles.

Democratic researchers countered that elves traditionally travel by moonlight, communicate through woodland animals, and have little practical need for automobiles.

Republicans demanded to know whether traveling by moonlight constituted interstate commerce.

EXHIBIT TWO — THE CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS

The controversy intensified when Democratic attorneys advanced the theory that elves born in American forests might qualify for citizenship under the Fourteenth Amendment, provided they could establish that their families had not recently immigrated from Middle-earth.

Several elves complicated the proceedings by claiming to be more than 900 years old.

One elderly elf, identifying himself as Thistlewick, reportedly testified that his family occupied the same hollow oak before Christopher Columbus was born and that he personally remembered an unpleasant disagreement with a Roman expedition that had wandered considerably farther west than intended.

Republican attorneys demanded birth certificates.

Democratic lawyers argued that anyone who had lived in Oregon for nine centuries had probably established residency.

The Department of Homeland Security was consulted about immigration status but reportedly advised that determining citizenship would be easier if someone could first establish whether elves were human.

A proposed congressional hearing was postponed when the committee discovered that its only available expert on nonhuman citizenship specialized in the legal rights of fictional characters.

EXHIBIT THREE — OPERATION WOODLAND VOTE

With the midterms approaching, Democratic campaign organizations reportedly launched Operation Woodland Vote, establishing registration centers inside hollow logs, abandoned treehouses, and several unusually spacious beaver lodges.

Volunteers received specialized training in woodland etiquette, including instructions not to disturb enchanted stones, step on mushrooms, or promise anything to an elf without consulting legal counsel.

The initiative immediately encountered administrative complications.

Most elves refused to provide conventional residential addresses, explaining that their homes were located beneath particular trees, behind waterfalls, or inside rocks visible only during a full moon.

One application listed the applicant's residence as "the third enchanted oak beyond the silver stream, turn left at the sleeping dragon."

Election officials rejected the address because the dragon did not appear in the county's geographic information system.

Another applicant listed his occupation as "guardian of ancient secrets" and his birthdate as "before the reign of men."

A third refused to disclose his age, citing an ancient woodland covenant.

Democratic attorneys reportedly began examining whether magical concealment qualified applicants for confidential voter registration records.

EXHIBIT FOUR — REPUBLICANS DEMAND IDENTIFICATION

Congressional Republicans called for an investigation after learning that certain elves could change their appearance, disappear at will, and travel considerable distances without passing through conventional security checkpoints.

One Republican congressman proposed legislation requiring all magical creatures entering polling locations to remain visible until their ballots were deposited.

Democratic attorneys objected that the proposal unfairly targeted a minority population based on traditional cultural practices.

The dispute escalated when an elf appearing before a fictional congressional committee transformed a Republican witness's necktie into a live salamander.

The congressman demanded that the elf be held in contempt of Congress.

The elf replied that he had already held Congress in contempt for approximately 600 years.

Republican investigators subsequently demanded assurances that no individual could use magical duplication to appear simultaneously at multiple polling locations.

Democratic officials dismissed the concern as speculative until one elf demonstrated the ability to create seven identical versions of himself.

All seven demanded separate speaking time before the committee.

EXHIBIT FIVE — SANTA CLAUS BECOMES A PERSON OF INTEREST

Federal investigators reportedly discovered that some woodland elves claimed family connections to employees of Santa Claus, immediately raising questions about foreign influence, dual citizenship, and whether the North Pole constituted an independent sovereign jurisdiction.

Democratic strategists initially welcomed the discovery, believing Santa's worldwide distribution network could provide an extraordinary logistical advantage for voter outreach.

The proposal encountered difficulties when attorneys discovered that the geographic North Pole sits in international waters and that Santa's workshop has never been recognized as an American municipality.

Santa was reportedly approached about endorsing a National Toy Manufacturing Subsidy Act but declined after learning that the proposed legislation contained 1,800 pages of unrelated spending provisions and would subject his reindeer to federal commercial aviation regulations.

The reindeer threatened to strike.

EXHIBIT SIX — THE POLITICAL SURVEY BACKFIRES

Democratic strategists initially assumed that elves would overwhelmingly support environmental conservation, renewable energy, expanded public lands, and restrictions on commercial logging.

A confidential survey produced considerably less encouraging results.

Many elves opposed property taxes because their families had occupied the same trees for centuries without receiving municipal services. Others rejected federal land management policies, explaining that their communities had governed the forests long before the Department of the Interior existed.

One woodland elder questioned why officials in Washington believed themselves qualified to regulate trees they had never personally visited.

Another demanded the repeal of restrictions on enchanted swords, crossbows, and privately owned battle-axes.

Researchers also discovered widespread opposition to deficit spending because most elves expected to live long enough to repay the national debt personally.

When asked about government assistance, one respondent explained that woodland communities had survived for thousands of years through private enterprise, cooperative labor, and occasional magical intervention.

Democratic strategists became visibly concerned when preliminary polling indicated strong support for lower taxes, limited government, private property rights, and the unrestricted possession of enchanted weapons.

A senior campaign official reportedly ordered the survey destroyed.

Republicans immediately requested a copy.

EXHIBIT SEVEN — THE GREEN PARTY CLAIMS THE ELVES

The Green Party entered the controversy by announcing that woodland inhabitants represented its natural political constituency.

Organizers approached elf leaders with proposals involving environmental protection, sustainable communities, and preservation of ancient ecosystems.

The elves expressed interest until learning that the party possessed no authority to guarantee protection from logging companies, developers, or federal bureaucrats.

One elder asked why humans needed an entire political party to understand that cutting down someone's house was generally a poor idea.

Unable to provide a satisfactory explanation, organizers offered to establish a committee.

The elf turned the committee chairman into a garden gnome.

EXHIBIT EIGHT — THE SUPREME COURT FACES A NEW DEFINITION OF PERSONHOOD

Constitutional scholars reportedly anticipate that the controversy could reach the Supreme Court, raising questions the Founders apparently overlooked when drafting the Constitution.

Among them are whether elves qualify as persons under federal law, whether magical transformations affect legal identity, and whether someone who has lived for 1,200 years retains voting rights after being declared legally dead by the Social Security Administration.

The situation became particularly complicated when several woodland leaders announced that they recognized neither federal authority nor political institutions established after the fall of the ancient forest kingdoms.

Democratic attorneys nevertheless encouraged them to register.

Republicans questioned why individuals who rejected the federal government would participate in its elections.

One elf responded that he had no intention of voting but wanted to know whether registration came with free transportation, subsidized housing, or government cheese.

THE VERDICT — THE GREATEST VOTER REGISTRATION DRIVE THAT NEVER HAPPENED

Operation Woodland Vote has reportedly entered an uncertain phase, with Democratic officials attempting to reconcile their expectations of millions of sympathetic new voters with evidence that elves possess ancient property claims, strong political opinions, and a profound distrust of centralized government.

Republicans, meanwhile, have established the fictional Congressional Committee on Electoral Integrity and Supernatural Interference, whose opening hearing was postponed after its principal witness was transformed into a squirrel.

The squirrel has retained legal counsel.

The final development came when a delegation of woodland elders allegedly traveled to Washington to deliver a formal statement concerning their political intentions.

Speaking through an interpreter, their leader explained that woodland civilization had survived countless wars, devastating plagues, the rise and fall of empires, and the collapse of entire kingdoms without ever requiring assistance from a congressional appropriations committee.

"We have lived peacefully in these forests for ten thousand years. We have asked your government for nothing. We have taken nothing from your treasury. We have built our own homes, raised our families, and defended our lands. We have watched human governments come and go, and we have learned one important lesson."

When asked what that lesson was, the ancient elf replied:

"The moment politicians discover you exist, they either want your money or your vote."

The delegation then vanished into a cloud of silver dust, leaving behind a handwritten message for congressional leadership.

"PLEASE REMOVE US FROM YOUR MAILING LIST."

Democratic officials reportedly announced plans for another population survey.

Republicans demanded a recount.

The elves have since erected a ten-foot magical barrier around their forests and posted a warning at every entrance:

NO SOLICITING. NO TAX COLLECTORS. NO CAMPAIGN WORKERS.

VIOLATORS WILL BE TURNED INTO CONGRESSIONAL STAFFERS.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

text:
$LUNC is live...Longnook Uncommon Compounders ETF

BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Longnook ETF LLC, a founder-led registered investment adviser, today announced the launch of the Longnook Uncommon Compounders ETF (Ticker: LUNC) on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The actively managed fund features an unconstrained global mandate, seeking long-term capital appreciation by searching for well-priced “uncommon compounders,” defined as overlooked companies demonstrating durable competitive advantages and strong returns on capital.

ShareWe built Longnook to challenge the status quo.

LUNC is led by Founder and Chief Investment Officer David Daglio, who brings more than 25 years of institutional asset management experience to the fund. During his tenure as Chief Investment Officer at Mellon (formerly The Boston Company), Daglio oversaw $500 billion in assets, personally managed more than $10 billion in long-only and hedged equity strategies, and earned recognition from Barron’s, Institutional Investor, and Forbes. The fund’s investment process evaluates companies across five dimensions: price, sustainable advantage, governance, balance sheet, and risk. This results in a concentrated portfolio of about 30 high-conviction ideas. The LUNC portfolio represents the direct evolution of the fundamental discipline he honed as an investor and business manager.
To manage this focused mandate, Longnook utilizes a proprietary AI tool engineered specifically for decision hygiene. While Daglio retains ultimate authority, the fund’s AI acts as an algorithmic skeptic, utilizing his pre-defined rules to objectively analyze information as it unfolds. This reduces the behavioral bias and thesis drift that often plagues active management.

Wouldn't have mattered. In the past 6 months the State Police have had a handful of Troopers (some newer, some not even off probation) fired for various misconduct - and they generally tend to either have an associates degree, bachelor's, working toward finishing one or have military service

The problem is... No one wants to be a cop anymore. In Massachusetts, in the 90s if they had a police exam, without exaggeration, thousands of people took some of those exams.

The municipal exam, you had to list 4 departments you were willing to accept an offer from. Competing against hundreds of people for a department that might have 4 openings

Even in corrections, where I landed, they could be a lot more selective on who they hired. I talked to people who did backgrounds and interview boards. They were swamped. An academy class that ended up being 50 people like mine... Might have started with legitimately hundreds of background investigations, interview panels, many declined offers. So many people wanted the job (because MA pays one of the highest in the country, good benefits, etc) they had the advantage that any blemish at all they could bypass you

Today... In both corrections and policing they are running RECRUITMENT DRIVES. Ads, meeting kids at college campuses. Begging people to take the job. That same academy class... They can't even get 25 people and 5 drop out week 1 when they tell them you're working nights/weekends/Christmas Eve AND Day.

The result... You end up with a mix of people. Some departments are so desperate, they'll hire a guy that could fuck up running a yard sale.

text:
𝐇𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐫𝐨 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐬 𝐈’𝐦 𝐰𝐚𝐭𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐛𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭 

Bitcoin doesn't move on interest rates alone, Global liquidity plays a huge role. 

Here's what I’m paying attention to. 🧵

➤𝑳𝒊𝒒𝒖𝒊𝒅𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝒊𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒖𝒆𝒍 𝒃𝒆𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒅 𝒂𝒔𝒔𝒆𝒕 𝒑𝒓𝒊𝒄𝒆𝒔. 

When money and credit flow more freely through the financial system, investors generally have more room to take risks.

When liquidity tightens, capital becomes harder to access, borrowing gets more expensive, and speculative assets face pressure.

Crypto is particularly sensitive to these changes.

➤𝑩𝒊𝒕𝒄𝒐𝒊𝒏 𝒄𝒐𝒖𝒍𝒅 𝒃𝒆 𝒂𝒏 𝒆𝒂𝒓𝒍𝒚 𝒔𝒊𝒈𝒏𝒂𝒍.

#Bitcoin's recent resilience could offer clues about where the global liquidity cycle is heading.

I suggests the next expansion could begin earlier than his previous forecast of the second half of 2027.

But there's a condition: Bitcoin needs to hold above $70K, alongside evidence that bank reserves are stabilizing or growing.

That's a scenario to monitor, not confirmation of a new bull market.

➤ 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑻𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒖𝒓𝒚 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑭𝒆𝒅 𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒓 𝒎𝒐𝒓𝒆 𝒕𝒉𝒂𝒏 𝒎𝒂𝒏𝒚 𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒍𝒊𝒛𝒆. 

The U.S. Treasury can influence liquidity through its debt issuance and buyback strategy, while the Federal Reserve manages bank reserves and short-term funding conditions.

Shifting toward short-term Treasury bills and maintaining adequate bank reserves can help ease pressure on financial markets.

The key is to watch what these policies actually do to liquidity, rather than judging them by headlines alone.

➤ 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒇𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒈𝒆𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒊𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒑𝒊𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆. 

liquidity cycle in four phases:

» Rebound — liquidity starts recovering.
» Calm — liquidity expands steadily.
Speculation — risk-taking and economic activity heat up.
» Turbulence — liquidity contracts and financial stress rises.

Each phase affects asset classes differently.

Markets have been in the later stages of speculation, but an earlier turn in the cycle remains possible.

➤ 𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆'𝒔 𝒂𝒏𝒐𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒓 𝒓𝒊𝒔𝒌 𝒃𝒆𝒏𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒉 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑨𝑰 𝒃𝒐𝒐𝒎.

AI may transform the economy, but that doesn't guarantee every company investing in it will succeed.

Some companies borrowed heavily when interest rates were low. As that debt matures, refinancing at higher rates could put pressure on their finances.

If liquidity tightens further, highly leveraged businesses could struggle even while demand for AI continues to grow.

Technology can be revolutionary while some investments in it still deliver poor returns.

➤ 𝑾𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒎𝒆𝒂𝒏 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒄𝒓𝒚𝒑𝒕𝒐.

The important question is whether global liquidity is expanding, whether bank reserves are holding up, and whether Bitcoin is responding to those changes.

If liquidity turns upward earlier than expected, it could create a more supportive environment for Bitcoin and eventually the wider crypto market.

But if financial conditions tighten, even strong narratives can struggle. 

◢ 𝐍𝐎𝐓𝐄:

I wouldn't treat $70K as a magic number or assume the next bull run is guaranteed.

I'd watch Bitcoin's price action alongside global liquidity data, bank reserves, and Treasury policy.

Understanding where capital is flowing can tell us more about the market's next phase than reacting to every headline.

The real edge is understanding the conditions that move the market before everyone starts talking about the price.
