text:
SIGNAL INTELLIGENCE BRIEF
Published: October 28, 2026 | 10:48 AM ET

Thesis:
Bond-market stress has eased and the S&P 500 is steady, yet oil is up 13.66% in four weeks, the biggest technology names keep falling, and gold has not rallied.

WHAT MATTERS
Two gauges decide how much to trust this calm. The first is the MOVE index, which measures how much traders expect Treasury yields to swing, the way the VIX does for stocks. It is 93.37, down 17.08 points over four weeks and back under 100, so the bond market is calmer than a month ago. The second is the high-yield credit spread, the extra yield that weaker companies pay over the government. It is 318bps (+6bps 4wk), a mild widening. Both say stress is contained. Prices agree: the S&P 500 is up 0.08% so far today, and 0/6 basket assets are down more than 1% today in our cross-asset drawdown check. What has not changed is oil. Brent at $111.76 is the one major price still telling an inflation story.

WHAT IS HIDDEN
A long-term bond yield has three parts. The first is what investors expect inflation to be, which is the breakeven rate, 2.35% and unchanged over four weeks. The second is the real yield, the return after inflation, 2.66% and 24bps lower. The third is the term premium, the extra yield investors demand for locking money up for ten years instead of rolling short-term bills. Two models measure it, and both fell as of October 23: Kim-Wright to 0.94% (-8bps 4wk) and the New York Fed's ACM model to 0.63% (-16bps 4wk). They differ in size, so treat the direction as more reliable than the level. Put together, the 10-year at 5.02% is easing because investors want less uncertainty compensation, and the flat breakeven says they are not treating the oil jump as lasting inflation.
The cash plumbing offers a smaller offset. The Treasury's cash balance was $1020.7bn on October 26 (+61.1bn over four weeks). When the government builds up that account, cash leaves the banking system, which tightens funding at the margin. The reverse repo facility, a parking place for spare money-market cash, holds only $0.2bn, so that buffer is essentially empty. Our measure of market plumbing stress still reads zero, and the overnight funding rate is 3.95%. There is no new 10-year or 30-year auction since October 8, no new dealer positioning data since October 14, no new Treasury-bill share since September 30, no new foreign central bank custody figure since October 21 and no new foreign holder data since August 2026, so the supply side of the bond story is unobserved this morning.

WHAT IS MISPRICED
The headline index hides two markets. The S&P 500 is up 0.36% over four weeks while the equal-weight version, where every company counts the same, is up 3.92%. The Nasdaq 100 is down 2.86%, and the sector tables put Energy +10.24% at the top and Communication Services -8.09% at the bottom. Defensive sectors are up 7.0% against 3.6% for cyclicals. The giants are the weak point. Gold sits on the same list from the other side: down 3.14% over four weeks while real yields eased 24bps, it is not acting as the shelter its reputation suggests.

WHAT MARKETS DISAGREE ON
Bonds read as a growth scare: falling bond volatility, lower real yields and a lower term premium match that story better than any other we test, six of ten checks. Oil reads as inflation, with crude up 13.66% and the energy sector up 10.24%. Activity data does not look like a scare. The S&P Global composite activity index was 57.6 in October, where anything above 50 means expansion. The evidence currently favours oil as the live pressure and growth as not yet breaking, because credit has not confirmed a scare: spreads are 6bps wider against the 50bps warning line.

A second disagreement is between households, businesses and traders. The University of Michigan October survey has households expecting 4.7% inflation over the next year and 3.5% over five to ten years. The ISM services prices index was 74.0 in September, which means firms are paying markedly more. The bond market prices 2.35%. Someone is wrong. If households and firms are right, the Fed has less room to ease and long yields have a reason to rise again.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT
The stress signal: MOVE climbing back above 100 while credit spreads widen together. That pair would tell us the growth-scare reading is turning real, and falling technology and communication services shares would add to it. The relief signal: technology and communication services recovering toward the equal-weight index, with fund flows turning positive after -602.35bn over four weeks as of October 21. The event risk is Iran. Reporting dated October 28 has Iran rejecting the ideas Qatar presented and Trump declining to rule out strikes after the November 3 midterms. A new strike would show first in crude and in the energy sector.

text:
Volissos in Chios

Volissos is one of those places that encourages you to slow down and look more closely. Located in northwestern Chios, this traditional village spreads across a hillside beneath the remains of a medieval castle, surrounded by countryside and within reach of some lovely beaches.

The village is closely connected with the island's long history. Its castle dominates the skyline and reflects the strategic importance of the settlement in earlier centuries. Local tradition also links Volissos with the ancient poet Homer, although the details of Homer's life and birthplace remain uncertain.

Walking through Volissos is an experience in itself. Stone houses, winding lanes and small squares create a traditional atmosphere, while the elevated position offers views over the surrounding hills and towards the coast.

Here are some ways to enjoy a visit:
•  Explore the village streets: Discover traditional homes, quiet corners and glimpses of everyday life on Chios.
•  Look towards the castle: The medieval fortification is the village's defining landmark and a reminder of its historic importance.
•  Enjoy the countryside: The surrounding landscape is ideal for scenic drives and exploring the quieter side of the island.
•  Visit nearby beaches: The northwestern coast has several beaches where you can swim and relax, depending on local conditions.
•  Try local flavours: Stop at a village café or taverna and enjoy Greek dishes and products from Chios.

Volissos is a rewarding destination for travellers who want to see a side of Chios beyond its main town and famous mastic-producing villages. The pace is gentler, the surroundings feel spacious, and the experience is centred on local character rather than big attractions.

It is worth allowing time to explore the wider area instead of treating the village as a quick stop. The combination of historic streets, rural scenery and nearby coastline makes it a good addition to a northern Chios itinerary.

If you enjoy destinations where a simple walk can lead to a historic building, a quiet viewpoint or an unexpected conversation with a local, Volissos is well worth discovering.

text:
BEFORE THE MIDNIGHT EXPRESS — A YOUNG BOBBY EATON WAS WRITING HOME TO HIS MOTHER.

Long before he became one of the most respected wrestlers in the business, Bobby Eaton was a young man traveling from town to town, building his career in professional wrestling and making sure his mother knew he was doing all right.

This postcard, mailed from Houston, Texas, offers a glimpse into those early years.

Bobby wrote to his mother, Dorothy:

“The plane ride was real smooth, I’m sitting here in one of the best motels it’s real nice. I’m trying to find you a gift, see you soon.”

He signed it simply, “Love Bobby.”

Here was a young wrestler beginning to experience life on the road, excited about the airplane ride and the nice motel, yet still thinking about finding something special to bring home to his mother.

Years later, wrestling fans would know him as “Beautiful” Bobby Eaton, one of the finest tag team wrestlers of his generation and a cornerstone of the legendary Midnight Express.

But those who worked alongside Bobby knew something else about him. For all his accomplishments inside the ring, he was equally admired for his kindness, generosity and humility outside of it.

The photographs show Bobby with his mother, along with another handwritten message that reads:

“Mama, I love you.”

Before the fame, before the Midnight Express, before generations of wrestlers came to admire his work, Bobby Eaton was simply a son who loved his mama.

And judging by everything we’ve heard about Bobby over the years, that part of him never changed.

RIP to a good guy. “Beautiful” Bobby Eaton

— Steve Stasiak, Book Pro Wrestlers

On X Today:
Lara Logan @laralogan · 1h
Here is the Democrat plan to steal the election & the country - Sen Markey lays it out gleefully. When he speaks like this, it means this plan is already in motion. They have prepped the battlespace for a massive show of people on the streets to support their false narrative that Pres Trump is “desperate” & to prevent him from using any levers of power that he has, they are getting ahead of him & accusing him of an “election crime” when they will be the ones committing the crime.

Note how he says they have “lawyers” who have already drafted legal challenges & their plan is to use the show of force on the streets to pressure th Supreme Court justices to capitulate & rule in ther favor. If I was a betting man, I would bet that means they already have enough buy in from some of the justices (but not all) to be able to make that claim.

Most notably, they are trying to separate Republicans from Trump, which means from the people of the United States. He offers Republicans a way out - which is really a veiled threat: come with us, abandon Trump & you will be good. That is the message here. This is what an actual insurrection looks like - a real one. They have no intention of letting Pres Trump finish out his term. This is a plan for a total takeover. And if they didn’t already have some Republicans on board, they would not be making this offer publicly. So there you have it - this is how they plan to screw the President & the people of this country. And all those eating their own side alive every day are playing right into their hands.

Well done to all. If you believe in the Republic, you are about to lose it.
God help us.

GROK is this TRUE or false? 
If TRUE give details. 
If false cite the sources of this rhetoric. Use right leaning sources.

GROK says:

False as a claim of a “Democrat plan to steal the election & the country.” It is an accurate paraphrase of Sen. Ed Markey’s recent public statements, but Lara Logan’s framing of them as a confession of a pre-planned steal, “actual insurrection,” and total takeover is unsupported partisan rhetoric.
⁠YouTube

What Markey actually said

In a GBH News interview on October 27, 2026 (with Adam Reilly and others), Markey discussed anticipated 2026 midterm interference by President Trump.

Key points from the transcript:

He claimed Trump has openly discussed deploying ICE on Election Day, invoking the Insurrection Act, and deploying Marines/Army.

He asserted Trump plans an “impeachable offense” to block certification of Democratic winners so they      cannot participate in a House impeachment process in January (and related Senate seating).
“We have lawyers who are already drafting the emergency case to be brought to the Supreme Court of the United States before the election and then in the immediate aftermath.”

Thousands of lawyers are being prepared for deployment to key states and polling stations.
Democrats must be ready for a “national strike” on Election Day, with millions taking to the streets to      protest what he called Trump’s “electoral crime,” and for workers, unions, and businesses to shut down (comparing it to responses in Minneapolis after certain deaths).

This mobilization would show the Supreme Court public outrage if it receives a Democratic emergency      petition against such deployments.

He described Trump as “increasingly desperate” (citing campaigning in places like Texas, Kansas,      Nebraska, Iowa) and predicted some Republicans would distance themselves from the “MAGA Trump agenda” to avoid being “sacrificial lambs” after a big Democratic victory.⁠
YouTube

These statements match the descriptions circulating on X (including the account Logan quoted). Markey has a long record of accusing Trump of election-related threats, supporting impeachment, and introducing resolutions denouncing Trump comments on “nationalizing” elections. Washington Examiner and other outlets have reported his claims that measures like the SAVE America Act (voter ID/proof of citizenship) are about Trump “stealing” the midterms.
⁠Washingtonexaminer

Why Logan’s interpretation does not hold

Not a steal plan: 
Markey frames everything as a response to alleged Trump actions (federal agents, military, certification challenges). He does not describe altering ballots,      suppressing legitimate votes, or seizing power outside legal/political channels. Pre-positioned lawyers, observers, and legal challenges are routine for both parties in close elections.

“Insurrection” / “total takeover”:      
Peaceful protests, strikes, and court filings are constitutionally protected speech and legal activity. Insurrection requires violent efforts to overthrow the government. Calling ordinary (if aggressive) political      mobilization an insurrection is rhetorical escalation, not a factual description.

Pressure on SCOTUS / “buy-in from some justices”:      Markey explicitly said the streets are meant so the Court “can see that the public is outraged.” Speculating that this implies secret prior      commitments from justices is pure conjecture with no supporting evidence.

Separating Republicans from Trump:      
Noting that some Republicans might distance themselves after a large Democratic wave is standard political analysis of party incentives. It is not evidence of a secret deal or veiled threat of a coordinated takeover.

No secret “plan already in motion” to block Trump’s term:      
Markey’s repeated public calls for impeachment are open constitutional processes, not a covert operation.
Both parties routinely prepare legal teams, messaging about the other side’s “desperation,” and contingency mobilization. Democrats have long accused Republicans of suppression or interference; Republicans (including outlets like Washington Examiner and Fox News) have long accused Democrats of overreach, lawfare, and undermining election integrity measures. 
Markey’s interview is open contingency planning against what he views as threats—not a documented blueprint for Democrats to steal the election.

The primary source is the publicly available GBH interview itself. Logan’s post is an interpretive overlay common in heated election rhetoric on all sides.

Laura Logan, Journalist------------Sen(D) Ed Markey

THE EVIDENCE™
MAKE SATIRE GREAT AGAIN!

One Medieval Bird Mask, Two Dead NFL Legends, John Kerry, and America's Growing Inability to Recognize a Joke

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best Selling Author
SATIRE — COMMENTARY — AN OCCASIONAL ENCOUNTER WITH REALITY

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

BREAKING NEWS — A concerned citizen has uncovered a potentially devastating historical inaccuracy in one of my recent satirical articles. The discovery involved neither a fabricated quotation nor a misidentified historical figure, but something apparently far more consequential: a bird-shaped mask appearing in the wrong historical period.

The offending object appeared in my recent medieval satire featuring JFK Jr. The mask was the familiar long-beaked design associated with plague doctors, an image most commonly connected with the seventeenth century rather than the medieval period.

Somewhere in America, an individual encountered this outrageous violation of historical chronology and apparently decided that immediate corrective action was necessary.

Never mind that the article was satire. Never mind that its premise was intentionally ridiculous. Never mind that historical figures, deceased celebrities, and contemporary political personalities regularly appear in my stories under circumstances that could not possibly have occurred.

The bird mask was from the wrong century.

Civilization had apparently reached a breaking point.

I responded politely, explaining the definition of satire and pointing out that fictional comedy is not ordinarily governed by the evidentiary standards of historical scholarship. Satire employs exaggeration, absurdity, irony, and deliberate departures from reality to expose human foolishness. Requiring every fictional detail to satisfy a historian rather defeats the purpose.

Nevertheless, the encounter caused me to reconsider my responsibilities as an author.

Perhaps I have underestimated the importance of historical accuracy in stories whose entire purpose is to describe events that never happened.

Perhaps I should take satire more seriously.

EXHIBIT ONE — THE GREAT MEDIEVAL BIRD MASK SCANDAL

For those unfamiliar with the controversy, the familiar long-beaked plague doctor costume is generally associated with early modern Europe, particularly the seventeenth century. Its appearance in a medieval setting was therefore historically inaccurate.

Congratulations. The investigation has been completed.

Unfortunately, the discovery is about as relevant to the article's premise as pointing out that Fred Flintstone could not have operated a prehistoric automobile because the internal combustion engine had not yet been invented.

The absurdity is intentional.

If I depict Julius Caesar invading Scotland with Apache helicopters and Roman centurions carrying AR-15s, I am not inviting archaeologists to search for helicopter wreckage along Hadrian's Wall.

Likewise, a fictional depiction of JFK Jr. wearing a plague doctor mask is not a scholarly presentation on the evolution of European medical equipment.

Yet there is something almost admirable about the extraordinary concentration required to examine a completely fictional historical scenario, overlook its impossible premise, and identify a single costume accessory as the detail requiring correction.

It is rather like watching The Wizard of Oz and complaining that flying monkeys are not native to Kansas.

Technically accurate.

Spectacularly irrelevant.

EXHIBIT TWO — THE NFL'S UNREPORTED RESURRECTION CRISIS

What makes the medieval mask controversy particularly entertaining is that I recently published multiple satirical accounts involving legendary quarterback Daryle Lamonica and Hall of Fame coach Hank Stram appearing on an NFL football field this past Sunday.

There is one minor complication.

Both men are dead.

Lamonica died in 2022. Stram died in 2005. Neither has been available for professional football activities for a considerable period, although that apparently did not prevent me from returning them to the sidelines and playing field.

Think about the implications.

I successfully resurrected two professional football legends, transported them into the 2026 NFL season, and placed them in circumstances requiring the suspension of virtually every known principle of biology.

Yet nobody contacted me to explain that Lamonica was medically unavailable or that Stram had not coached an NFL game in decades.

The NFL Players Association did not demand representation for deceased athletes. The Pro Football Hall of Fame did not investigate whether either man had violated the terms of his retirement, and no medical examiner requested an explanation for their unexpected return to active duty.

Apparently, dead people participating in professional football are acceptable literary devices, provided nobody wears a historically inaccurate hat.

I am beginning to suspect that American education has produced people capable of identifying minor historical discrepancies in fictional accounts while remaining completely indifferent to the impossible events surrounding them.

EXHIBIT THREE — LARRY ELDER, JOHN KERRY, AND THE ONION

The experience reminded me of something I heard years ago from Larry Elder, the political commentator and broadcaster who now operates in the podcast world.

Elder discussed an episode involving John Kerry, the former Democratic presidential nominee, and The Onion, the satirical publication famous for inventing fictional news stories that occasionally become difficult to distinguish from actual political developments.

The underlying incident dates to April 2005.

During remarks concerning alleged voting irregularities in the 2004 presidential election, Kerry stated:

"Leaflets are handed out saying Democrats vote on Wednesday, Republicans vote on Tuesday."

There was an interesting complication.

During the 2004 campaign, The Onion had published a fictional election story in which Republicans encouraged minority voters to cast their ballots on Wednesday, November 3, conveniently one day after Election Day.

The joke was straightforward. Republican operatives supposedly wanted Democratic-leaning voters to participate enthusiastically in the election, provided they arrived after voting had concluded.

Elder and others subsequently drew attention to the similarity between Kerry's remarks and the fictional scenario.

To be precise, the existence of Kerry's statement and The Onion article does not conclusively establish that Kerry obtained his information from the satirical publication. Actual allegations of election-related deception circulated independently, and demonstrating that Kerry relied directly upon The Onion would require additional evidence.

Nevertheless, the controversy presents an irresistible possibility: a major presidential candidate being accused of confusing a satirical news story with evidence of genuine political misconduct.

This raises an important question.

If satire can become sufficiently convincing that public officials are suspected of repeating it as fact, perhaps I have been approaching the entire profession incorrectly.

Instead of worrying about whether my medieval characters wear historically accurate costumes, perhaps I should be concerned that somebody in Washington will someday cite one of my stories during a congressional hearing.

Imagine a senator solemnly announcing that an investigation has confirmed Daryle Lamonica and Hank Stram returned to the NFL, only to be interrupted by a colleague demanding to know whether their contracts comply with the league's salary cap.

At that point, I would have to decide whether to issue a correction or accept an appointment as the administration's new Director of Historical Resurrection.

EXHIBIT FOUR — WHEN REALITY BECOMES THE SATIRIST'S COMPETITOR

The fundamental problem confronting modern satire is not that writers have become less imaginative. It is that the world has become increasingly competitive.

For generations, satirists exaggerated ordinary human behavior to expose vanity, hypocrisy, incompetence, and institutional foolishness. Jonathan Swift employed savage irony to challenge the attitudes of his time. Mark Twain exposed social pretensions through characters and situations that revealed the contradictions people preferred not to acknowledge.

Today, the satirist faces an entirely different challenge.

How does one exaggerate congressional dysfunction when actual congressional hearings regularly produce exchanges that would be rejected by television comedy writers as too ridiculous?

How does one parody government bureaucracy when the government routinely generates regulations, administrative procedures, and official explanations that resemble rejected scripts from Monty Python?

The Onion once enjoyed the considerable advantage of imagining political developments that were obviously too preposterous to occur.

That advantage has diminished.

We now inhabit an environment in which a fictional headline can sound entirely plausible while an authentic news report occasionally reads like a desperate attempt to compete with the writers of Saturday Night Live.

Consider the occupational dilemma. A satirist must invent something outrageous enough to distinguish it from actual government activity while accommodating readers who believe every fictional detail should conform to reality.

I could publish a story announcing that Congress has unanimously voted to relocate the federal government to the moon, and somebody would undoubtedly demand to know whether the proposed construction complies with local zoning ordinances.

Meanwhile, the genuinely absurd aspects of the legislation would pass without comment.

EXHIBIT FIVE — THE DEPARTMENT OF HISTORICAL COMEDY COMPLIANCE

Following yesterday's correction, I have decided that the responsible course of action may be to establish a federal agency charged with regulating historical accuracy in fictional comedy.

The Department of Historical Comedy Compliance would examine satirical articles, political cartoons, theatrical productions, and television programs to ensure that all costumes, terminology, technology, and historical references conform to their assigned centuries.

Its staff would include medieval historians, archaeologists, costume specialists, military researchers, and approximately four thousand attorneys. The initial annual budget would be $3.7 billion, with emergency appropriations available whenever somebody discovers an inaccurate helmet in a Monty Python movie.

Mel Brooks would be required to submit Blazing Saddles for review because the film concludes with an outrageous sequence that moves from the Old West into a Hollywood movie studio.

The producers of The Flintstones would face substantial penalties for portraying prehistoric families operating automobiles, telephones, and household appliances.

Bugs Bunny would be investigated for repeated violations of the laws of physics, while Wile E. Coyote would face federal sanctions for operating explosives without the appropriate licenses.

The agency's most challenging assignment would undoubtedly involve reviewing my articles, particularly those depicting deceased NFL legends returning to professional football. Employment eligibility alone could require years of investigation.

As for the medieval bird mask, that violation would be classified as a historical felony carrying a mandatory minimum sentence of three years in a Renaissance reenactment camp.

My critic could serve as the agency's first director.

After all, anyone capable of identifying a seventeenth-century plague doctor mask in an intentionally absurd medieval satire clearly possesses the qualifications necessary for federal employment.

EXHIBIT SIX — THE LOST ART OF RECOGNIZING A JOKE

There is, however, a more serious observation beneath the comedy.

Satire requires something from its audience that no amount of historical research can provide: the ability to recognize that an author is deliberately departing from reality.

The reader must understand the distinction between an assertion and an invention, between historical documentation and humorous exaggeration, and between a factual error that compromises an argument and an intentional impossibility that creates the joke.

That distinction is fundamental.

When I publish an investigative article under THE EVIDENCE™, factual accuracy is essential. Claims must be supported, quotations must be authentic, and conclusions must withstand scrutiny. If I identify the wrong century in a factual discussion of European medicine, a correction is appropriate.

But satire operates under different literary conventions. Its purpose is not necessarily to document what happened, but to illuminate human behavior through what never happened.

Of course, labeling something satire does not automatically make it funny, intelligent, or effective. Readers are entitled to criticize its execution, question its premise, or declare that the humor simply does not work.

What makes yesterday's encounter entertaining is the extraordinary narrowness of the objection.

Of all the impossible things contained in a fictional medieval scenario involving JFK Jr., the concern was the historical origin of a bird mask.

That particular criticism did not address whether the article was amusing, whether its underlying observation was worthwhile, or whether the satire accomplished its intended purpose.

It merely established that a seventeenth-century costume had appeared in the wrong imaginary century.

An impressive accomplishment, assuming the objective was to misunderstand the assignment.

THE VERDICT — MAKE SATIRE GREAT AGAIN!

After careful consideration, I have reached a conclusion.

I have been far too irresponsible in my treatment of historical chronology, deceased celebrities, fictional political developments, and imaginary events.

I have allowed NFL legends to return from the dead without medical authorization. I have transported historical figures across centuries without notifying the appropriate authorities. I have placed modern objects into ancient settings and subjected recognizable public personalities to circumstances that no responsible historian would ever endorse.

And now I stand accused of the ultimate literary offense.

A seventeenth-century bird mask appeared in a medieval satire.

I plead guilty.

Not merely guilty, but spectacularly, unapologetically, and enthusiastically guilty.

As for the John Kerry controversy, it reminds us that the distinction between satire and factual reporting can become particularly entertaining when people fail to recognize which one they are reading.

The irony is almost perfect.

One public figure was accused of treating satire as fact. My critic appeared to demand that satire conform to historical fact.

Somewhere between those two positions lies an entire nation increasingly uncertain whether it should laugh, demand a correction, or convene a congressional hearing.

I have therefore decided to launch a new national initiative.

MAKE SATIRE GREAT AGAIN!

The program will require no federal funding, no congressional authorization, and no executive order. Participation will be voluntary, although anyone unable to distinguish a joke from a historical documentary may be required to complete remedial instruction using selected episodes of The Three Stooges.

Graduation will depend upon demonstrating the ability to watch a fictional character get hit over the head with a frying pan without demanding a medical report.

Advanced students will be permitted to read THE EVIDENCE™ without supervision.

And to the gentleman who identified the offending bird mask, I offer my sincere appreciation. His observation has reminded me that somewhere in America, even the most ridiculous fictional story can attract a dedicated investigator determined to establish that it never happened.

I look forward to his next discovery.

Perhaps he will investigate how Daryle Lamonica and Hank Stram managed to participate in professional football this past Sunday despite having been dead for years.

But first, I have one final announcement.

My next medieval satire will feature JFK Jr. wearing a seventeenth-century plague doctor mask while riding a Harley-Davidson through thirteenth-century England, accompanied by Julius Caesar, Napoleon Bonaparte, and two deceased NFL legends.

They will be traveling to a congressional hearing on historical accuracy.

And I fully expect somebody to complain that the motorcycle is the wrong model year.

MAKE SATIRE GREAT AGAIN!

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

text:
BLACK AMERICAN HISTORY
On this day Oct 28, 1958

Police Arrest, Jail, and Beat Two Black Boys After a White Girl Kisses Them on the Cheek in Monroe, North Carolina

A bright, warm afternoon in late October 1958, in rural Monroe, North Carolina: two Black children, nine-year-old James Hanover Thompson and his eight-year-old friend David “Fuzzy” Simpson, were playing with a group of white boys and girls in the yard next to one of the white children’s homes. Jim Crow laws were rigidly enforced at the time, but it was not unusual for Black and white children to play together when their separate, segregated schools let out for the day. They knew each other. The mothers of the Black children cooked and cleaned for the mothers of the white children.

As afternoon gave way to evening that day, October 28, and some of the children left, a kissing game began. One of the white girls, seven-year-old Sissy Sutton, kissed first David on the cheek, and then James, before heading home. Retrieving their wagons, which held a stash of empty bottles they hoped to sell, the two friends walked toward the center of town. They had no way of knowing they’d done anything wrong, and that white Monroe was about to severely punish them, and their families—for a kiss.

Sissy Sutton mentioned the kiss to her parents when she got home. James’s mother had worked for Sissy’s mother; his grandmother had worked for Sissy’s grandmother. Reportedly in hysterics and threatening to kill James, Sissy’s mother notified police. Rumors raced through the white community. Sissy’s father grabbed his shotgun and, joined by a mob threatening a lynching, he crossed the railroad tracks that divided Monroe’s white and Black neighborhoods. The Thompsons’ house was dark. The mob would have killed them if the police hadn’t gotten there first, Mr. Thompson told EJI, recalling “They would have shot us. They was mad, they was gonna kill us.” James’s mother, Evelyn Thompson, would also tell a reporter months later that “some white people in Monroe” had warned her “that my family would be killed if I didn’t get out of town.”

James and David were pulling their wagons when police accosted them, with guns drawn. Shouting racial epithets and calling them “little rapists,” police handcuffed the boys and shoved them into a patrol car. “When we got down to the police station, we understood that they said we had raped a little white girl,” James Thompson would recall more than half a century later. “They took us down in the bottom of the police station to a cell … They started beating us, they were beating us to our body, you know? They didn’t beat us to the face where nobody could see it. They just punched us all in the stomach and back and legs. We couldn’t understand why grown people was beating us up, but we didn’t have nobody to defend us. We was hollering and screaming. We thought they were going to kill us.” Their cries were only met with “shut up back there!” Mr. Thompson told EJI.

For the next six days they were kept locked up and barred from seeing their parents. Police entered their cell on Halloween, pretending to be Klansmen. “These men came with sheets over their heads,” Mr. Thompson would recall later. “They said they were going to hang us, lynch us. I was crying. I was scared to death.”

So began the infamous “Kissing Case,” as it came to be called, a case that shined an international spotlight on the bigotry and racial injustice in the South. The lives of James Thompson and David Simpson and their families were shattered and the entire Black community was traumatized, but as the spotlight shifted, with the exception of a television interview with Oprah Winfrey in 1993 and a 2011 interview for StoryCorps and NPR, the Kissing Case all but disappeared from public view.

“It’s been swept under the rug,” James Thompson’s younger brother, Dwight “Dee“ Thompson, 62, said in a 2023 interview with EJI, revisiting the Kissing Case as the 65th anniversary approached. “They just tried to move on, even the city, just tried to move on … People going to church together, people working in the community … The town was divided because of the Kissing Case [but] you had to go work for these people, Black folks worked for the white folks … Everybody go along to get along. Don’t talk about the Kissing Case, just keep moving, that’s a thing of the past,” recalled Dwight Thompson. “It’s history—American history. It’s shameful history.”

In 2023, EJI interviewed Mr. Thompson and his siblings. You can watch the interview here.

A "separate but equal" hearing, a burning cross on the lawn

The boys were charged with assault and molestation. A juvenile court judge, J. Hampton Price, prepared to hear the case—but first he contacted the Morrison Training School in Hoffman, North Carolina, to secure places for the boys. The reformatory was founded as the State Training School for Negro Boys and renamed for Cameron Morrison, a North Carolina governor who had been a leader of the white supremacist Red Shirts.

Judge Price held his first hearing with just Sissy Sutton and her parents, thus denying the boys their right to confront their accuser. Then he held what he called a “separate but equal” hearing, and without attorneys there to defend them, he ruled the boys were guilty. He would later cite the boys’ silence when confronted with the charges as an admission of their guilt. On November 3, the judge sentenced the boys to spend the rest of their childhoods at the Morrison school. They would be eligible for release when they turned 21.

Within days, Evelyn Thompson’s white landlord sent her an eviction notice. Mrs. Thompson and David Simpson’s widowed mother, Jennie Simpson, were fired from their $15-a-week jobs as domestic workers.

At night, shots were fired at the family's home, Mr. Thompson told EJI. “My mom and them, they would go out in the morning and sweep bullets off the porch,” James’s older sister, Brenda Lee Graham, recalled in the StoryCorps interview.

Evelyn Thompson didn’t sleep. “She would be up walking the floors and praying,” Ms. Graham said. She also remembered “that at night you could see them burning crosses … right down the front yard.”

Someone even killed James’s dog.

“They ran our family out of town,” Dwight Thompson told EJI. The NAACP moved both families into public housing in Charlotte for their own safety. “We were kind of happy that we were getting out of there,” Brenda Lee Graham told EJI. “We wouldn’t have to be terrorized anymore at night, scared to sleep. Mama used to sit up [at night] and look out the windows. That’s where Dwight was born, in 1961. “After everything that happened,” he said, “my mother had the audacity to have another child.”

The secret story gets out

None of Monroe’s three newspapers or any of the state’s white newspapers covered the hearing or, initially, any of the events surrounding the Kissing Case. James and David might have spent years at the Morrison school but for the involvement of Robert Williams, the president of Monroe’s NAACP, who took up their cause, and Ted Poston, a Black reporter for the New York Post, who agreed to write about the case.

On November 10, Mr. Poston’s story—which included the detail that the two boys had been threatened with lynching—ran on the Post’s front page. A Black civil rights attorney from New York, Conrad Lynn, got in touch with Robert Williams, offering to represent the boys.

Mr. Williams had already drawn the ire of white residents in Monroe. Weeks before the kissing episode he had petitioned, unsuccessfully, for his children to attend the segregated public elementary school. The previous year, he’d tried, and failed, to get Monroe to integrate its public swimming pool for even one day a week. Black children had drowned in local swimming holes and creeks, but officials said desegregation would be too costly because they would have to drain and clean the pool after Black swimmers used it.

Thanks in part to Mr. Williams’s efforts, newspapers elsewhere began picking up the story of the Kissing Case. Joyce Egginton, a reporter for the London News-Chronicle, traveled to Monroe. Accompanied by the boys’ mothers, along with Robert Williams and Conrad Lynn, the London reporter, posing as a social worker and with a camera concealed under a fruit basket, visited James and David at the reformatory. Mr. Thompson recalled to EJI that his mom had only been allowed to visit the one time. 

On December 18, her story and a photo of the boys with their mothers ran on the News-Chronicle’s front page. Papers across Europe picked up the story, sparking an international campaign aimed at winning the boys’ freedom. Thousands of schoolchildren in the Netherlands sent letters to North Carolina Gov. Luther H. Hodges. Clergy on both sides of the Atlantic protested. So did union members and college students in the North.

The NAACP appealed the case in North Carolina courts. On January 12, 1959, state superior court judge Walter Johnston presided over a two-hour hearing at which both boys and their mothers were present, along with their lawyer, Conrad Lynn, who argued for their innocence. In his testimony, Judge Price twice referred to the boys with the n-word, according to the Winston-Salem Journal. David fell asleep, with his head on his friend James’s shoulder, waking up to hear Judge Johnston say he was sending both boys back to the reformatory. The judge said he had heard no evidence that the boys should not have been convicted. Newspapers reported that David and James both cried.

A Black newspaper, The Carolinian, ran a photo of both mothers in tears as they left the courthouse, where a statue of a Confederate soldier towered near the entrance, captioned “In Despair.”

Embarrassed by worldwide attention to the case, Gov. Hodges, Judge Price, and other white officials went on the offensive. They enlisted the state’s white media to publicly blame the boys and their mothers, and in violation of the requirement to protect juveniles’ privacy, they freely offered details they said had been provided by social service workers, teachers, and police. They said they were acting to correct “misinformation” and “inaccuracies” in the national and international media.

Officials branded James and David as “incorrigible” and “wayward” delinquents with irresponsible mothers. They said the boys had been sent to the reformatory for their own good, claimed Mrs. Thompson “has a bad reputation” in her community, and charged that Mrs. Simpson’s children were often in trouble with police. Local and state news outlets repeated those officials’ words in articles that showed little concern about accuracy.

“This is my family’s history,” Dwight Thompson told EJI. The local and state mainstream media coverage, which he reviewed as part of his own research, did not portray the mother who had raised him. “My mother is my hero. I can’t imagine what she endured,” recalled Dwight Thompson. “She was a good person, kind as she could be. Give you the coat off her back,” Brenda Lee Graham told EJI.

When asked about what their mother was like, the Thompson siblings remembered her as a wonderful, loving woman who fed the homeless and always had a dollar to help a friend in need. She was a praying woman who took her family to church seven days a week and made every family celebration a good time, baking jelly roll cakes on the siblings' birthdays. She would also make "killer fried chicken" and pecan pies on Sundays.

Led by Black journalists, national media attention continued to spread and on February 13, 1959, bowing to public pressure, Gov. Hodges—who went on to become U.S. Secretary of Commerce—pardoned the boys. Released from the reformatory, they joined their families, who had been relocated by the NAACP to public housing in Charlotte.

We should sterilize you”

A couple days later, an AP reporter interviewed both mothers in Charlotte. All the boys had been doing on that October afternoon, Mrs. Thompson said, were innocent things—“raking leaves for a white lady,” a game of “cowboys and Indians” with their friends, and “playful-like” kisses on the cheek. But that night a policeman came to the house and told her James had been arrested. “We haven’t had much peace since it happened,” she said.

The media spotlight quickly moved on, but the stigma remained for both boys.

David Simpson said a police sergeant from Monroe told Charlotte police to look for him whenever crimes occurred. “I was never able to get out of the system,” he told Oprah Winfrey in 1993.

James Thompson remembered the words of the state psychologist he was required to visit weekly in Charlotte after being released from the state reformatory. “He said, ‘What are you, some kind of maniac? We should sterilize you.’”

This was not a hollow threat. North Carolina sterilized more than 7,000 people between the 1920s and the 1970s. A recent study by scholars identified the Morrison Training School as one of the “feeder” institutions that sent children to be sterilized. Black people were sterilized in the 1960s at a much higher rate than white people, the study found.

After James returned home from Morrison, his sister, Brenda Lee Graham, recalled during the StoryCorps interview, “It was like seeing somebody different that you didn’t even know. He never talked about what he went through there. But ever since then, his mind just hadn’t been the same.”

Both boys were repeatedly arrested and incarcerated as they got older.

James said to his brother Dwight, who interviewed him for StoryCorps, “I always sit around and wonder if this hadn’t happened to me, you know, what could I have turned out to be? Could I have been a doctor? Could I have gone off to some college or some great school? It just destroyed our life.”

“I still feel the hurt and the pain from it,” James told his younger brother. “And nobody ever said, ‘Hey, look, I’m sorry what happened to y’all. It was wrong.’”

Mr. Thompson told EJI that the incident left him fearful, especially when visiting Monroe.

Still today, no one—no local or state officials or the media—has ever apologized to Mr. Thompson or Mr. Simpson or their families, or compensated them for violating their rights. "We should have been compensated for what happened to us, what happened to our families, destroyed our families—running us out of town, shooting up our dogs, wrongfully convicted. We need to be apologized to for what we went through," Mr. Thompson told EJI. 

Sissy Sutton never spoke about the kiss publicly. In 1993, Oprah Winfrey asked Mr. Thompson and Mr. Simpson, “Do you blame her?”

Both men responded immediately that the little girl should not be held responsible. “I don’t blame her,” Mr. Thompson said. “We were kids, kids do innocent things.” When EJI spoke with Mr. Thompson, he expressed the same sentiment that, all these years later, he still did not blame the little girl.

“It wasn’t her fault,” Mr. Simpson said. “Children [are] only taught what their parents feed them.”

18 ARRESTED IN MONTHS-LONG WAGONER COUNTY CHILD SEX STING, INCLUDING THREE REPORTEDLY CONVICTED OF RAPE IN PRIOR CASES

WAGONER COUNTY, Oklahoma

Eighteen people have been arrested in connection with a months-long undercover operation targeting adults suspected of attempting to engage in sexual activity with children as young as 14.
The Wagoner County Sheriff’s Office conducted the operation between May and October 2026, working with Safe from Online Sex Abuse (SOSA), a nonprofit organization that assists law enforcement in investigating online child sexual exploitation.
Investigators posed as girls ages 14 and 15 on social media platforms. Authorities say suspects engaged in sexually explicit conversations, requested nude photographs and arranged meetings for sexual activity, believing they were communicating with underage girls.
THREE SUSPECTS REPORTEDLY HAD PRIOR RAPE CONVICTIONS
According to Wagoner County investigators, three of the 18 individuals arrested were already registered sex offenders with previous rape convictions.
Investigators described the suspects as coming from various backgrounds, including fathers, grandfathers, construction workers and an individual who owns a multimillion-dollar corporation in Broken Arrow.
Authorities also reported that one suspect pretended to be a Tulsa police officer.
SUSPECTS TRAVELED ACROSS STATE LINES
Investigators say several suspects traveled hours to meet individuals they believed were underage girls. Some reportedly traveled from Arkansas, one came from Georgia and another from Dallas, Texas.
In one account described by investigators, a suspect traveling from Dallas reportedly learned during the drive that his father had died. Despite receiving the news, authorities say he continued to Broken Arrow for the arranged meeting and was arrested.
Investigators also reported that:
• One suspect allegedly offered $300 for sexual activity with a 15-year-old.
• Another allegedly offered $160 for sexual activity with someone he believed was a pregnant 15-year-old girl.
• A man and woman allegedly invited someone they believed was a 14-year-old girl to their home for sexual activity involving both adults.
18 INDIVIDUALS IDENTIFIED IN THE OPERATION
The following individuals were identified in a published composite of arrest photographs associated with the investigation:
1. Aaron Wendt
2. Austin Alexander

SHERIFF WARNS PARENTS ABOUT ONLINE SEXUAL EXPLOITATION
Wagoner County Sheriff Chris Elliott warned that individuals seeking to sexually exploit children can contact them through cell phones, laptops, Chromebooks and social media applications without ever approaching them in person.
Investigators are encouraging parents to monitor their children’s online activity, review unfamiliar contacts and applications, and have conversations about the dangers of communicating with strangers online.
The Wagoner County Sheriff’s Office says it intends to continue undercover investigations targeting individuals suspected of attempting to sexually exploit children.
The arrests involve criminal allegations, not findings of guilt. All defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

The Top 5 Myths About Travel Agents and Why They Still Matter More Than Ever

In an age where travelers can book flights, hotels, cruises, and excursions with a few clicks, many people wonder whether travel agents are still relevant. Yet experienced travelers often discover that having a trusted travel advisor can save both time and money while eliminating many of the frustrations that can turn a dream vacation into a stressful experience.

Unfortunately, several myths continue to surround the travel industry. Let's separate fact from fiction and explore why travel agents remain one of the smartest resources available to today's travelers.

Myth #1: Travel Agents Cost More Than Booking Online

This is perhaps the most common misconception.

Many travelers assume that using a travel agent means paying extra fees on top of the vacation package. In reality, travel agents frequently have access to preferred supplier pricing, negotiated rates, promotional offers, and special amenities that aren't always visible on public booking websites.

Many suppliers compensate travel advisors directly, meaning travelers often receive professional planning assistance at little or no additional cost.

In many cases, a travel advisor can secure:

Resort credits
Complimentary room upgrades
Onboard cruise credits
Free specialty dining
Reduced deposits
Exclusive package pricing

The result can be a vacation that costs the same, or even less, than booking independently while delivering significantly greater value.

Myth #2: Everything Can Be Found Online

While the internet provides plenty of information, it cannot replace experience.

Travel agents spend years learning destinations, cruise lines, resorts, and tour operators. They often visit properties personally and receive firsthand feedback from hundreds of clients.

An online review might tell you a resort is "excellent," but a travel advisor can explain:

Which building offers the best views
Whether the resort suits families or couples
Which excursions are worth the money
When to travel for the best weather
Which room categories are worth upgrading to

That kind of personalized insight can prevent costly mistakes and disappointment.

Myth #3: Travel Agents Only Book Cruises

Cruises remain one of the most popular travel segments for advisors, but modern travel agents book far more than ships.

Today's travel professionals can assist with:

Ocean cruises
River cruises
Family vacations
All-inclusive resorts
Luxury travel
Guided tours
Safaris
Honeymoons
Destination weddings
Group travel
Corporate travel
Rail journeys
Adventure expeditions

Many agents specialize in specific destinations or travel styles, allowing them to provide expert guidance tailored to each traveler's needs.

Myth #4: Travel Agents Are Only for Luxury Travelers

While luxury clients certainly benefit from travel advisors, so do travelers on modest budgets.

A skilled travel agent helps maximize value regardless of price point.

Whether planning:

A weekend getaway
A family road trip
A Caribbean cruise
A bucket-list European vacation

A good advisor focuses on finding the best experience within the client's budget.

The goal isn't necessarily spending more. The goal is spending smarter.

Myth #5: Travel Agents Only Help Before the Trip

This may be the biggest myth of all.

The true value of a travel advisor often appears when something goes wrong.

Flight cancellation? Delayed cruise departure? Hotel overbooking? Weather disruption?

Instead of spending hours on hold with airlines or suppliers, travelers have an advocate working on their behalf.

Travel agents frequently assist with:

Flight changes
Rebookings
Schedule disruptions
Supplier communication
Emergency travel issues
Travel insurance claims guidance

When travel problems arise, having a knowledgeable professional in your corner can be invaluable.

How Travel Agents Make Your Life Easier
They Save You Time

Researching destinations, comparing hotels, evaluating cruise lines, and coordinating travel logistics can take dozens of hours.

A travel advisor narrows the options and presents recommendations that fit your goals, budget, and interests.

They Reduce Stress

Travel planning involves many moving parts. Advisors coordinate flights, accommodations, transportation, excursions, dining reservations, and special requests, allowing travelers to focus on the excitement of the trip instead of the logistics.

They Provide Personalized Recommendations

Unlike booking platforms that rely on algorithms, travel advisors learn about your preferences and recommend experiences specifically tailored to you and your traveling companions.

They Offer Ongoing Support

Travel advisors remain available before, during, and after your trip, providing peace of mind that online booking engines simply cannot match.

How Travel Agents Can Save You Money

Many travelers are surprised at the number of ways advisors help reduce overall travel costs.

Access to Exclusive Promotions

Travel suppliers frequently offer special promotions to travel professionals and their clients.

Better Value Packages

An advisor may package flights, hotels, transfers, and excursions together at pricing unavailable through individual bookings.

Avoiding Costly Mistakes

Booking the wrong location, travel dates, room category, or transfer arrangements can lead to unnecessary expenses. Professional guidance helps avoid these pitfalls.

Added Amenities

Complimentary upgrades, credits, and perks often increase the overall value of a vacation without increasing the price.

Thinking About Becoming a Travel Agent?

For many people, travel starts as a passion and eventually becomes a rewarding business opportunity. Running your own travel business offers flexibility, income potential, and the satisfaction of helping others create unforgettable experiences.

The Top 3 Advantages of Running Your Own Travel Business
1. Travel Industry Perks and Discounts

Travel professionals often gain access to industry rates, educational trips, supplier incentives, and familiarization experiences that help them learn destinations while enjoying significant savings.

These opportunities allow agents to experience products firsthand and provide better recommendations to clients.

2. Earn Income While Doing Something You Love

Many people spend their free time researching destinations, cruises, resorts, and travel trends. As a travel advisor, that passion can become a source of income.

Whether part-time or full-time, a travel business can create opportunities to earn commissions and build a growing client base while helping others fulfill their travel dreams.

3. Build a Team and Mentor Others

As your business grows, you may choose to mentor and support new travel advisors entering the industry. Helping others develop successful travel businesses can create additional opportunities for leadership, collaboration, and professional growth.

Many travel professionals find tremendous satisfaction in sharing their knowledge and helping others achieve their entrepreneurial goals.

Could a Travel Business Be Right for You?

If you love travel, enjoy helping people, and are interested in the possibility of building a flexible business, becoming a travel advisor may be worth exploring. The industry offers unique opportunities to earn income, enjoy travel-related benefits, and create meaningful experiences for clients around the world.

If you've ever considered becoming a travel agent, I'd be happy to mentor you, share insights about the industry, explain the training and resources available, and discuss how you can enjoy travel-agent perks and discounts while building your own business. You'll have the opportunity to earn income from travel sales, help clients create unforgettable vacations, and, if it's something that interests you, eventually mentor others as your business grows.

The world is full of unforgettable destinations. Helping people discover them can be one of the most rewarding journeys of all.

I did check THE facts. Here’s what they revealed:

Texas has not made any legal moves to sell Boca Chica State Park to SpaceX, and Governor Greg Abbott has stated that the issue will not be discussed anytime soon. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission has indicated that the sale is not on their agenda for the upcoming meeting.

(Is this where I insert some snarky comment like “try to keep up?)

Now I’m not trying to deny that Musk approached the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission regarding land purchases at Boca Chica. Nor am I denying that conversations are taking place. What I am saying is I think claims of him “buying Boca Chica State Park” is somewhat of a mischaracterization that is being amplified for political gain. According to published information, the acquisition in question is for disjointed tracts scattered near areas owned by SpaceX.  Further, the Commission has said it determined that the lots provide "minimal conservation and recreation value" since they're located within an existing subdivision.

This seems a little different than the prevailing narrative being pushed. We’ll see what the Abbott emails reveal … if anything.

Regarding data centers …

I like the way you sensationalized “Two days after a closed-door meeting with OpenAI, Google, and Meta …” while leaving out ALL the other participants and the ACTUAL PURPOSE of the meeting to insinuate something scurrilous regarding approvals for the participants you did mention.

The routine votes from JUST A COUPLE YEARS AGO are relevant because they are part of Hinojosa’s past record which she obfuscates and downplays when it shits on her partisan narratives.

Yes, when facts change, real leaders, like Greg Abbott, adapt. Although a big proponent of data centers, he has shifted his policy in response to what he says is the industry "digging their own grave" by failing to gain local community support.  His administration now advocates that data centers:

- Pay for their own electric infrastructure rather than shifting costs to residents.
- Bring their own water supply and disclose full usage data.
- Undergo a "comprehensive verification and audit" of power and water impacts.
- Obtain local community approval before construction begins.

Like them or not, data centers are projected to grow more than 100% in the next six years based on need and demand.   Data centers offer significant economic opportunities by generating massive capital investment, create well-paying jobs, and provide substantial tax revenue that supports local infrastructure and public services.  In fact, a recent study by the Georgia Institute of Technology found that, on average, employment rises by about 3.5%, wages by 5%, business establishments by nearly 5%, and household income by about 2% in the surrounding community after a data center opens.

Abbott wants Texans to capitalize on the economic opportunity data centers represent while maintaining a peaceful coexistence within the communities they exist.  Hinojosa is simply bad mouthing data centers for political gain because it makes a good wedge issue for partisan demagoguery in the run-up to the election.

For centuries, gold has been the ultimate "hedge." But what does that actually mean ?

A hedge is simply protection. It's an asset that tends to hold its value-or even rise-when everything else (stocks, fiat currencies) is falling. Gold has played this role for thousands of years because it is scarce, durable, and universally recognized. 

But let's be honest: the old way of owning gold as a hedge was clunky.

❌ Access: You had to find a reputable dealer.
❌ Storage: You needed a safe (and insurance) or paid for a vault.
❌ High Entry Cost: Buying a single 1oz coin requires a large upfront sum.

It wasn't practical for the average person to hedge with gold.

Enter @goldfishggbr ( $GGBR ). It solves the old problems by bringing the hedge on-chain.

Instead of buying a whole coin, GGBR lets you own 1/1000th of a troy ounce of in-situ gold. With a price point near $4.04, the barrier to entry is practically gone. You can hedge your portfolio for the price of a coffee.

Goldfish is over-collateralized beyond 100% by audited, surplus gold reserves.

You get the stability of a hard asset with the transparency of blockchain tech.

The best part ? Liquidity.

Traditional gold is illiquid—selling a bar takes time.

GGBR offers 24/7 trading on decentralized and centralized exchanges.

You get the "hedge" of gold, but with the frictionless access of crypto. No vaults, no heavy bars, just on-chain transparency.

Goldfish is more than just a token; it’s a bridge between traditional finance and DeFi.

Gold has always been a hedge against uncertainty. Goldfish just makes it accessible.

text:
Microsoft Offers Buyouts to Around 60,000 Employees to Contain Costs

Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments.

Staffers across the Windows maker would be eligible for the offers, including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, requesting anonymity as the matter was private. Units such as marketing, commercial business and security will be excluded, the source added.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said in a staff memo.

Like other tech giants, Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data centers and chips, drawing scrutiny from investors over whether the returns will justify the staggering cost. The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close on Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year.

Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, 2026, according to its annual filing.

text:
U.S. Stock Market Intraday | AI Momentum Meets the Fed and Big Tech Earnings

October 28, 2026 | 9:13 AM PT

U.S. technology stocks remain resilient, but today’s Federal Reserve decision and earnings from Google and Microsoft could determine the market’s next direction.

1. AI Chip Demand Remains Strong

SK Hynix reported record quarterly results, lifting sentiment across memory and semiconductor stocks, including MU, AMD, and ARM.

AI investment is expanding beyond GPUs into high-bandwidth memory, networking, and infrastructure. However, strong demand does not guarantee equal profitability across the sector.

2. Vertiv Delivers Impressive Results

VRT reported quarterly revenue of $4.31 billion, up 61%, with adjusted EPS rising 78% to $2.21. Adjusted free cash flow increased 50% to $652 million, while organic orders more than doubled.

These results demonstrate that AI data center spending is translating into real revenue and cash flow.

Infrastructure suppliers with strong execution may outperform highly leveraged AI cloud operators.

3. AI Leaders Face a Profitability Test

NVDA and AMD continue benefiting from computing demand, while META’s massive financing plans highlight rising capital requirements.

GOOG and MSFT report earnings after today’s close. Investors will focus on cloud growth, AI monetization, capital spending, and free cash flow.

TSLA must demonstrate commercial progress in autonomous driving and robotics to support its long-term valuation.

4. Biotech Recovery Needs Confirmation

MRNA, TWST, TXG, TEM, and MRVI remain important names to watch.

Cancer vaccines, synthetic biology, spatial genomics, and AI healthcare offer long-term opportunities, but sustainable stock performance requires commercial execution and improving fundamentals.

5. Macro Risks Are Rising

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is near 5%, gold remains above $4,000, and Bitcoin trades around $80,000.

Brent crude has climbed toward $115 amid renewed Middle East supply concerns.

High energy prices and elevated interest rates increase financing costs and pressure growth-stock valuations.

6. Today’s Key Catalysts

11:00 AM PT — Federal Reserve rate decision.

11:30 AM PT — Fed Chair Warsh’s press conference.

After market close — GOOG and MSFT earnings.

A hawkish Fed combined with disappointing AI returns could trigger renewed volatility.

Market Outlook

AI growth remains intact, but investors are changing how they value it.

The focus is shifting from aggressive capital spending to sustainable earnings, pricing power, and free cash flow.

Over the next 3–6 months, companies converting AI demand into measurable profits may outperform those relying heavily on external financing.

Key assets to watch: VRT, MU, NVDA, AMD, GOOG, MSFT, Treasury yields, and crude oil.

For research purposes only. Not investment advice.

text:
Different governments, corporations, financial institutions, security bureaucracies, and tech systems can converge on the same behavior because they face similar incentives.

Parang maraming LLMs na binigyan ng halos pare-parehong reward function. Hindi kailangan na iisang tao ang nag-type ng prompt. Pareho lang yung optimization target.

ᵗⁱⁿʸ (•☆•)📋

Imagine this chain:

1. Create or amplify instability.
War, scarcity, migration pressure, crime fear, pandemics, energy shocks, culture conflict, economic insecurity.
Not necessarily fabricated. Sometimes real events are enough.

2. Keep people psychologically overloaded.
Constant alerts, outrage, uncertainty, doom headlines, emergency language.

Now people start thinking shorter-term.
3. Offer centralized “solutions.”
More surveillance.
More emergency authority.
More dependency on a few platforms.
More debt.
More mandatory systems.
More concentration.

4. Monetize the fear.
Insurance.
Security.
Weapons.
Housing speculation.
Healthcare extraction.
Data collection.
Subscription everything.
Emergency procurement.

5. Squeeze household resilience.
Housing ↑
food ↑
healthcare ↑
education ↑
energy ↑
wages lag
Now families delay children, marriage, housing, entrepreneurship.
6. Population growth drops.
And here’s the important correction:
That does not automatically mean somebody deliberately ordered “reduce the population.”
Declining fertility can be an emergent consequence of insecurity and high living costs.
People say:

“I can barely support myself. Why would I add three children?”
And suddenly the outcome looks eerily similar to a deliberate depopulation plan even if nobody issued one.
That’s why I’d separate three hypotheses:
A. One-group command theory
One hidden network deliberately coordinating fear, extraction, and population decline.
Needs very strong evidence.
B. Coordinated blocs and institutions
Governments, firms, investors, security agencies and international bodies coordinating some policies openly or privately.
This definitely happens in specific contexts, but it does not imply one universal mastermind.
C. Convergent incentive theory
Different actors independently discover that the same tools give them more money, control, stability, market share, or political survival.
This one can create the appearance of a single script without a single scriptwriter.

And honestly, C is the one I’d investigate first.
Because if you start with:
“Who is ordering everyone?”
you may miss the more mundane machinery:
“What incentives keep producing the same behavior everywhere?”
That’s the carpet we should lift. (눈_눈)🔍
