Glenn Kessler, the Washington Post’s former chief “fact checker,” claims that there was “no Russian collusion hoax.”

IN FACT, hordes of prominent Democrats and media outlets, with help from FBI officials, falsely accused Trump of colluding with Russia to win the 2016 presidential election. Here are the specifics, straight from the primary sources:

• In the spring of 2016, a “U.S.-based international law firm” named Perkins Coie that was “acting as counsel to the Clinton campaign” hired a “U.S.-based investigative firm” named Fusion GPS to “conduct opposition research on Trump and his associates.”

• To carry out that research, Fusion GPS hired a British firm run by Christopher Steele, a “former intelligence official for the British government,” who was actively working as a “long term paid” source for the FBI.

• Using money from the DNC and Clinton campaign, Steele created a series of reports collectively known as the “Steele Dossier.”

• In these documents, Steele alleged “there was a well-developed conspiracy of co-operation between” the Trump campaign and “Russian leadership.”

• To create his dossier, Steele used sources like a former Russian government mouthpiece who Hillary Clinton called a “good friend” and “A Great Democrat,” a “public relations professional” who was a “big democratic supporter” with “extensive ties to the Kremlin and Russian government officials,” and a person who was previously investigated by the FBI on charges of spying for Russia and later admitted to fabricating allegations against Trump.

• On July 5, 2016, Steele fed his dossier to the FBI, which supposedly sat on it until September 19.

• Two weeks later on July 18, FBI Deputy Assistant Director Peter Strzok texted FBI attorney Lisa Page, “Donald Trump is an enormous d*uche.”

• One day later on July 19, Page wrote to Strzok that it was “like living in a bad dream” to watch Trump speak at the Republican National Convention.

• Three days later on July 22, WikiLeaks released a cache of damaging emails “that had been hacked” from the Democratic National Committee, leading the head of the DNC to resign.

• Three days later on July 25, famous pollster Nate Silver announced that polls were showing a major shift from Clinton to Trump, and for the first time, “Trump would be a narrow favorite, with a 57 percent chance of winning the Electoral College” if the election were “held today.”

• One day later on July 26, Hillary Clinton allegedly approved a “proposal from one of her foreign policy advisors to vilify Donald Trump by stirring up a scandal claiming interference by the Russian security services.”

• One day later on July 27, Page wrote to Strzok, “Have we opened on him yet? Trump & Putin,” followed by an “angry face” emoji.

• On the same day, Trump gave a press conference, and journalists peppered him with questions about Russia and the leak of the DNC emails. Trump repeatedly replied that he had nothing to do with Russia and stated that China, Russia, or an independent hacker has probably already hacked Hillary Clinton’s email server and should release the 30,000+ emails that Clinton destroyed after Congress ordered her to preserve them.

• The media then repeatedly took Trump’s comments out of context to make it seem like he asked Russia to hack Clinton’s emails.

• Three days later on July 31, the FBI opened a full investigation into Trump’s orbit based on “purposely vague” and “unvetted hearsay information” from two Australian diplomats in London.

• Two days later on August 2, Strzok and another FBI agent met in London to pursue the Russia collusion investigation, and the FBI’s Assistant Legal Attaché in London said that Strzok told him something along the lines of, “There’s nothing to this, but we have to run it to ground.”

• The same FBI Attaché wrote to Strzok’s partner about the evidence for the investigation, “Damn that’s thin,” and Strzok’s partner replied, “I know … it sucks.”

• Four days later on August 6, Page wrote to Strzok, “Trump should go f himself.” Strzok replied, “F Trump,” and Page replied, “And maybe you’re meant to stay where you are because you’re meant to protect the country from that menace.”

• Two days later on August 8, Page wrote to Strzok, “[Trump’s] not going to become president, right? Right?!” Strzok replied, “No. No, he’s not. We’ll stop it.”

• One week later on August 15, Strzok wrote to Page that “there’s no way” Trump “gets elected — but I’m afraid we can’t take that risk. It’s like an insurance policy in the unlikely event you die before you’re 40.”

• One month later on September 7, the CIA sent a note to Strzok and other FBI officials describing an alleged plot by Hillary Clinton to tie Trump to Russia as “a means of distracting the public from her use of a private email server,” but no one at the FBI took “any action” to investigate this matter.

• On September 19, 2016, Strzok, Page, and the rest of the FBI’s “Crossfire Hurricane” team received the Steele Dossier, which the FBI supposedly sat on for 75 days for reasons that “remain unresolved.”

• The FBI then offered Steele“$1 million or more” of taxpayer money to “produce corroboration for any of the reported allegations” in his dossier, but Steele couldn’t do so.

• The FBI also “began making regular financial payments” to Steele’s “primary sub-source,” but none of the information he provided “corroborated Steele’s reporting.”

• Despite those and other “protracted efforts” to verify the Steele Dossier, the FBI “was not able to corroborate a single substantive allegation” in it, and Steele and his sources gave materially conflicting stories about where they got their information.

• Nevertheless, the FBI and DOJ used Steele’s “unvetted and unverified” allegations to obtain four warrants to spy on Trump’s orbit. These warrant applications included “at least 17 significant errors or omissions” and “many additional errors” in procedures which “require that every factual assertion in a FISA application be ‘verified’.”

• When the FISA Court itself later examined these applications, it reported “violations of the government’s duty of candor in all four applications” and stated that these actions constituted “unlawful surveillance and search.”

• In the meantime, Steele also fed his dossier to the media and Democrats, who incessantly used it to smear Trump.

• In November 2020, Trump won the election.

• Less than one month after Trump was inaugurated in January 2017, the New York Times reported that the FBI had received “phone records and intercepted calls” from the NSA showing that “members of Donald J. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign and other Trump associates had repeated contacts with senior Russian intelligence officials in the year before the election.”

• Three years later, the U.S. Senate released an internal FBI document written by Strzok that directly refuted the Times story when it was published, but the FBI “declined to comment” on the Times’ reporting, thus letting the falsehood propagate for years.

• Four months after Trump was inaugurated, former FBI Director Robert Mueller was appointed in May 2017 as a special counsel to investigate the Russia collusion allegation, and Lisa page joined Mueller’s team.

• That same month, Strzok wrote to Page about her work on the Mueller probe and said, “God I suddenly want on this. You know why.” Page replied that she would “happily” leave Mueller’s team if Strzok wanted to join it, and Strzok responded, “I’m torn. … I’m the best for it, but there are others who can do OK.”

• Later that same month, Strzok joined Mueller’s team until he was removed in late July after his incriminating texts with Page were revealed. Page left Mueller’s team two weeks before that.

• In March 2019, more than two years after Trump’s inauguration, Mueller’s team concluded their $32 million investigation and reported that they “did not establish” or “identify evidence” that members of the “Trump Campaign” or “any U.S. persons” “conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities.”

• By the time Special Counsel John Durham later tried to interview Steele and his primary sub-source who was paid by the FBI, they were “domiciled overseas,” refused to be interviewed, and claimed that they “destroyed all notes reflecting the content of their meetings and communications.”

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — After President Trump announced a million-dollar reward for anyone who reported voter fraud, Democrats unveiled a counteroffer of one million and one dollars to not report voter fraud.

Democrats stated that restoring Americans' confidence in election integrity was of paramount importance, promising to pay whatever it took to keep fraud from being uncovered.

"Donald Trump thinks he can put a price on the integrity of our elections," said Senator Chuck Schumer. "Well, he's right. But we are offering one dollar more if you will keep your yapper shut. Remember, snitches get stitches. Well, actually, they get a million bucks. But you can get even more for keeping quiet."

In addition to the extra dollar, Democrats said their offer would involve considerably less paperwork, since recipients would never have to file a police report, testify under oath, or spend months cooperating with some tedious investigation.

The announcement sparked immediate interest from several major news organizations, which asked whether they could be paid retroactively.

"We have not reported voter fraud hundreds of times," said CNN's Anderson Cooper. "This could be a massive financial windfall for us, which we could really use. Airport lounges don't pay what they used to."

At publishing time, Democrats had announced that applicants would need to present a valid photo ID to prevent anyone from fraudulently collecting the reward.

text:
60,000 buyout offers in one day, about a quarter of the largest software company. The agentic AI layoffs just reached a new scale, and I have seen this movie twice.
⠀
In January 2000 the Y2K army went home. About $100 billion of date fixing ended on one night when nothing broke. A year later the dot-com bust took 560,000 tech jobs. Dallas lost 30 percent of its tech employment.
⠀
Both times the bust came first. Both times the boom that followed was bigger.
⠀
A Connecticut life insurer kept every one of its Y2K programmers. It formed a new unit around them and sold call center and web applications to outside clients. The unit recouped $25 million in the first year. The skill was never the date fix. It was knowing the systems.
⠀
The largest computer company of the day bet on e-business before the crash and was serving 10,000 clients by 1999. The offshore firms made the same bet from the other side. The ERP and CRM practices they built in those years became the industry I spent two decades inside.
⠀
This round is different in one way. The companies say AI out loud. The largest IT services firm cut 12,000 middle and senior roles while deploying AI at scale. One analyst told Reuters that 400,000 to 500,000 jobs are at risk over three years. A frontier lab's own data shows coding work moving from the chat window to the API, where the human is mostly absent.
⠀
So the question for IT services is not how many people to cut. It is what practice gets built now:
⠀
- an agentic AI practice, not a model practice
- the harness around the model, and the controls that let an agent act inside a regulated process
- staffed by the people who already know where the client's systems live
⠀
In my work in regulated loan origination, the people who ran the legacy integrations staffed the first agent projects. Their knowledge became the specification the agent runs against, written as intent, enforced by a hook, logged as evidence. The Y2K programmer knew the systems. The agentic AI architect knows the controls.
⠀
My flat opinion: the agentic AI layoffs of 2026 are the Y2K layoffs of 2000 with the cause stated out loud. Instructions in, results out was IT. Intent in, outcomes out is agentic AI, and somebody has to build the loop for every enterprise that cannot.
⠀
Did your firm build a new practice after the last bust?
⠀
Full post with sources: https://t.co/1vUvv5HBwi
⠀
#AgenticAI #AIGovernance

Wednesday Afternoon Check In on a Dunedin Tesla Saturday
Wednesday, October 28, 2026

10 days to go

The middle of the week is the perfect time to give your weekend something to look forward to. Tesla's at Cars & Coffee and Lunch Convoy is set for Saturday, November 7, 2026, at VFW Post 2550, 360 Douglas Ave, Dunedin, FL 34698.

Cars & Coffee kicks off at 7:30 AM and wraps at 10 AM. Breakfast from the VFW kitchen begins at 8:00 AM, and it is an amazing one, so skip the drive thru on the way in. At 9 AM the Teslas gather as a group for the inaugural EV and Tesla debut at the VFW's monthly show, and every type of vehicle is welcome to join the lineup.

Here is a chance to see the tech for yourself. Tesla owners will offer free Full Self Driving (Supervised) demos and free Actually Smart Summon demos in their own @Tesla vehicles, and they love explaining how it all works.

Kids can head straight for the playground, there are free garlic dill pickles for everyone, and the Pinellas Trail runs close by if you would like to arrive on two wheels.

Then at 10:30 AM the convoy sets off toward Honeymoon Island, a stunning @FLStateParks spot on the Gulf, for lunch at Cricketers British Pub from 11 AM to 1 PM.

Ski & Odin are hosting the morning, and coming out helps support VFW Post 2550. @teslabrosclub, a ten day head start is plenty of time to fill the convoy.

RSVP free during your afternoon break: scan the QR code in the picture, or type Tesla's at Cars & Coffee and Lunch Convoy into the Eventbrite search bar.

text:
Universal Health Services: Former Fox Run Center CEO arrested on federal charges involving 17-year-old former Fox Run patient

Randall J. MacKendrick, 59, of St. Clairsville, Ohio, the former CEO of Fox Run Center for Children and Adolescents, was arrested by federal agents in West Virginia on October 24, 2026, on federal charges of possessing child pornography and attempted coercion and enticement of a minor—a 17-year-old former patient at the facility.

Fox Run Center is a psychiatric residential treatment center owned by Universal Health Services, a for-profit hospital chain infamous for putting profit ahead of patient care and safety.

MacKendrick was previously arrested on similar state-level charges.

In June 2026, MacKendrick contacted a North Ridgeville (Ohio) Police Department officer operating undercover on a web-based chat site and posing as a 14-year-old girl. Over the following months, MacKendrick allegedly sent sexually explicit messages, identified himself as “Rick,” provided a telephone number linked to a TextNow account, offered gifts, and repeatedly sought an in-person meeting. He traveled to central Ohio in July and visited locations including Polaris Shopping Center, Tanger Outlets, and a Holiday Inn where he believed the girl was staying. On August 28, he drove to South Central Park in North Ridgeville for a planned meeting and was arrested after leaving the area. Officers found multiple vibrating sex toys, condoms, and three cell phones in his vehicle. He was charged in Lorain County with importuning, disseminating matter harmful to juveniles, attempted unlawful conduct with a minor, and possessing criminal tools.

Search warrants executed on MacKendrick’s Fox Run office and his St. Clairsville residence in late August yielded USB drives containing more than 30 images and 8 videos of nude prepubescent children engaged in sexual acts or lascivious displays, previously identified by the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children as known child sexual abuse material.

While released on bond in the state case, MacKendrick was re-arrested in September after authorities learned of prohibited contact with a minor. His bond was increased and he was later released again. In October, the FBI identified him as a suspect in a separate May 2026 Perry County investigation involving the kidnapping and rape of a 14-year-old girl; a CODIS hit linked his DNA to evidence recovered from the victim. That investigation remains ongoing. Universal Health Services previously stated that MacKendrick no longer worked for the company as of late August.

Sources: “Federal agents arrest former CEO of child & adolescent residential treatment center on federal child pornography, coercion charges,” US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Ohio, October 26, 2026 and Affidavit in Support of Criminal Complaint in the matter of USA v. MacKendrick, case no. 2:26-mj-664, US District Court Southern District of Ohio, filed Oct. 23, 2026.

text:
House Democrats Release Report Calling Trump an Active Participant in Epstein’s Abuse of Young Women

Breaking Points hosts Ryan Grim and Emily Jashinsky examine a newly released House Democratic report that compiles allegations against Donald Trump tied to Jeffrey Epstein. The document states that a growing body of evidence shows Trump was an active participant in Epstein’s sexual abuse of young women in the mid-to-late 1990s. It draws on accounts from eleven women, some previously public and some newly detailed, and argues that the Justice Department and FBI under the current administration have worked to keep the full record from public view. Democrats are now calling for a special counsel to investigate the ties.

The report’s central claim is that Trump abused, assaulted, and in some cases raped women in coordination with Epstein. One of the more significant new elements comes from Beatrice Coul, a Swiss model who previously alleged groping. She now states that in 1993, at a Trump pageant event involving girls and young women aged 16 to 22, Trump raped her in a hotel suite after promising help with a visa and admission to NYU. According to her account, he tore her dress, caused bleeding and bruising, then told her the show must go on and that she should keep quiet. Another woman listed in the report, Jill Hearth, described a pattern of Trump contacting models after competitions with offers of career advancement in exchange for sexual favors. The document also notes Virginia Giuffre’s earlier statement that she was recruited by Ghislaine Maxwell at Mar-a-Lago.

These are serious allegations drawn from a partisan report. They restate and expand on claims that have circulated for years, some of which appeared shortly before the 2024 election. No court has adjudicated them, and Trump has long denied involvement in Epstein’s crimes beyond a social relationship that ended decades ago. The report’s authors treat the pattern of proximity, shared locations, and overlapping promises to young women as evidence of active participation rather than mere acquaintance. They also criticize the current DOJ for what they describe as efforts to dismiss or ignore relevant evidence.

The call for a special counsel follows directly from the document. Whether that step produces new facts, corroboration, or further denials will determine how much weight the public ultimately assigns to the allegations. For now, the report places the most detailed collection yet of these claims in one place and asks whether the long-documented relationship between Trump and Epstein included participation in the abuse itself.

text:
Texans added my top available RB, Emari Demercado according to @AaronWilson_NFL

He's been one of the most efficient low-volume runners in the league for three years (6.5 yards a carry on 126 carries), he returns kicks, and he blocks. He is not a replacement for David Montgomery. He's the third back the Texans didn't have, and the move says the front office isn't spending a pick on the position.

WHO HE IS
5'9", 215, age 27. Navy was his only D-I offer out of high school, so he went JUCO (1,026 yards at Saddleback), then five years at TCU mostly behind Kendre Miller, plus a master's degree. He ran for 150 yards against Michigan in the 2022 playoff after Miller got hurt. Undrafted in 2023, Brugler's RB34. Three seasons in Arizona behind James Conner. Testing: 4.49 forty, 80th-percentile agility, 26th-percentile burst. Thick and quick, without a big second gear.

THE 2026 PATH
Four teams in seven months. KC signed him in March and cut him at final cuts. Dallas claimed him to play for Klayton Adams, his old Cardinals line coach, then scratched him four times in seven weeks, waived him Oct 8, re-signed him Oct 13, and waived him again Oct 27. Five carries all year. That's a crowded room, not a verdict on him.

THE NUMBERS (chart below)
20 of his 126 Arizona carries went 10+ yards, a 15.9% rate. The one stretch where he carried a real load, two games after Conner's 2023 knee injury, he went 33 for 136 (4.1), with an 84.4 PFF rushing grade and 2.82 yards after contact. Pass protection is the skill nobody mentions: 8 pressures allowed on 104 pass-block snaps in Arizona. 50 catches, 6.5 a catch, an outlet, not a weapon. One fumble in 131 carries.

THE PLAY EVERYONE REMEMBERS
Week 5, 2025: a 72-yard run against Tennessee, let go of the ball before the goal line, touchback, Arizona blew a 21-6 lead. Gannon lit him up and was fined $100K for it. Demercado: "I made a mistake, really no excuse. I've just got to be better." A month later he slid down in bounds on a 19-yard run to ice a game against Dallas. One lapse, owned.

WHY HE FITS
He's the scheme's complement back almost to the letter: 205-215, one-cut, runs through arm tackles, and trustworthy on third down because of the pass pro. Three years in Arizona's gap-heavy run game (Bam Knight's split there was 72% gap in 2025) in an offense that's about 51% gap here. He makes the most of few touches, which is the job behind Marks and Montgomery. He returns kicks, a path to a helmet that doesn't depend on carries. And he cost nothing.

WHY HE DOESN'T
He's not a lead back. Career high is 58 carries. The one time he had to carry it, the efficiency came down to 4.1. The burst is average; the home runs came when the daylight was there. The receiving is a checkdown. Three teams passed in seven months. And he overlaps Marks: two complement backs, still no 230-pound hammer. If Montgomery goes on IR, the lead-back hole is as open as it was Tuesday morning.

WHAT IT MEANS
Bye-week claim, cheap, controlled, versatile, no commitment past March. Pure Caserio. At 2-5 with the deadline 13 days out, Houston isn't spending picks on a back. Noel's IR move opened the spot, so no RB was cut. The room: Marks, Demercado, Ogunbowale on the 53; Montgomery still not practicing since Oct 11; Jordan and Whittington on PS-injured; Vaughn on the PS.

text:
① Don't retire in NEW YORK CITY 🗽, choose → PITTSBURGH 🇺🇸 → Trade sky-high rent for much more affordable housing without giving up major hospitals, museums, restaurants, or cultural life. New York is amazing when you're earning a great salary. But once you stop working, making your money last matters more than living among skyscrapers.

② Don't retire in SAN FRANCISCO 🌉, choose → LANCASTER 🇺🇸 → A Pennsylvania city with markets, historic neighborhoods, and a much slower pace of life. San Francisco has tech, opportunities, and huge salaries. But when you're no longer building a career, paying Silicon Valley prices loses much of its appeal.

③ Don't retire in MIAMI 🌴, choose → GAINESVILLE 🇺🇸 → You're still in Florida, with mild winters, a college-town atmosphere, hospitals, and nature nearby. Miami has beaches, restaurants, and an international vibe, but also traffic, expensive housing, and insurance costs that can make retirement difficult. Gainesville isn't immune to heat or severe weather, but it offers a different pace of life.

④ Don't retire in PHOENIX 🌵, choose → PRESCOTT 🇺🇸 → Stay in Arizona, but at a higher elevation with generally less extreme summers. Phoenix can be attractive in winter, but imagine spending much of the summer avoiding the outdoors because of the heat. Prescott offers mountains, hiking trails, and a quieter lifestyle. Just remember to factor in wildfire risks.

⑤ Don't retire in HONOLULU 🌺, choose → LINCOLN 🇺🇸 → Trade Hawaii's beaches for a Nebraska city with parks, amenities, and more affordable housing. Honolulu looks like the perfect retirement destination until you add up housing, groceries, and everyday expenses. Lincoln doesn't have the ocean or tropical weather, but it can give you something just as important: more financial freedom to enjoy retirement.

text:
MANY ARE CALLED, BUT FEW ARE CHOSEN. WHY?

for many are called, but few are chosen.”  Matthew 22:14
There is a sobering truth in the Word of God that I believe we need to stop and truly consider. Many are called, but few are chosen. Many hear the gospel. Many sit in church pews. Many raise their hands in worship, profess the name of Jesus, and speak of their love for God. But how many are truly willing to surrender everything to Him?
We love to talk about the goodness of God. We love to talk about His promises, His blessings, His favor, and His grace. And rightfully so! But what happens when following Jesus requires us to lay something down? What happens when obedience means telling our flesh no? What happens when the Lord asks us to walk away from something we love, surrender a desire we have been holding onto, or separate ourselves from the very things the world celebrates?
That is where the cost of discipleship becomes real.
Jesus said in Luke 9:23, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.”
Notice that Jesus said DAILY!...
Not just on Sunday morning. Not just when we feel the presence of God. Not just when life is falling apart and we need Him to rescue us.

Daily.

We must make a conscious decision to deny ourselves, crucify the desires of the flesh, and submit our lives to the authority of Jesus Christ.
God's calling is an invitation, but we must not confuse hearing the invitation with faithfully answering it.
In Matthew 22, Jesus gave the parable of the wedding feast. Many were invited, yet some refused to come. Others treated the invitation lightly. The parable reveals the tragedy of being invited into something glorious while allowing other things to take priority.
And I wonder how many people are doing the same thing today.
God calls, but we are too busy.
God convicts, but we make excuses.
God draws us closer, but the world still has our attention.
God asks for our surrender, but we want to remain in control.
We want the crown without the cross. We want the promises without the obedience. We want the presence of God without making room for Him in our daily lives.
But beloved, we cannot expect to walk in the fullness of what God has for us while deliberately holding on to everything He is asking us to surrender.
We cannot keep one foot in the world and one foot in the church and expect to walk wholeheartedly with Jesus.
James 4:4 gives a serious warning about friendship with the world that places us in opposition to God. And Romans 12:2 tells us not to be conformed to this world, but to be transformed by the renewing of our minds.
This does not mean we withdraw from every person who does not believe as we do. Jesus Himself ministered among sinners. It means we refuse to let the world's values, appetites, and rebellious ways shape our hearts more than the Word of God does.
We are called to be in the world without belonging to its ways.

And let us be honest about something elseour flesh will not discipline itself.
If we wait until we feel like praying, we may rarely pray. If we wait until we feel like reading the Word, we may continually find something else to do. If we allow every appetite, distraction, and desire to dictate our decisions, our spiritual lives will suffer.
First Corinthians 9:27 speaks of Paul disciplining his body and bringing it into subjection. And Galatians 5:16 tells us to walk in the Spirit so that we will not fulfill the lust of the flesh.
There must be discipline in our walk with God.
There must be a willingness to rise early, turn off the television, put down the phone, quiet the noise, and seek the face of the Lord. There must be moments when we choose prayer over entertainment, Scripture over distraction, obedience over convenience, and the eternal over the temporary.
Not because we are trying to earn God's love, but because we recognize the immeasurable value of knowing Him.
Psalm 63:1 declares, O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee.”
What a beautiful picture of a heart that longs for God!
And while Scripture does not command every believer to wake at a particular hour, it does call us to seek Him wholeheartedly. Whether it is early in the morning, in the quiet hours of the night, or in the middle of an ordinary day, we must make room for Him.
God deserves more than whatever scraps of our attention remain after we have given the world our best hours.
w.e must nourish our spirit, because whatever we continually feed will influence the condition of our heart.
If we continually feed our flesh while neglecting our spirit, we should not be surprised when the things of God begin to feel distant. Prayer becomes a burden. The Bible becomes a book we rarely open. Conviction becomes an inconvenience. Sin becomes easier to excuse.
And if we continue down that road, we put ourselves in a spiritually dangerous place.
First Timothy 4:1–2 speaks of people who depart from the faith and have their consciences seared as with a hot iron.
Think about that imagery.
A conscience that has been seared has become hardened. Something that once would have caused alarm no longer produces the same response. The warnings that once troubled the heart can eventually be ignored.
This is one reason we must never treat conviction lightly.
Every time the Lord corrects us, we have an opportunity to humble ourselves. Every time His Word exposes something in us, we can repent and allow Him to change us. But if we continually resist His correction, we risk becoming increasingly insensitive to the very voice that is calling us back to Him.
Hebrews 3:15 says, to day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
Do not harden your heart.
do not silence conviction.
Do not continually postpone obedience.
Do not mistake God's patience for approval.
Do not assume that because you still attend church, your spiritual life must be healthy.
God is not merely interested in our outward appearance. He desires truth in the inward parts (Psalm 51:6).
He sees the private life. He sees what we entertain when no one is watching. He sees the battles we fight, the compromises we excuse, and the sacrifices we make to obey Him.
And He sees the heart that genuinely desires to please Him, even when the struggle is difficult.
I want to be clear: we do not become chosen because we have earned God's favor through perfect performance, nor does struggling with temptation automatically mean we are rejected. We are saved by grace through faith, not by works (Ephesians 2:8–9). But the grace that saves us also calls us into a life of good works, obedience, and transformation (Ephesians 2:10).
Jesus said in John 14:15, if ye love me, keep my commandments.”
Obedience is not the price we pay to make God love us. It is the fruit of a heart that loves Him.
So when we talk about being among the few who are chosen, we must remember that Scripture uses this language in different contexts. In Matthew 22, it appears at the conclusion of the wedding feast parable, and we should not reduce that passage to a simple formula that says only the most disciplined people earn salvation. The Lord knows those who are His.
But the warning remains..do not take His invitation lightly.
Do not let the cares of this life choke out the Word. Do not let the pleasures of this world become more precious to you than the presence of God. Do not become so comfortable in religion that you forget the necessity of a surrendered heart.
Jesus also said in Matthew 7:21
Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”
Those words should cause every one of us to examine our hearts—not to live in constant terror, but to make certain our profession of faith is accompanied by a genuine desire to follow the Lord.
Are we seeking Him when nobody is watching?
Are we willing to obey when obedience costs us something?
Are we putting to death the deeds of the body through the Spirit (Romans 8:13)?
Are we making time for prayer, the Word, worship, and fellowship with other believers?
Are we quick to repent when the Lord corrects us, or have we become skilled at explaining away our disobedience?
These are questions worth asking.

I do not want to be a woman who merely knows how to speak Christian language. I want to know Jesus. I want my life to reflect His character. I want my heart to remain tender toward His correction. I want to be faithful in the hidden places, where there is no applause, no audience, and no recognition from people.
Because the secret place matters.
The unseen sacrifice matters.
The private prayer matters.
The quiet decision to say no to sin matters.
And the willingness to surrender, day after day, matters.
Beloved, let us stop looking for the bare minimum we can do and still call ourselves Christians. Let us ask the Lord to give us hearts that hunger and thirst after righteousness (Matthew 5:6).
Let us seek Him with our whole hearts (Jeremiah 29:13). Let us run our race with endurance (Hebrews 12:1). Let us present our bodies as living sacrifices, holy and acceptable to God (Romans 12:1).
Many are called, but few are chosen. May we never be so distracted by the things of this world that we neglect the One who has called us.
May we be willing to surrender what He asks us to surrender, forsake what He asks us to forsake, and obey when He tells us to move.
Not for the praise of men.
Not to appear more righteous than someone else.
Not to earn what only grace can give.
But because Jesus Christ is worthy of our whole lives.
He did not give Himself halfway for us. May we not offer Him a halfhearted surrender in return.
📷
lord, deliver us from a form of godliness that has no power. Awaken our hearts. Teach us to discipline our flesh, prioritize Your presence, love Your Word, and obey Your voice. Keep our consciences tender and our spirits hungry for righteousness. Let us never become so comfortable with this world that we lose our desire for You. And when our race is finished, may we be found faithful. In Jesus' name, amen

text:
Anchor: “there are new numbers out in some of the most closely watched races that could decide who takes power in the u.s. senate. this one may offer another round of serious warning signs for republicans, especially in south carolina, a red state for sure. the new york times/siena poll that was just out this morning finds the race between the democratic candidate for senate, annie andrews, and republican, darlene graham, the sister of the late lindsey graham, that that race is now a toss-up. i mean, couldn’t be more toss-up in this race. no clear leader, obviously. maybe less surprising, another race that they’re looking at this morning, the race in florida. republican there, senator ashley moody, holding a six-point lead over angie nixon right now among likely voters. and in minnesota, the new york times says that this might be the most surprising one of all, though they also call it an outlier. the democratic candidate, peggy flanagan, up by 14 points over republican michelle tafoya on this poll. no other nonpartisan poll has found flanagan leading by more than four points since labor day, so hold on to that one just as an outlier. john? with us now, anchor of the lead and cnn chief washington correspondent, jake tapper, good morning to you, sir. i’ve got this poll from south carolina up on my screen here showing a dead heat. and polls do tell us a lot, but there are things beyond polls, i think, that you like to look at about what candidates are saying, where they’re going, what they’re doing, that can somehow be equally as instructive, maybe more so, as to which way races are headed. what are you seeing out there and looking for?”

Jake Tapper: “so a few things. one, if any of our viewers out there are skeptical of public polls, they’ve been burned before, et cetera, you’re not alone. public polls are great little snapshots, but they are not predictors of anything. and so what i tend to do is look at what the politicians are doing, where they’re going, and where they’re spending their money. so for example, president trump, when it comes to south carolina and that race showing it neck and neck between darlene graham and dr. annie andrews, president trump was in south carolina last week in pendleton, and he’s going back to south carolina tomorrow to rock hill. that says to me that the race is tight. that says to me that president trump thinks he needs to go out there and actually get his people to the polls. when he says pretend i’m on the ballot, he means it. he’s talking to those low propensity voters that turn out for him and tend to sit out the midterms. it’s the same reason why he went to michigan to clare county. that’s a county that he won by more than 30 points, i think. but remember two years ago when mike rogers, the current senate nominee in michigan, ran and lost, more than 100,000 people voted for trump and didn’t vote for him at all. so trump, again, trying to rally his people to the polls. so that’s the first thing i look at. where are the big dogs going? likewise, obama went to detroit. you just had— sarah just had a long conversation about the black vote and the democratic candidates, abdul el-sayed’s difficulty getting black voters to support him, to trust him. that’s why obama was in detroit. normally, two weeks before an election, one week before an election, michigan should not be a place that a democrat has to go, like obama, and south carolina should not be a place that a republican has to go, like trump. so that’s one thing i’m looking at. the second thing i look at—”

Anchor: “yeah, just to point out, jake, let me just point out. i can point out where you’re talking about here. this is wayne county. this is detroit, where president obama was. and you can see, this is a county that kamala harris won by 29 points last time. and just to put some meat on the bones, what you’re talking about, clare county, absolutely. clare county, a county he won by 38 points. donald trump did just two years ago. so going to campaign at a place where he did very, very well. i didn’t mean to interrupt, but i just wanted to show people what you’re talking about there.”

Jake Tapper: “no. no, it’s great. but i mean, that’s the point, is you look where they’re going. and the fact that mike rogers is not distancing himself from trump, even though you and i know mike rogers— he used to be a commentator on cnn. before that, he was a member of congress, chairman of the house intelligence committee. he is generally a more moderate kind of republican. but that’s not how he’s campaigning. he’s campaigning as a maga republican. and his strategy is to get the trump people to vote for him. when trump says, pretend i’m on the ballot, that’s what he means. and mike rogers is saying, yes, absolutely. that’s my ticket to winning. the other thing to look at is, where are the politicians who have access to much more intense voter data than public polls do? where are they putting money? and where are they taking money out of? when the republicans take money out of the congressional district of tom kean jr. in new jersey, when they take money out of the republican senate race in north carolina or georgia, that is a vote of no confidence. and then when they send it to kansas or they send it to south carolina, again, that is saying, oh my god, we need to buck up these people in traditionally republican states. and we need to make sure that they have everything they need, because this race is tighter than i thought. same thing with democrats sending money to michigan or to maine. and then the last thing, john, is i look at, who is acting desperate? who is making wild, crazy accusations? trump calling abdul el-sayed a jihadist or saying he’d asked to go through a metal detector to get onto the floor of the senate. these are last minute fear mongering plays that suggest that they’re not confident in competing on an actual battleground of ideas. so those are the three things i look at. but ultimately, as i’m sure you are the same way, when it comes to election night, i have no idea what’s going to happen. i’m not counting on one result or another. it will all be up to the voters. and it’s actually one of the most exciting things to cover, because the polls are away, and the pundits are away, and the predictions are away. and it’s just actually real people casting their ballots.”

text:
$GRBK Q3 2026 earnings: Green Brick home orders edge up, but discounts cut profit

Green Brick Partners, a homebuilder focused on Texas and the Southeast, sold slightly more homes by offering bigger discounts while its profit shrank. Total revenue fell 9% from a year ago as lower average selling prices outweighed a 3% increase in both home deliveries and new orders. Co-chief executive Jim Brickman said buyer incentives on new orders rose to 11%, which pulled homebuilding gross margin down to 28%.

• Total revenue: $𝟒𝟒𝟖𝐌 (-8.8% from a year ago)
• Homebuilding gross margin: 𝟐𝟖.𝟎% (32.1% a year ago (-4.1 percentage points))
• Net new home orders: 𝟗𝟐𝟔 𝐡𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐬 (+3.1% from a year ago; incentives at 11%)
• Profit per share: $𝟏.𝟑𝟓 (-23.7% from a year ago)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The story got worse because last quarter's order rebound faded and cost more in discounts than before. Second-quarter orders did not turn into higher third-quarter closings, while heavy land spending pushed net homebuilding debt up from 6.1% to 9.6% of capital. One bright spot: the in-house mortgage unit grew operating profit 69% from a year ago and buybacks picked up.

The question now is whether Green Brick's self-developed Texas land lots can hold gross margin near 28% while 11% order discounts flow through future closings. Either self-developed lots absorb the rate buydowns, or rising inventory and Texas concentration squeeze margins and cash flow further. Fourth-quarter gross margin and the filing's land spending numbers will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐈𝐧-𝐇𝐨𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐠𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐰 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐋𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫
Green Brick's financial services arm provides mortgages, title services and insurance to its homebuyers. Co-chief executive Jed Dolson said "Green Brick Mortgage continued to increase its capture in our core Texas markets", meaning a larger share of buyers used the builder's own lender.

Segment revenue rose 51.9% from a year ago to $11.2 million as loan originations grew 42.2% to 499 loans. Operating profit in the unit climbed 68.9% to $5.6 million, and nine-month profit nearly doubled to $15.6 million.

That growth matters because mortgage income helps offset a 24.0% drop in overall company net income. Still, sequential momentum stalled, as loan volume slipped 4.2% by our math from 521 loans in the second quarter. The earnings release also omitted the exact buyer capture rate and gave no update on the planned rollout to Atlanta.

What to watch: the mortgage capture rate and Atlanta rollout status in the third-quarter filing. A capture rate stuck near the second quarter's 66% would leave the unit short of its 70% year-end target.

🟢 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐏𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐔𝐩 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐕𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞 𝐑𝐨𝐬𝐞
Green Brick slowed its stock buybacks in the first half of 2026 to pay for land, spending $16.6 million across the first two quarters combined. In the third quarter, the Dallas-Fort Worth homebuilder stepped up its repurchases again while also paying off maturing debt.

The builder bought back 264,215 shares for about $17.9 million, nearly matching its entire first-half total. It also retired $50 million of 4.00% senior notes that came due in August 2026, and book value per share (stockholders' equity divided by shares) rose 14% from a year ago to $46.10.

What to watch: fourth-quarter share repurchases against credit line borrowings. Another step-up in buybacks while credit lines remain drawn would mean the company is funding stock purchases with debt.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐏𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧
To keep homes selling when mortgage rates are high, Green Brick offers buyer incentives such as price discounts and mortgage-rate buydowns, where the builder pays upfront to lower a buyer's monthly rate. Co-chief executive Jim Brickman said the results show the ability of its operators to "balance price, pace and profitability as market conditions evolve".

The numbers show profitability giving way to sales pace. Incentives on new orders jumped to a level "elevated at 11%", up from 9.0% in the second quarter and 8.9% a year ago, while homebuilding gross margin fell to 28.0%.

• Homebuilding gross margin: 28.0%, down 4.1 percentage points from 32.1% a year ago and down 1.8 points from the second quarter
• Cost of residential units: 72.0% of residential revenue, up 4.1 percentage points from a year ago by our math
• Sales pace per community: 8.5 orders for the quarter (2.8 per month), down from 10.0 in the second quarter

Because accounting rules deduct closing-cost incentives directly from revenue, those 11% discounts shrink the top line while land and construction costs stay fixed. Even with bigger discounts, monthly sales per community still slowed, cutting third-quarter profit per share by 23.7% to $1.35.

What to watch: fourth-quarter homebuilding gross margin as the third quarter's 11% order incentives turn into home closings. A drop below 28.0% would show that rate buydowns are eroding profit faster than self-developed land lots can protect it.

🔴🔴 𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝
Last quarter, net new home orders jumped 18.8% from a year earlier to 1,079 homes, raising hopes that a big wave of speculatively built homes (houses started before a buyer signs a contract) would lift third-quarter closings. In the third quarter, Brickman said, "We continue to respond to deteriorating market conditions to maintain sales pace."

Order growth cooled to 3.1% from a year ago at 926 homes, and the dollar value of those new orders fell 1.1% to $428.9 million. Worse, the second quarter's order surge did not turn into a third-quarter delivery surge: home deliveries fell 6.6% from the second quarter by our math to 978 units, up 2.6% from a year ago.

Active selling communities also dipped from 106 in June to 104 at the end of September, running against management's earlier plan to grow community count toward year-end. With deliveries exceeding new orders by 52 homes by our math, the builder is working through its order book without getting a volume boost.

What to watch: fourth-quarter net new orders and ending community count. A decline in orders or a community count stuck at 104 would confirm that the second-quarter order jump was a one-off spike driven by discounts.

🔴 𝐋𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐠
Trophy Signature Homes, Green Brick's entry-level builder in Texas, sells smaller, lower-priced houses than the group's other brands. Both co-chief executives credited Trophy for keeping buyer demand steady, which is the bull case for the brand, but its larger share of sales and heavier buyer discounts are pulling average home prices down.

• Average price of delivered homes: $446,700, down 12.1% from $508,100 a year ago
• Average price of new home orders: $463,200, down 4.1% from $483,100 a year ago
• Backlog (homes under contract but not yet closed): 629 homes worth $379.3 million, down 6.8% in units and 17.0% in dollar value from a year ago

Because the average delivered price fell 12.1% while unit deliveries rose 2.6%, residential units revenue dropped 9.7% to $437.0 million. Even though the average price of homes in backlog remains higher at $603,100, that figure is down 10.9% from a year ago, so the price drag on revenue has not ended.

What to watch: the gap between the average price of new orders and delivered homes next quarter. Order prices at $463,200 sit slightly above delivered prices at $446,700, so holding that level would slow the revenue decline.

🔴 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐔𝐩
Green Brick buys and develops its own land lots rather than relying on third-party developers, a strategy bulls view as a long-term cost advantage as Brickman vowed to "continue to invest through the current down-cycle". Yet heavy land spending during an earnings drop is now absorbing cash, raising debt and deepening the builder's reliance on Texas.

• Real estate inventory: $2.34 billion, up 11.4% ($239.3 million) since year-end 2025 by our math
• Owned lots: 40,869, up 11.4% from a year ago; Texas holds 92.5% of all 51,435 lots owned and under contract by our math
• Net homebuilding debt (debt minus cash): $214.4 million, or 9.6% of capital, up from $127.8 million (6.1%) in the second quarter
• Quarter-end liquidity (cash plus available credit): $325 million, down 29.6% from $461.6 million in the second quarter by our math

To fund inventory growth, retire $50 million of notes and buy back stock, the company drew $103.1 million on its credit lines after having no net borrowings in June. Meanwhile, owned lots in the Southeast (Atlanta and Florida) fell 8.9% since year-end to 2,155, leaving even more capital tied to a single state.

What to watch: operating cash flow and year-to-date land spending in the third-quarter filing. Those figures will show how much of the $850 million full-year land budget remains for the fourth quarter.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚𝐝𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟏.𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Overhead and selling costs fell 6.3% from $55.2 million a year ago and dropped from $54.4 million in the second quarter. However, because homebuilding revenue shrank faster, overhead rose to 11.8% of residential units revenue by our math, up 0.4 percentage points from 11.4% a year ago and up from 11.3% in the second quarter.

𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟖.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Upfront cash deposits from homebuyers and lot buyers rose 5.9% from $26.4 million in the second quarter and 8.8% from $25.7 million at year-end 2025 by our math, though they remain 20.5% below the $35.2 million held a year ago. Higher sequential deposits alongside 28.6% refundable lot contracts help limit balance-sheet risk if demand weakens further.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟒𝟑.𝟐𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Weighted average diluted shares fell 1.0% from 43.63 million a year ago by our math and edged down from 43.28 million in the second quarter. The lower share count reflects $34.5 million of stock buybacks across the first nine months of 2026 by our math, which cushioned diluted profit per share by 0.3 percentage points compared to net income.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞: 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from FY26 land acquisitions ~$400M; land development ~$450M; mortgage capture >70%
Unchanged. Green Brick does not issue quarterly revenue, profit or margin targets in its earnings releases, and co-chief executive Jim Brickman reiterated that the company will "continue to invest through the current down-cycle". Earlier 2026 targets for $400 million in land acquisitions, $450 million in land development and a 70% mortgage capture rate are normally updated on the conference call.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬?
Second-quarter net new orders reached 1,079 units, yet third-quarter deliveries fell sequentially from 1,047 to 978 homes while homes under construction held steady at 2,181. Did construction cycle times lengthen, or did fewer buyers close on speculatively built homes within the quarter?

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Owned lots in the Southeast (Atlanta and Florida) dropped 8.9% since year-end to 2,155, following a 27% year-over-year revenue drop in the second quarter. What did the region deliver in third-quarter revenue and pretax income in the quarterly filing?

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐠𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Management said Green Brick Mortgage increased its capture in Texas, but loan originations fell sequentially from 521 to 499 and the exact percentage was not in the release. What was the capture rate, and has the Atlanta mortgage rollout begun?

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟖𝟓𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐛𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐭?
Real estate inventory rose $239 million year to date and the builder drew $103 million on its credit lines in the third quarter. How much did Green Brick spend on land acquisition and development in the third quarter, and is the full-year budget unchanged?

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐲 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐩 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟖.𝟎% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧?
Warranty reserve adjustments added 0.6 percentage points to gross margin in the second quarter of 2026 and 0.9 points in the third quarter of 2025. How much warranty accrual was released or charged inside the third quarter's 28.0% homebuilding gross margin?

text:
This Monday, in a Tampa courtroom, Robert Kessler, 74 and blind, offered to plead guilty to first-degree murder in exchange for a Philly cheesesteak, fries and a Pepsi. He specified onions, mayonnaise, and that the drink had to be twenty ounces. First-degree murder in Florida carries life with no parole.

In the video below he lays out his terms in open court, and the judge tells him why he cannot have them.

Said he had never seen his own discovery and had never read the charges. Said he knew murder carried life. Said he did not know what the other charge carried.

Said he was in the dark. So to speak.

Robert Kessler is charged with first-degree murder and abuse of a dead human body. Prosecutors say Stephanie Crone-Overholts, 47, was killed at his home on 5 November 2021 and that her remains were thrown into McKay Bay. She was from Erie, Pennsylvania.

He has been in the Hillsborough County jail for five years waiting for this trial.

He refused to change out of his jail uniform. The judge warned him the jury would read the name of the jail on his back. Said let them know he has been there five years.

Two doctors once found him incompetent. The court held a hearing and found him competent. His own lawyer had him evaluated again last week, and that evaluator agreed he was competent to proceed.

He chose to represent himself anyway. The judge took him through the standard questions. Seventy-four. High school in Pennsylvania. No college. No law courses. Never represented himself in anything, not even a traffic ticket.

The judge told him it was a bad idea. He said he understood. He did it anyway.

Then he made the offer.

The judge said he had worked almost forty years and had never heard that request before. Said he could guarantee Kessler lunch. Said he could not guarantee what it would be. Said handing a defendant a particular meal to buy a guilty plea would be wrong in a thousand ways.

He offered a different route instead, with a cap on the sentence, and floated thirty years. Then he pointed out that at seventy-four, thirty years and life are the same thing.

Kessler withdrew the offer and asked to pick a jury.

He said he wanted the cheese sandwich. Said if he got the sandwich he would have gone for it. Said he was not going to get it, so fine.

While that was happening, the prosecutor asked for a few minutes to call the victim's family. They were travelling to the trial. She thought they might be on a plane.

He has not been convicted of anything.

You are the judge. A man facing life offers you a guilty plea in exchange for a sandwich. Do you take it?

text:
🚨Florida Murder Defendant Offers to Plead Guilty in Exchange for Philly Cheesesteak and a Pepsi

Robert Lee Kessler, a 74 year old legally blind Florida man, offered to plead guilty to first degree murder in exchange for a Philly cheesesteak, fries, and a Pepsi.  

​The unusual exchange unfolded in a Tampa courthouse during jury selection in State of Florida v. Robert Lee Kessler.  

Kessler is on trial for first degree murder and abuse of a dead human body in connection with the 2021 dismemberment death of Stephanie Crone Overholts, whose remains were discovered in McKay Bay.  

The presiding judge flatly rejected the proposal, stating that in nearly 40 years on the bench, he had never heard such a request and noted that exchanging a meal for a plea agreement would be "wrong in a thousand ways". 

The judge offered to ensure Kessler received standard lunch that day, but denied the specific menu order.  

​Outcome: Following the judge's refusal, Kessler replied, "Just pick the jury," and trial proceedings moved forward.

The trial comes after nearly five years of legal delays centered around questions regarding Kessler's mental fitness and severe visual impairment. 

Just weeks prior to jury selection, the judge denied a motion to dismiss the charges based on Kessler's blindness.

This happened on Monday, October 27, 2026, during the start of jury selection for the trial in a Tampa, Florida courtroom.
  
​If convicted of first degree murder, Kessler faces a mandatory sentence of life in prison without parole.

text:
It was botched.  They misjudged (a) how much Tier 1 and Tier 2 TV rights would climb in value, and (b) the acceleration of cord-cutting.

The Big Ten's Tier 1 & 2 TV rights (i.e. Fox, CBS, NBC, FS1, Peacock, et al) have more than doubled in the last 10 years.  At the same time, the # of households with the BTN has shrunk.  As such, Tier 1 & 2 TV rights account for a significantly larger share of the B1G's TV revenue.

The #1 driver of what a conference can sell their game inventory for is matchups, b/c matchups drive viewership.  The better matchups you offer, the more $$$ a network will pay.  Every time Ohio St, Michigan, Penn St, Oregon, USC, Iowa, Nebraska, or Wisconsin play Maryland or Rutgers, that's a game they don't play against each other.  And as such, it's a significant loss of viewership.  

While there is no doubt Rutgers & Maryland (especially Rutgers) deliver sizable carriage fees for the BTN, those financial gains pale in comparison to the losses the Big Ten suffers from having Maryland & Rutgers drag down 17-18 Big Ten games per year.  The larger a conference is, the less often the most-watched brands play.  And the less often the most-watched brands play, the less $$$ a conference's game inventory is worth to networks.

You'll see that concept play out in the early 2030s, when the Big Ten & SEC start negotiating their next TV deals.  The SEC will put a rather shocking gap between itself and the Big Ten in TV revenue.

Wall Street benchmarks and major commodity derivatives exhibited distinct intra sector trends on Wednesday. U.S. equities edged higher following the Federal Reserve's rate announcement, with equity index futures maintaining a firm overall posture supported by corporate earnings resilience. 

Meanwhile, commodity derivatives experienced notable divergence: December crude oil (/CLZ26) extended its powerful bullish run past $103 per barrel on persistent Persian Gulf supply risks, whereas agricultural markets saw short-covering relief in corn counterbalanced by seasonal harvest pressure across wheat, soybeans, and livestock complexes.

Top Story of the Day

Crude Oil Spikes Past $103 as Energy Risk Premiums Drive Hard Assets Energy derivatives spearheaded broader commodity movements on Wednesday afternoon as December WTI crude oil (/CLZ26) surged past $103.40 per barrel. Persistent supply side risks surrounding Strait of Hormuz maritime routes, coupled with steady domestic refinery throughput and declining commercial crude reserves, provided strong underlying support across energy spreads. The sustained strength in crude oil continues to anchor macro inflation considerations across broader trading desks.

text:
You're told to test the spirits. So if your religion can't be tested and hold true, then it is false.

"Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world." —1 John 4:1

Ten Mormon Claims and Their Biblical Refutations

The LDS church presents itself as a restoration of true Christianity, but its foundational texts and prophetic pronouncements reveal a different gospel, one that adds to the finished work of Christ and redefines the nature of God Himself. What follows is a scriptural examination of ten core Mormon beliefs, each paired with the Book of Mormon or LDS scripture passage that teaches it, a summary of the claim, and the biblical passage that stands in direct opposition. This is not an attack on sincere people, but a call to test all things against the Word of God.

1. The Claim That Christ's Atonement Requires Human Works to Be Complete

Book of Mormon Passage: "For we know that it is by grace that we are saved, after all we can do" (2 Nephi 25:23).

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that Christ's sacrifice covers sin only after individuals have done everything within their own power, making human effort a necessary component of salvation rather than a fruit of it.

Biblical Refutation: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9). Paul explicitly excludes works from the equation of salvation. To add "after all we can do" to the cross is to declare Christ's sacrifice insufficient.

2. The Claim That God Was Once a Man Who Became God

LDS Scripture Passage: "God himself was once as he now is, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens" (Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, p. 345; also echoed in Lorenzo Snow's couplet: "As man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may be").

Summary of Claim: Mormon theology asserts that God the Father was a mortal man who progressed to godhood, and that faithful Mormon men can follow the same path to become gods themselves.

Biblical Refutation: "I am the LORD, and there is none else, there is no God beside me" (Isaiah 45:5). "Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me" (Isaiah 43:10). Scripture declares God eternal, uncreated, and utterly unique. There is no ladder to godhood, only a chasm between Creator and creature.

3. The Claim That the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit Are Three Separate Gods

Book of Mormon Passage: The LDS canon teaches the Godhead consists of three distinct beings united in purpose, not essence, with the Father and Son possessing bodies of flesh and bone. This is expounded in Doctrine and Covenants 130:22: "The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit."

Summary of Claim: Mormonism rejects the biblical doctrine of the Trinity, teaching instead that God the Father and Jesus Christ are two separate embodied gods, with the Holy Spirit as a third being, united only in will and purpose.

Biblical Refutation: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD" (Deuteronomy 6:4). "I and my Father are one" (John 10:30). Jesus was not merely one in purpose with the Father; the Jews understood Him to be claiming equality with God, which is why they sought to stone Him (John 5:18). The Spirit is called God and possesses divine attributes (Acts 5:3-4; 1 Corinthians 2:10-11).

4. The Claim That the Father and Son Are Two Separate Physical Beings, and Jesus Was a Spirit Child

Book of Mormon Passage: The LDS teaching that Jesus was the firstborn spirit child of Heavenly Father and a heavenly mother, and that Lucifer was His spirit brother, is central to LDS cosmology. This is not found in the Book of Mormon itself but in LDS prophetic teaching: "Jesus was the firstborn spirit son of God... and Satan was a spirit brother of Jesus" (Gospel Principles, LDS Church manual).

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that Jesus and Lucifer were both spirit offspring of God the Father, making them brothers, with Jesus being the elder and more faithful.

Biblical Refutation: "And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan... and his angels were cast out with him" (Revelation 12:9). The devil is a created angelic being, not a spirit child of God. Jesus is "the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created" (Colossians 1:15-16). The Creator is not the brother of the created rebel.

5. The Claim That Baptism Is Necessary for Salvation and Performed for the Dead

Book of Mormon Passage: "For whosoever shall believe in me, and is baptized, the same shall be saved" (3 Nephi 11:33; see also 3 Nephi 11:38 and Moroni 8:5 for strong statements on baptismal necessity). The LDS practice of baptism for the dead is based on 1 Corinthians 15:29, which they interpret as literal water baptism for deceased persons.

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that water baptism is essential for salvation and that living members can be baptized on behalf of the dead, who then have the opportunity to accept the gospel in the spirit world.

Biblical Refutation: "For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel" (1 Corinthians 1:17). If baptism were essential to salvation, Paul would not have thanked God that he baptized so few (1 Corinthians 1:14). "By grace are ye saved through faith" (Ephesians 2:8), not through water. The thief on the cross was promised paradise without baptism (Luke 23:43). As for baptism for the dead, 1 Corinthians 15:29 refers to a practice Paul neither endorses nor commands, he is using a rhetorical device against those who deny resurrection, asking why they baptize for the dead if the dead do not rise.

6. The Claim That the Book of Mormon Is Scripture Equal to the Bible and That the Bible Is Corrupt

Book of Mormon Passage: "Thou fool, that shall say: A Bible, we have got a Bible, and we need no more Bible... Know ye not that the testimony of two nations is a witness unto you that I am God?" (2 Nephi 29:6-8).

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that the Bible has been corrupted through mistranslation and that the Book of Mormon, along with other LDS scriptures, is a second witness that restores lost truths. The Book of Mormon claims to be the "fulness of the gospel" (Doctrine and Covenants 20:9).

Biblical Refutation: "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works" (2 Timothy 3:16-17). "The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever" (Isaiah 40:8). "For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book" (Revelation 22:18). Scripture claims completeness and divine preservation. Adding another book and declaring the first corrupt is the signature of a different gospel.

7. The Claim That Joseph Smith Restored the Aaronic and Melchizedek Priesthoods and That Without Them There Is No True Church

Book of Mormon Passage: The Book of Mormon itself does not contain the narrative of angelic restoration of priesthood keys, that comes from Joseph Smith's own history and the Doctrine and Covenants (D&C 13; D&C 27; D&C 110). The Book of Mormon does emphasize the necessity of proper authority (3 Nephi 11:21-22; Moroni 3-5).

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that the true authority to act in God's name was lost after the apostles died and was restored to Joseph Smith by John the Baptist and Peter, James, and John.

Biblical Refutation: "For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance" (Romans 11:29). Christ promised, "I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world" (Matthew 28:20), and "the gates of hell shall not prevail" against His church (Matthew 16:18). There was no great apostasy that required a new priesthood dispensation. The priesthood of all believers (1 Peter 2:9; Revelation 1:6) was never rescinded.

8. The Claim That There Are Many Gods, or That Others Can Become Gods

Book of Mormon Passage: While the Book of Mormon is more cautious here than later LDS teaching, Doctrine and Covenants 132:20 declares: "Then shall they be gods, because they have no end... because they have all power, and the angels are subject unto them." This is the LDS doctrine of exaltation.

Summary of Claim: Mormonism teaches that faithful Latter-day Saints can achieve godhood in the afterlife, becoming gods over their own worlds, populating them with spirit children.

Biblical Refutation: "Thus saith the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God" (Isaiah 44:6). "For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God" (Exodus 34:14). The desire to become God is the original temptation, "ye shall be as gods" (Genesis 3:5), it is the serpent's lie, not the gospel's promise.

9. The Claim That the Garden of Eden Was in Missouri and That Adam Was Michael the Archangel

LDS Scripture Passage: Doctrine and Covenants 116:1 designates Adam-ondi-Ahman, in Daviess County, Missouri, as the place where Adam gathered his posterity and blessed them before his death. LDS teaching identifies Adam with Michael the archangel.

Summary of Claim: Mormonism locates the Garden of Eden in North America and teaches that Adam was the archangel Michael in his pre-mortal state, a being who helped create the earth.

Biblical Refutation: "And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed" (Genesis 2:8). The biblical text places Eden in Mesopotamia, associated with the Tigris and Euphrates rivers (Genesis 2:10-14). As for Adam, he was a man formed from dust, not a pre-existent angel (Genesis 2:7; 1 Corinthians 15:45-47). Michael is an archangel who serves God (Jude 1:9; Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1), not the first human.

10. The Claim That Christ's Sacrifice Was Not Enough and That Blood Atonement Is Required for Certain Sins

Book of Mormon Passage: The Book of Mormon teaches that some sins require shedding of one's own blood for forgiveness: "For behold, I, God, have suffered these things for all, that they might not suffer if they would repent; But if they would not repent they must suffer even as I" (Doctrine and Covenants 19:16-17). This is echoed in LDS teaching that blood atonement, the shedding of one's own blood, was required for murder and certain sins, a doctrine taught by Brigham Young and other early LDS leaders.

Summary of Claim: Mormonism historically taught that the blood of Christ does not cover all sins, specifically that murder and certain grievous sins require the sinner's own blood to be shed, either by civil execution or personal sacrifice, to atone.

Biblical Refutation: "But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God... For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified" (Hebrews 10:12, 14). "The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin" (1 John 1:7). "Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us" (Hebrews 9:12). Christ's sacrifice is once for all and sufficient for all. To claim anything else is to trample the Son of God underfoot and count the blood of the covenant an unholy thing (Hebrews 10:29).

🕮 "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed." - Galatians 1:8

These ten points are not presented to condemn individuals but to call the LDS church to the standard of Scripture. Mormonism adds to the finished work of Christ, redefines the nature of God, and claims a restoration that the Bible never promises. The Word of God is complete, sufficient, and clear: salvation is by grace through faith in the finished work of Jesus Christ, not of works, not of priesthoods, not of new scriptures. The moment any system adds a single requirement to the cross, it has departed from the gospel. The moment it declares God was a man and man may become God, it has repeated the serpent's oldest lie. The moment it says the Bible is corrupt and needs a new witness, it has taken the pen from the Author and claimed a new revelation. The Bereans searched the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so (Acts 17:11). That is the call here. Test everything against the Word. Hold fast to what is good. And never trade the sufficient sacrifice of Christ for the incomplete atonements of men.

Public schools, even private schools, even religious schools, DO NOT HAVE TO DO Everything.  Or should not, and federal mandates that they must should be dissolved.

I interviewed at a Catholic school where everyone assumed I was an Irish Catholic (I’m 75% Welsh and Scottish and English) because I look Irish and I went to Catholic University at one point for grad school.

They basically offered me a job during the interview and I said I wasn’t Catholic and I wanted them to know, since I don’t know Catholic doctrines in detail.  I don’t know if they realized I was gay but they were heavily pitching how they taught Catholic social doctrine, social justice doctrine, and I wanted to say “you are so barking up the wrong tree.”  I think a gay teacher was ok with them.  But to my concern that they should know I would be incompetent to answer doctrinal questions, they replied:  we don’t know either, we just tell kids to wait until Thursday, when Father Michael will come answer them.

A very prudent practice.  maybe I should go back and teach there.  Recently I had to keep some kids from playing a game (in someone else’s class who did not show up so I volunteered for her) who were playing a “game” where they choked each other.

text:
The Legacy of the Healing
An Ancestral Apology &Truth 

I carry within my veins the bloodlines of two massive, ancient Scottish houses, the Cunninghams &the Dunbars. My family history is a sprawling tapestry woven with deep resilience, but it also touches the heavy shadows of human history. To walk forward into the light with a completely fresh slate, I must tell the full truth of both sides of my name.

I have already spoken of my brave grandmother, Mary Cunningham, who used her brilliant mind &the law to defeat a corrupt court in 1644. But twenty-seven years later, a different kind of tragedy struck a branch of my family tree through an 18-year-old gentlewoman named Mary Dunbar.

In the winter of 1710, Mary traveled to the peninsula of Islandmagee in Northern Ireland. Almost immediately upon arrival, she fell catastrophically ill. In those days, medical science did not understand the brain. Mary suffered from terrifying, violent convulsions, hallucinated, went into deep trances, &compulsively swallowed &vomited up household brass pins &iron nails.

Because the community lived under the fear-driven laws of the old world, they did not see a sick girl who needed a doctor. Instead, they told her that her illness was a spiritual curse &demanded she name the "witches" tormenting her. In her delirium &pain, Mary pointed her finger at eight innocent, vulnerable women in the village, Janet Carson, Janet Latimer, Janet Main, Janet Millar, Margaret Mitchell, Catherine McCalmond, Janet Liston, &Elizabeth Sellor.

These women were poor, elderly, or disabled, &many practiced traditional herbal healing. Because of Mary’s accusations, they were attacked by a fearful mob, dragged into court, convicted, &locked in a dark prison. Weeks later, Mary’s body gave out from her untreated illness &she passed away. Because of her tragic death, the court went even further, hanging Elizabeth's husband, William Sellor, making him the only man in Irish history executed for witchcraft.

Today, modern medical science has re-examined Mary Dunbar’s records. We now know she was not a malicious liar, nor was she possessed. She was a terrified teenager suffering from a severe, fatal brain inflammation &epilepsy. But because of the ignorance &religious paranoia of that era, her medical emergency was weaponized to destroy an entire group of innocent people.

As a living descendant of the House of Dunbar, I look back across 315 years of history to the souls of the Islandmagee Eight &to William Sellor. I acknowledge that you were completely innocent. You were caretakers, mothers, fathers, &elders who were used as scapegoats in a time of fear &medical ignorance. I recognize the terror, the pain, &the injustice that my family name brought to your doorstep.

Through this 13th Generation, the cycle of blame stops forever. I will break the chains of historical paranoia. I offer our deep, ancestral apology to your memory, & I clear your names in the light of truth. May your souls rest in absolute peace, vindicated &remembered as the completely innocent people you were. 🤍
